docs.title: Create Saudi e-invoices in your application
docs.text:
fatoority is an open-source SDK and CLI for Saudi e-invoicing. Build standard and simplified invoices from application data, including credit notes, debit notes, and prepayment invoices. Calculate totals and VAT, generate UBL XML, then sign and validate invoices locally before submitting them through the ZATCA APIs.

Use the Rust library, add it to your application in Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, C#, Kotlin/Java (including Android), or C/C++, or run the command-line tool from your terminal.

Run the sandbox walkthrough Choose your language View on GitHub

fatoority is an independent project and is not affiliated with ZATCA.

Start with one complete example in Python, C#, or TypeScript covering creation through reporting, with a diagram of the ZATCA journey.

docs.title: What you can build
docs.text:
Task How fatoority helps Create invoices Build invoice data with calculated totals and UBL XML output. Choose standard or simplified tax invoices, credit/debit notes, or prepayments. Handle pricing and VAT Apply line or document discounts and charges, use price-base quantities, and group VAT by category and rate with exact decimal arithmetic. Include business references Carry purchase orders, contracts, delivery dates, payment instructions/accounts, and party/item identifiers into XML. Read existing XML Inspect supported fields and totals. Signed import checks cryptographic integrity and QR consistency while retaining the original XML. Validate locally Check UBL schemas and the pinned SDK's 257 business-rule assertions. Inspect rule findings, warnings, and incomplete stages before submission. Sign invoices Sign with a matching certificate and private key. Compute invoice hashes and prepare API payloads. Generate QR payloads Generate base64 invoice QR data or read the payload embedded in signed XML. Onboard and submit Generate a CSR, obtain or renew credentials, run compliance checks, and integrate reporting or clearance.

Local invoice processing needs no official SDK installation or network access. The Rust core has no Java dependency. The JavaScript package includes WebAssembly for Node.js and browsers; Kotlin/Java also has an Android artifact. Use prepared API requests when your application needs its own HTTP transport.

Local validation helps catch problems before submission. It does not establish ZATCA gateway acceptance or certificate issuer trust. See the validation guide for coverage and how to interpret results.

docs.title: Try it: validate an invoice
docs.text: Start with a local XML schema check. You do not need an account, certificate, or API credentials for this example.

docs.title: 1. Install the CLI
docs.text:
With Rust and Cargo installed, run:

cargo install fatoora-cli

You can also download a binary for your platform from GitHub Releases. Extract the archive and put the fatoora executable on your PATH.

docs.title: 2. Download the sample invoice
docs.text: Save sample-invoice.xml in your working folder. It contains demonstration data for this schema check.

docs.title: 3. Run the check
docs.text:
From the folder containing the file:

fatoora validate --invoice sample-invoice.xml

Expected output:

OK

OK means the XML passes the bundled UBL schema check. To run local ZATCA rules and inspect individual findings, follow the invoice validation guide. For more terminal commands, see the CLI guide.

docs.title: Choose your language
docs.text:
Install the package for your application, then follow its examples. The project and most packages are named fatoority; existing API names such as Python's fatoora import and Rust's fatoora_core remain unchanged.

RustPythonJavaScriptC#Kotlin / Java / AndroidC / C++ 
cargo add fatoora-core

Import fatoora_core in your code. Create your first invoice or browse the Rust API reference.

pip install fatoority

Import fatoora in your code. Follow the Python setup and examples.

npm install fatoority

Use the WebAssembly package in Node.js or a browser. Follow the JavaScript/TypeScript setup and examples, including browser asset setup and API transport requirements.

dotnet add package Fatoority

Use the Fatoora namespace with .NET 8 or later. Follow the C# setup and examples, including supported native platforms.

Install from Maven Central with Gradle or Maven.

Gradle (build.gradle.kts):

repositories { mavenCentral() }
dependencies {
    implementation("com.fatoority:fatoority:0.7.0")
}

Maven (add inside <dependencies> in pom.xml):

<dependency>
  <groupId>com.fatoority</groupId>
  <artifactId>fatoority</artifactId>
  <version>0.7.0</version>
</dependency>

Import com.fatoora in your code. Follow the Kotlin/Java examples for supported platforms and Android setup. For Android, use com.fatoority:fatoority-android:0.7.0 instead of the desktop artifact.

Download the fatoora-ffi-* archive with the native library and C/C++ headers from GitHub Releases.

Follow the C/C++ setup and examples for compilation and linking instructions.

docs.title: Continue your integration
docs.text:
If you are adding invoicing to an application, start with creating an invoice. The business-case recipes cover pricing and document types. Then sign and validate the XML before sending it.

For device onboarding, generate a CSR, then use the ZATCA API client to request credentials and submit invoices. The guides explain the inputs needed at each step.

docs.title: About the project
docs.text:
The core is written in Rust and shared by the CLI and language bindings. The project code is available under the MIT or Apache-2.0 license. Third-party materials retain their upstream terms; see the third-party notices.

See the SDK compatibility notes for the scope of comparison with the official SDK, and benchmarks for measured performance and methodology.

Need help with an integration? Open an issue. To help improve the library or these docs, read the contributing guide.

docs.title: Benchmarks
docs.text: Benchmarks compare Fatoority with the official ZATCA SDK on local fixtures. CLI process timings and warm C# API timings measure different workloads.

docs.title: CLI hashing
docs.text:
CLI invoice hashing benchmark results: - bench/cli/results/hash_bench.md

Command Mean [ms] Min [ms] Max [ms] Relative ZATCA SDK 537.8 ± 8.6 522.0 549.1 187.35 ± 12.59 fatoora-cli 2.9 ± 0.2 2.4 3.6 1.00

The actual script for the benchmark is located at bench/cli/hash_bench.sh

Set FATOORA_CLI to the official SDK executable path and optionally FATOORITY_CLI to this project's fatoora executable. The script otherwise uses the local release or debug build for this project.

docs.title: C# / .NET
docs.text:
Measured on Linux x86_64 with an AMD Ryzen 7 7800X3D, .NET SDK 8.0.425, and Release builds on 2026-10-12. Each value is the median milliseconds per warm call across seven batches after 15 warmup calls.

Operation Invoice Official .NET SDK Fatoority Speedup Hash Simplified 2.487 ms 0.176 ms 14.1× Hash Standard 2.851 ms 0.336 ms 8.5× Sign Simplified 13.630 ms 0.875 ms 15.6× Sign Standard 15.423 ms 1.366 ms 11.3× Validate Simplified 265.453 ms 5.940 ms 44.7× Validate Standard 264.568 ms 5.992 ms 44.2×

Both implementations matched expected hashes, and both signing outputs passed official validation. Both validators accepted the same frozen signed documents. The official SDK's external CEN/KSA rules match our pinned rule sources.

These timings include public API costs: XML parsing, credential parsing in the official signing method, and JSON result parsing in our validator. Our signer reuses parsed credentials. They describe these fixtures on this machine; large invoices, concurrency, HTTP, memory use, and other platforms were not measured.

Fresh-process medians, including startup and one simplified-invoice operation:

Operation Official .NET SDK Fatoority Hash 120 ms 50 ms Sign 248 ms 51 ms Validate 1,260 ms 184 ms

See the C# benchmark harness for reproduction commands and the recorded results for raw samples, binary hashes, and measurement details.

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text: Bug reports, documentation fixes, tests, and code improvements are welcome. For a large API or behavior change, open an issue first so the approach can be discussed before implementation.

docs.title: Set up a checkout
docs.text:
Install stable Rust and Git, then run:

git clone https://github.com/mqqz/fatoority.git
cd fatoority
cargo check --workspace --locked

Ordinary builds and tests need neither Java, an installed ZATCA SDK, nor a system XML library. Language-binding work needs additional tools; see binding development.

docs.title: Find the right place
docs.text: Directory Contents fatoora-core/ Invoice model, signing, XML, validation and API client fatoora-cli/ Command-line interface fatoora-ffi/ Shared bridge for language bindings fatoora-derive/ Procedural macros bindings/ Language facades, packages and their tests docs/ Guides and reference pages bench/ and fuzz/ Benchmark harnesses and fuzz targets

docs.title: Make and check a change
docs.text:
Keep changes focused. Add a regression test for a bug, and update the relevant guide or reference when public behavior changes.

Run these checks from the repository root:

cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings
SKIP_ZATCA_LIVE_API=1 cargo test --workspace --all-features --locked -- --skip doc_example_api

The test command skips live ZATCA requests. Local HTTP tests still need loopback networking. Start with the test for the behavior you changed, then run the workspace checks before submitting.

If you changed… Also check… A binding or shared bridge Generation, language tests and installed packages Validation, signing or XML behavior Validation and SDK compatibility tests Documentation The strict documentation build below Performance-sensitive code The relevant harness in bench/

For longer property-test runs, set PROPTEST_CASES=10000 when running the relevant test. Keep minimized regression inputs and failure seeds. See fuzz/README.md for fuzzing instructions.

docs.title: Edit the documentation
docs.text:
python3 -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/python -m pip install mkdocs-material mkdocs-macros-plugin
.venv/bin/mkdocs serve

On Windows, use executables under .venv\Scripts instead of .venv/bin. The preview prints its local URL. Before submitting, run:

.venv/bin/mkdocs build --strict --site-dir /tmp/fatoority-docs

Use a temporary output directory suitable for your system. Guides should walk through a task; reference pages should document inputs, results and behavior. Keep language-specific examples and notes inside the appropriate language tab. Check changed links, narrow screens and every tab you edited.

docs.title: Choose the target branch
docs.text:
main ships non-breaking 0.7.x releases, so a pull request into main must not break the public Rust API. Breaking changes for 0.8.0 go to the next branch.

CI runs cargo-semver-checks on fatoora-core and fatoora-ffi against the v0.7.0 tag. The check fails a pull request into main that contains a breaking change. On a pull request into next it reports the result without failing. To run it locally:

cargo install --locked cargo-semver-checks@0.51.0
cargo semver-checks -p fatoora-core --baseline-rev v0.7.0
cargo semver-checks -p fatoora-ffi --baseline-rev v0.7.0

The baseline is built from the git tag, so your checkout needs the v0.7.0 tag (git fetch --tags).

docs.title: Submit a pull request
docs.text:
Explain the problem, the resulting behavior and how you checked it. Include any remaining limitations. CI runs additional platform and package checks; a local pass does not replace those checks.

Follow the code of conduct. Original contributions are licensed under both MIT and Apache-2.0. Identify third-party material and retain its licenses and notices. For security reports, use the security policy.

Release maintainers can follow the release checklist.

docs.title: Supported Versions
docs.text: Security updates are provided for the latest main branch and the most recent published releases.

docs.title: Reporting a Vulnerability
docs.text:
If you discover a security issue, please report it privately (i.e. don't open an issue).

  • Contact: open a GitHub Security Advisory or email the maintainer.
  • Include: a clear description, steps to reproduce, affected versions, and any potential impact.

Please do not disclose the issue publicly until it has been addressed.

docs.title: Disclosure Process
docs.text: After receiving a report, we will: - Acknowledge receipt - Investigate and provide an estimated timeline - Release a fix and coordinate public disclosure

docs.title: Validation and compatibility tests
docs.text: Use these checks when changing validation, XML serialization, signing, QR generation or CSR encoding. The compatibility reference documents user-visible coverage, differences and limits; this page covers maintaining the evidence.

docs.title: Run offline checks
docs.text:
From the repository root:

python3 scripts/business_rules.py check
python3 scripts/integrity_validation.py check
python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests -v
cargo test -p fatoora-core --locked --test sdk_parity
cargo test -p fatoora-core --locked --lib sdk_canonical_corpus
cargo test -p fatoora-core --locked --lib invoice::validation

These checks replay frozen evidence without Java or an installed SDK. Cargo may download missing dependencies; add --offline when dependencies are cached. Missing fixtures, changed checksums and unexpected results fail the checks.

docs.title: Add a regression
docs.text:
Define the expected outcome before changing the implementation. Keep a small failing input and test the result, error or report stage that matters. For a business-rule change, retain the assertion site and location as well as the rule code.

Fixture directory under fatoora-core/tests/fixtures/ Purpose sdk-parity/ Frozen signing, hashing, QR, schema and CSR evidence sdk-parity-typed/ Reviewed captures for changed typed-builder output business-rules/ Rule catalog, coverage ledger and SDK observations

Do not regenerate expected output just to make a failing test pass. Inspect the input, executable rule source and original SDK output. Keep intentional compatibility differences explicit. SDK exit status alone is insufficient: a rejected invoice can still produce exit code zero.

For arithmetic changes, retain independently calculated expectations and exercise rounding boundaries. For integrity changes, include tampered inputs and check that rejection is attributed to the expected stage.

docs.title: Compare fresh output with the SDK
docs.text:
This optional step requires the pinned SDK 238-R3.4.8, its dummy test credentials and a JDK with java and javac. Set FATOORA_HOME to the SDK installation. The tools check the SDK pin and use an isolated copy.

python3 scripts/sdk_parity.py verify \
  --sdk-root "$FATOORA_HOME" \
  --output /tmp/fatoora-sdk-verification

The output directory must not exist. Review report.json and its evidence directory. This checks freshly generated output against the recorded layer outcomes; it does not make live gateway requests.

docs.title: Refresh evidence intentionally
docs.text:
For unchanged input cases, capture a candidate:

python3 scripts/sdk_parity.py capture \
  --sdk-root "$FATOORA_HOME" \
  --output /tmp/fatoora-sdk-candidate

For an intentional serializer or input change, first run cargo run -p fatoora-core --locked --example sdk_parity_export -- /tmp/fatoora-sdk-inputs, then pass --inputs /tmp/fatoora-sdk-inputs to capture.

Business-rule and integrity changes use their own capture commands:

python3 scripts/business_rules.py capture --family ksa-prepayment \
  --sdk-root "$FATOORA_HOME" --output /tmp/business-rules-candidate
python3 scripts/integrity_validation.py capture \
  --sdk-root "$FATOORA_HOME" --output /tmp/integrity-candidate

Choose the mutation family relevant to the change. Use new output directories, inspect the candidate differences and raw logs, then replace only reviewed fixtures. Preserve manifests, hashes, source notices and the rule-coverage ledger. Run the offline checks again after updating evidence. A new SDK version requires an explicit pin and source review.

docs.title: Binding development
docs.text: Use this page when changing the shared bridge or a language package. Installation and application code belong in the binding reference.

docs.title: Change the API once
docs.text:
1. Implement the behavior and its tests in fatoora-core.
  2. Expose it in the appropriate fatoora-ffi/src bridge: crypto.rs, invoice.rs, or api.rs. Shared errors and input conversion live in common.rs.
  3. Regenerate the bindings. Update a handwritten facade when it needs language-specific conversion or resource handling.
  4. Test the affected language and its installed package. Update public examples and reference documentation.

Preserve exact decimals, absent versus empty values, structured errors and ownership on failure. Test consumed objects, returned children after parent disposal, and concurrent close where relevant. Test HTTP behavior against a local server.

docs.title: Return strings
docs.text:
Strings leave the bridge through a &mut DiplomatWrite argument; no binding sees a string handle.

Value FFI shape Bindings Required fn x(&self, out: &mut DiplomatWrite) -> Result<(), Box<BindingError>>, written with common::write A plain string; errors throw Optional, cannot fail fn x(&self, out: &mut DiplomatWrite) -> Option<()>, written with common::write_optional A nullable string Optional, can fail fn x_present(&self) -> bool (or Result<bool, Box<BindingError>>) plus a required-string x that fails when the value is absent One nullable string x; errors throw

A nullable string is str | None, string | null, String?, string?, std::optional<std::string>, or a NULL C string. The generated code frees the write buffer on both paths.

Option<()> has no error channel, and Diplomat cannot express Result<Option<()>, E>. Before reaching for a pair, argue the error away:

  • Write NUL as-is. write_optional never fails; the C facade rejects a string containing NUL itself, and the other languages return it unchanged.
  • Index into a list with a _len getter plus an index method returning a required string, as PaymentMeans::instruction_note_at and ZatcaStageReport::evaluated_assertion do. An out-of-range index is an error, not an absent value.

Use an x_present/x pair only when computing the value can fail, as decoding ValidationResponse::cleared_invoice_xml can, or when the object can be consumed, as SignedInvoice::zatca_key_signature can. The C, C#, Kotlin and JavaScript generators recognize the pair by name: they call x_present first, return null when it is false, and hide x_present. The Python facade does the same with _invoke_optional. Raw x fails when the value is absent, so callers of the raw C++ and Kotlin (com.fatoora.raw) classes check x_present first.

docs.title: Generate and verify
docs.text:
Generated files are checked in. Edit the bridge or generator, then regenerate; do not edit generated output directly.

Install the pinned generators once:

cargo install diplomat-tool --version 0.17.0 --locked
python3 scripts/install_dotnet_generator.py
python3 scripts/install_kotlin_generator.py

The installer scripts select the required fork revisions. Then run:

python3 scripts/generate_bindings.py
python3 scripts/generate_bindings.py --check
cargo test -p fatoora-ffi --locked

The combined check covers all generators, including C# and Kotlin. It requires all three installed tools. For work confined to a handwritten language facade, run that package's checks below without regenerating unchanged bridge code.

docs.title: Check the affected package
docs.text:
C and C++PythonJavaScriptC#Kotlin and Java

Install a C11 and C++17 compiler alongside Rust and Python. Run:

python3 scripts/check_native_bindings.py
python3 scripts/check_c_reference.py
python3 scripts/check_c_examples.py

These compile native callers and exercise ownership, errors and examples. The API example's check does not submit an invoice.

The public C facade is generated from the native headers. Change scripts/generate_c_facade.py or scripts/c_facade_runtime.c when adjusting that facade, then run the combined generation check.

Source builds require Python development headers, CMake, a C++20 compiler and Rust. In an activated virtual environment:

python -m pip install "./bindings/python[dev]"
python -m pytest bindings/python/tests
python -m pip wheel --no-deps ./bindings/python -w /tmp/fatoority-wheels

Install the resulting wheel in a fresh environment and run bindings/python/tests/wheel_smoke.py. Keep the source package off PYTHONPATH so the check uses the installed package and its bundled native library.

Add facade regressions for decimal conversion, exceptions, lifetime handling or GIL behavior when those contracts change.

Install Node.js 22+, npm and the Rust WASM target:

rustup target add wasm32-unknown-unknown
npm ci --prefix bindings/js
python3 scripts/build_js.py
npm run check --prefix bindings/js
node bindings/js/tests/runtime.test.mjs
npx --prefix bindings/js playwright install chromium
node bindings/js/tests/browser.mjs
python3 scripts/check_js_package.py

Use the build script so optimization and artifact-size checks run consistently. The checks cover declarations, runtime behavior, browser loading and an installed npm package.

scripts/generate_bindings.py also runs scripts/generate_js_facade.py, which derives bindings/js/members.mjs (the property and optional-string tables patch.mjs applies) and bindings/js/raw.d.mts (the adapted declarations) from the generated JavaScript. Change that script, not its output, to adjust which getters are properties.

Install the .NET SDK required by bindings/dotnet, plus Rust and Python. Run:

python3 scripts/generate_dotnet.py --check
python3 scripts/check_dotnet.py

To test an already built NuGet package as well, pass --package-dir dist/dotnet. Keep disposal, optional results, byte copies and error ownership covered by the package tests.

Install the JDK required by bindings/kotlin, plus Rust and Python. Use the checked-in Gradle wrapper:

python3 scripts/generate_kotlin.py --check
python3 scripts/build_kotlin.py
bindings/kotlin/gradlew -p bindings/kotlin test -PnativeDir="$PWD/target/jvm-release"
python3 scripts/check_kotlin.py

The package check uses a fresh Java consumer. Android changes also need the Android build and emulator checks described in the package README. Preserve both language interfaces when changing factories, optional values or exceptions.

docs.title: Before submitting
docs.text: Run the workspace checks, review generated diffs, and test the packaged library rather than only a build-tree import. Include the relevant license and notice files when changing packaging. Platform-specific changes need their platform CI results.

docs.title: Invoice model and preservation contract
docs.text:
The supported invoice profile is the ZATCA data dictionary dated 19 May 2023 and XML implementation standard 1.2. The source URLs, SHA-256 digests, profile applicability and all 150 dictionary rows are recorded in fatoora-core/tests/fixtures/model-coverage.json. The dictionary's spelling errors in XML paths are corrected in the executable selectors (AdditionalDocumentReference, ChargeIndicator and currencyID).

dictionary_source_to_output_coverage extracts source XML values directly and compares them with regenerated XML. It fails if a dictionary row has no exercised source occurrence. The corpus includes official invoice-family examples, advance adjustments, mixed categories, and a constructed invoice containing optional pricing and metadata fields. This is field coverage, not exhaustive coverage of all combinations.

docs.title: API inventory
docs.text:
Area Representation and API Issue time UTC builder timestamps serialize with Z; imported AST dates/times retain their clock representation while issue_datetime() represents the corresponding UTC instant. Reference times also preserve Z. Invoice kind InvoiceType::{Tax, Prepayment, CreditNote, DebitNote}(InvoiceSubType); credit/debit constructors no longer embed references or reasons References and reasons Append billing_reference(OriginalInvoiceRef) and payment_means(PaymentMeans); instructions belong to their payment entry Notes note(InvoiceNote) appends in order; notes() exposes all entries; note() reads the first Line construction Existing LineItem::new plus LineItem::builder(); named quantity, price, base quantity, gross price, price discount, supplied amounts, identifiers, allowances and charges Adjustments Adjustment::amount or percentage; line .allowance/.charge; invoice .allowance(DocumentAdjustment)/.charge(DocumentAdjustment) specify VAT independently VAT breakdowns vat_breakdown(VatBreakdown) accepts checked supplied amounts; tax_exemption assigns document breakdown metadata independently of line metadata Delivery Delivery has independent actual/latest dates, and preserves an explicitly present empty container Party identifiers identifier(OtherId) appends, identifiers() reads all schemes in source order; first-ID getters remain available Buyer An optional party and optional address; no address is invented on import Address Province/state is an additional optional field; empty basic address strings represent omitted components in the existing address API Payments Ordered payment entries, each with ordered optional instructions and an optional account; account identifier and payment terms are independent Totals Prepaid amount and signed payable rounding amount are builder inputs Bindings Mutable set_* and add_* methods; C/C++/Python/JS/C#/Kotlin generated from the shared FFI; Python also has a handwritten facade

Adding province to address struct literals, making Party::address() optional, and removing embedded credit/debit reference fields are intentional Rust breaking changes. Party identifiers and payment instructions now use collections. AllowanceCharge::omit_vat_rate() (read back with has_vat_rate()) preserves an absent rate for out-of-scope adjustments; other categories require a rate. Imported AST timestamps are converted to UTC for issue_datetime(); issue_date() and issue_time() preserve their XML representation. Rust tests and FFI callers are updated together. Existing aggregate discount/charge setters remain available for callers using one category; combining them with independent adjustment entries is rejected. First-entry convenience getters remain available, but collection getters are required to inspect all supplied values.

docs.title: Monetary dependencies
docs.text:
Accepted supplied values are stored once. Expected values are calculated transiently for checks. Serialized values are the same values used downstream.

Value Input and check Downstream use Item net price Supplied net or gross minus price discount; supplied net must agree exactly Exact rational quantity × net price / price base Line net Round the complete rational price calculation to cents, subtract line allowances and add charges; accepted supplied net may differ by at most 0.01 Document line extension and category/rate taxable sums Line VAT Retain supplied cents; when absent in construction, round accepted line net × rate / 100 Line gross only; never sum line VAT to obtain document VAT Line gross Accepted line net plus accepted line VAT, exact equality Serialized line RoundingAmount Adjustment Supplied cents, or base × percentage / 100 rounded to cents; when both supplied, require exact equality Line net or the adjustment's document category/rate Breakdown taxable Accepted line nets in that category/rate, minus its document allowances plus charges Breakdown tax expectation Breakdown tax Retain accepted supplied cents; standard-category tolerance is invoice-line count × 0.01 around the half-even rounded exact product; other categories require zero Sum of document breakdown taxes Document VAT Sum accepted breakdown taxes, exact equality with supplied document tax Tax-inclusive total; same-currency accounting tax Tax-inclusive Tax-exclusive plus document VAT, exact equality Payable equation Prepaid Supplied cents; when type-386 adjustment lines exist, equals their taxable plus tax subtotals Subtract from payable; adjustment lines never add ordinary taxable sales Payable Tax-inclusive minus prepaid plus payable rounding, exact equality XML and QR tag 4

Decimal input remains decimal, never binary floating point. Price-basis division uses integer rational arithmetic until the final cent rounding, so non-terminating per-unit prices do not lose precision prematurely. Zero or negative price bases fail. Supplied sub-cent monetary totals fail. No global epsilon or import-repair mode is introduced.

docs.title: Specification and executable rule precedence
docs.text:
The published standard controls field ownership and representation. The existing business validator retains the pinned SDK 238-R3.4.8 executable semantics; its fixture manifest pins the executable hashes. Neither artifact is silently replaced on a discrepancy.

  • BR-KSA-50 was removed in standard 1.2. Import therefore does not reject supplied line VAT simply for differing from quantity × unrounded price × rate. Gross and document equations remain checked.
  • BR-S-08 describes category-and-rate allocation. Typed calculations use that allocation. The pinned executable validator has category-wide behavior for some mixed-rate cases; business-rule results remain independent of model acceptance.
  • BR-CO-17/BR-S-09 executable tolerances apply to standard-category breakdown tax, including their half-even midpoint policy. For taxable 53.30 at 5%, the tolerance center is 2.66; with one line, 2.65–2.67 are accepted and 2.68 is rejected. Default construction uses the published commercial rounding convention (2.67 in this case). Typed checks use the exact decimal product rather than the SDK binary-float intermediate; business validation retains that executable behavior.
  • Price-base calculations retain exact rational arithmetic. The SDK's executable line calculation uses an intermediate three-decimal truncation; this difference must be considered when evaluating cent boundaries.

docs.title: XML and validation boundaries
docs.text:
Optional structures distinguish absence from presence. Present PaymentMeans requires a code; present item identification requires an ID; present adjustments require their indicator and amount; a present price base must be positive. Delivery dates are independent. Date lexical errors fail import, while date-order business constraints are reported by business validation. Buyer addresses can be absent; a present address requires a valid country. Partial buyer street/building/city/postal components use the existing empty-string omission convention; supplied blank XML values fail import rather than disappearing. Price discount containers require both discount and gross amounts.

Numeric lexical formatting, scalar surrounding whitespace, ISO country/currency spelling, namespace prefixes and XML whitespace may normalize. Repeated supported values retain order. Optional line VAT/rate/gross and document allowance/charge/prepaid/rounding amount presence is retained. BR-KSA-12/13 permit absent rates on out-of-scope document adjustments; import preserves that absence, Rust construction uses omit_vat_rate() on DocumentAdjustment, AllowanceCharge, VatBreakdown and LineItem, and the bindings expose omit_vat_rate() (omitVatRate, OmitVatRate). Schema validity, business-rule validity, and typed-model acceptance are distinct test outcomes. A preservation test does not certify compliance.

Content outside this typed profile follows the existing permissive import policy and may be dropped from regenerated XML. This is not arbitrary UBL lossless round-tripping. Signed import retains original XML verbatim; reconstructed XML is unsigned and does not inherit a hash or signature authenticating another document. Live ZATCA acceptance is a separate operation.

docs.title: Requirements and observed behavior
docs.text:
The May 2023 ZATCA security standard, section 4.1, lists Tags 7–8 for stamped invoices and restricts Tag 9 to simplified invoices and their notes. Section 2.2.1 distinguishes platform clearance stamping of standard invoices from EGS stamping of simplified invoices.

The pinned SDK 238-R3.4.8 independently generated Tags 1–8 for standard tax invoices, credit notes and debit notes; simplified equivalents contained Tags 1–9. Fatoority produced the same tag sequences and decoded values for Tags 4, 5 and 9. Tag 9 contains the certificate's binary signature bytes. Certificate signature metadata remains available for standard documents.

These standard cases are local SDK signing exercises. They are not gateway-cleared documents and establish no platform issuer trust. The original standard XML samples contain Tags 1–8. One foreign-currency sample fails strict Tag 5 comparison as described below. No newly obtained production clearance fixture or live clearance submission was used. Imported certificates are checked against their document's signature and QR; they need not match a locally configured signer.

docs.title: Findings and changes
docs.text:
Finding Root cause Changed paths QR-001 Certificate metadata was treated as unconditional QR content invoice/qr.rs centralizes subtype and required stamp tags; invoice/sign.rs supplies Tag 9 only for simplified documents QR-002 The model QR constructor formatted money independently of source XML Typed signing now serializes first; the obsolete model constructor was removed. XML construction preserves decimal text QR-003 sign_with_bundle() reconstructed a second QR from typed totals invoice/builder.rs retains the payload extracted and checked against the final XML. Signed CLI commands use that payload QR-004 Invalid Base64 was unwrapped or replaced with empty bytes; Tag 9 TLV errors were ignored invoice/qr.rs bounds binary inputs and propagates decoding and field-length errors through structured QR errors QR-005 The integrity decoder required nine tags and the import decoder had different framing checks invoice/xml/parse.rs and validation/integrity.rs share bounded decoding and explicit subtype applicability. The SDK report still skips standard signature/QR stages QR-006 Tag 4 used byte equality while Tag 5 used decimal equality Both fields use the existing bounded exact XML-decimal implementation. A separate SDK-profile check retains Tag 4 lexical matching. BT-110 selects the document-currency tax amount

Signed imports now verify signature, digest, certificate metadata and QR consistency. They preserve the supplied XML and reject mismatches. The original XML signature verifier and signing postconditions remain in use. No certificate trust or revocation checks were added.

docs.title: Decimal observations
docs.text:
For each of 300, 300.0, 300.00, 300.01, 0.00, 45.0, 45.00 and 123456789012345678901234.56, both generators retained the supplied XML spelling in Tags 4 and 5. The pinned SDK accepted those QR fields on Fatoority-signed XML. The decimal probes deliberately alter totals without rebuilding invoice lines; some therefore fail business rules. QR acceptance is a separate result.

The SDK and development API reject QR Tag 4 115.0 against XML 115.00. The underlying exact comparison recognizes monetary equality, while a separate SDK-profile formatting check rejects the different spelling under SDK-QR-004. Signed import checks monetary integrity; full-profile validation remains a separate operation. The frozen qr-total-scale SDK output and native SDK-profile expectation are unchanged. Tag 5 retains SDK-QR-003, including rejection of NaN, exponent syntax and float-collision mismatches. Business-rule scale checks remain separate.

The sample Standard/Invoice/Advance Payment adjustments with foreign currency invoice.xml has document currency USD, accounting VAT 1068.75 SAR and invoice VAT 285 USD. Its original QR uses 1068.75 in Tag 5. The published security standard names BT-110; the XML standard, sections 9.2 and BR-KSA-CL-02, distinguishes BT-110 from accounting-currency BT-111. Fatoority selects 285 and rejects the original sample on strict import under SDK-QR-005. This selection follows the published business-term interpretation. The pinned SDK regenerated 1068.75; this observed difference is recorded in the comparison report. Standard SDK-profile QR validation remains inapplicable.

docs.title: Reproduce the comparison
docs.text:
Build the CLI, then run with the pinned SDK installed. Choose new output directories. Set TMPDIR to a filesystem with enough space for an isolated SDK copy if needed.

cargo build -p fatoora-cli --locked
python scripts/qr_parity.py --sdk-root "$FATOORA_HOME" --output /tmp/qr-comparison
python scripts/sdk_parity.py verify --sdk-root "$FATOORA_HOME" --output /tmp/sdk-verification

qr_parity.py writes the input XML, SDK and Fatoority signed XML, raw process evidence and report.json. The report contains source/input hashes, encoded QR payloads, decoded tag sequences, exact Tags 4/5, Tag 9 in Base64, SDK validation outcomes and Fatoority stage results. It verifies that the installed SDK remains unchanged. A reviewed copy of the report is stored in tests/fixtures/qr-correctness/report.json under fatoora-core.

The broader SDK verification checks freshly exported model and XML signing output against existing golden validation outcomes. It includes standard documents for which the SDK skips QR verification; those skips remain explicit.

docs.title: Regression coverage and API changes
docs.text:
Tests cover both signing paths and all six invoice/note combinations, unchanged imported XML, equality of embedded and exposed QR, certificate metadata retention, binary Tag 9 content, lexical decimal preservation, exact decimal equivalence, document-currency VAT selection, malformed Base64, oversized fields, subtype errors, TLV framing/order/duplicates and tampering. C/C++ and Python checks exercise the shared native boundary.

Public method signatures are unchanged. QrCodeError::InvalidField adds an invalid-input error to a non-exhaustive enum, with structured error details for bindings. Signed parsing is stricter; callers that used it to inspect corrupted documents should retain their source XML and use finalized parsing for supported invoice fields. The CLI rejects a failed signed import instead of generating an unsigned replacement QR. See migration guidance.

docs.title: Verification performed
docs.text:
Formatting and workspace Clippy passed with warnings denied. The workspace unit, integration and documentation suites passed with live ZATCA API tests disabled. The pinned SDK golden verification passed, and the 16-case SDK QR comparison retained matching capture-source hashes. Release metadata, frozen business-rule/integrity evidence and 73 release-tool unit tests passed. Native C/C++ contracts and C examples passed. All 71 Python binding tests passed against the current native library in an isolated copy of the existing Python package.

No new wheel, NuGet, JVM, WASM or platform release package was built. C#, Java and JavaScript runtime suites were not rerun. No registry publication or platform certificate trust check occurred. The development compliance probes below used no production endpoint.

docs.title: Development compliance API observations
docs.text:
One disposable compliance credential and 15 explicitly approved public test probes were sent to https://gw-fatoora.zatca.gov.sa/e-invoicing/developer-portal/compliance/invoices. Fresh issue dates and UUIDs were used; paired QR mutations retained the same signed invoice, certificate and digest. The credential secret and private key were temporary. The recorded responses are in tests/fixtures/qr-correctness/development-api.json under fatoora-core.

Probe Development compliance result Six subtype-correct baselines HTTP 200/202; PASS or WARNING, with REPORTED/CLEARED response fields Tag 4 115.0 or 115 against XML 115.00 HTTP 400; invoiceTotal_QRCODE_INVALID Tag 5 15.0 against XML 15.00 HTTP 200; PASS Incorrect Tag 4 116.00 against XML 115.00 HTTP 400; invoiceTotal_QRCODE_INVALID Incorrect Tag 5 16.00 against XML 15.00 HTTP 200; PASS, despite the mismatch Simplified invoice missing Tag 9 HTTP 400; QRCODE_INVALID Standard invoice containing Tag 9 HTTP 202; WARNING, with CLEARED Standard foreign-currency invoice with Tag 5 285 USD or 1068.75 SAR Both HTTP 200; PASS, with CLEARED

These observations confirm Tag 4's additional formatting constraint. Acceptance of the incorrect VAT and unexpected standard Tag 9 controls prevents treating the development service as an integrity oracle. It does not resolve the standard-invoice VAT currency discrepancy. Fatoority retains exact VAT mismatch rejection and the published BT-110 interpretation. The standard warnings concern existing supply-date, charge-reason and exemption-reason fields; they are unrelated to the QR probes.

The endpoint was the development compliance check, not the reporting or clearance submission endpoints. Its REPORTED/CLEARED fields are recorded response values; it returned no cleared XML. No production acceptance or genuine platform-stamped XML fixture was established. scripts/qr_development_api.py reproduces this credential-issuing, external-submission workflow only when explicitly authorized.

docs.title: Release checklist
docs.text: This page is for maintainers publishing a release. A version tag starts independent publication workflows for crates.io, PyPI, npm, NuGet, Maven Central and native release assets. Merging a release PR does not publish packages.

docs.title: Prepare the candidate
docs.text:
Create a release/<version> branch. Keep one version across all packages:

Update Files Rust packages and internal dependencies The four crate manifests and root Cargo.lock Python bindings/python/pyproject.toml and bindings/python/uv.lock JavaScript bindings/js/package.json and bindings/js/package-lock.json C# bindings/dotnet/Fatoora.csproj Kotlin and Java bindings/kotlin/build.gradle.kts Independent Rust workspaces fuzz/Cargo.lock and scripts/xsd-compat/Cargo.lock

Avoid unrelated dependency upgrades. Add a curated changelog entry, including migration instructions for changed public contracts. Leave the release date as Unreleased until publication.

docs.title: Validate before tagging
docs.text:
Run the workspace checks, affected binding checks and the following commands. Substitute the intended release tag:

python3 scripts/check_release.py --tag v0.7.0
python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests -v
cargo doc --workspace --no-deps --locked
cargo package --workspace --list
cargo publish --workspace --locked --dry-run

The release checker requires Python 3.11+; workspace publication requires Cargo 1.90+. Package verification can require registry access. Fix failures rather than bypassing verification.

Inspect packages for expected code, schemas, native libraries, headers and licenses. Test installed packages in fresh consumers. Run python3 scripts/check_xml_free_artifacts.py <artifact paths> on the built native archives and wheels. Wait for the candidate's platform and package CI checks, and recheck the final commit after changes.

docs.title: Check publication access
docs.text:
Confirm registry ownership and credentials without printing secret values. Versions must be unused at each destination.

Destination Publication setup crates.io CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN with access to all four crates PyPI Trusted publisher for python.yml and the pypi environment npm NPM_TOKEN with access to fatoority NuGet Trusted publisher for dotnet.yml Maven Central Verified namespace, Central token and signing key

The publication workflows in .github/workflows/ define the registry configuration.

docs.title: Publish and verify
docs.text:
After the release PR is reviewed and merged, tag the exact tested commit. Replace the version and commit below:

git tag -a v0.7.0 TESTED_COMMIT_SHA -m "Release v0.7.0"
git push origin v0.7.0

Check each registry and native release asset independently. Verify installation in fresh consumers and the docs.rs build, then publish the curated release notes and date. An uploaded artifact or one green workflow is not proof that every package was published.

docs.title: Recover a partial release
docs.text:
Keep the tag fixed. Check which versions exist and whether a registry deployment is still pending before retrying. Resume only missing publications from that same commit.

The sequential Cargo publisher can stop on an already-published crate; do not blindly rerun it. npm, NuGet and Central support workflow-specific retries on the existing tag. For Central, inspect the deployment status before uploading another bundle. Published versions are immutable; a code fix needs a new version.

docs.title: SDK compatibility and limits
docs.text: fatoority uses recorded evidence from ZATCA SDK 238-R3.4.8 to check invoice hashes, canonical XML, signatures, QR data, CSR structure and validation outcomes. Running the library requires neither Java nor an SDK installation.

docs.title: What is covered
docs.text:
Area Scope Invoice formats Standard and simplified invoices, credit notes and debit notes Signing and hashing Canonical bytes, invoice digests, signed properties and signature integrity QR Encoded fields and their relationship to invoice and certificate data CSR English/Arabic subjects, environments, encoding and signatures Local validation Bundled UBL schema, 105 CEN assertion sites, 152 Saudi assertion sites and applicable integrity checks

The validation reference explains report stages and outcomes. The schema-only operation checks XSD; the local ZATCA operation runs the wider pipeline. Signature and QR checks are inapplicable to standard documents under this profile.

Compatibility tests are evidence for the cases they cover. They do not establish certificate issuer trust, revocation status or remote invoice acceptance. Some fixtures intentionally contain rejected invoices; do not treat every fixture as a compliant template.

docs.title: Known differences and limitations
docs.text:
Policy Behavior SDK-QR-001 QR generation, signing integrity and SDK-profile validation use PayableAmount (BT-115) for tag 4, including prepayment and payable rounding adjustments. This matches the recorded SDK behavior and the Fatoora Developer Community clarification for SDK 3.3.1 and later. SDK-QR-002 Tag 3 must contain a complete RFC3339 timestamp; a missing offset is interpreted as UTC. Comparison uses instants. Native validation rejects inconsistent offsets, a different day and malformed suffixes accepted by the recorded SDK CLI runs. SDK-QR-003 Tag 5 uses exact XML-decimal equality. Native validation rejects NaN, exponent syntax and distinct values that collapse to the same binary float. Captures also show the SDK accepting 16.0 against invoice VAT 15.00; native validation rejects that mismatch. SDK-QR-004 Both money tags use bounded exact XML-decimal comparison. The SDK validation profile additionally requires Tag 4's spelling to match XML; the pinned SDK and development API reject 115.0 against 115.00. Signed import checks monetary integrity separately from this full-profile formatting requirement. SDK-QR-005 Tag 5 selects BT-110 in the document currency. The historical foreign-currency advance-payment sample and SDK QR generator select SAR BT-111 instead; strict import rejects that original payload. Standard SDK-profile reports still skip QR checks. LOCAL-INTEGRITY-001 Signature algorithms, references and structure are restricted to the supported profile. Duplicate IDs, unbound references and malformed TLV data are rejected. This is a constrained invoice verifier; arbitrary XMLDSig transforms are unsupported.

The signing contract does not authenticate the signing-time field as a trusted timestamp. Keep that distinction when using signature metadata for audit records.

The recorded foreign-currency builder case fails the SDK rule requiring SAR as VAT accounting currency. Choose invoice currency and tax-accounting behavior according to your integration requirements, and inspect the local validation report before submission.

docs.title: Validation resource limits
docs.text:
Resource Limit XML input 8 MiB Element nodes 100,000 Element depth 128 Retained XML data 64 MiB Decimal digits 4,096 Findings 10,000 Finding data 8 MiB

Exceeding a limit produces an execution error, potentially with a partial report. DTD declarations in invoice input are rejected. Pattern evaluation has additional bounded resource use. See error details.

docs.title: Evidence and maintenance
docs.text:
The frozen manifest retains the historical SDK-QR-001 mismatch from its capture; it does not describe current QR generation. Current regression tests require both SDK and Rust QR tag 4 to match PayableAmount.

The frozen corpus records SDK outputs and checksums. The recorded verification report identifies the source and artifacts checked in that run; it is not a verification of every subsequent commit.

Contributors changing these behaviors should follow validation testing.

docs.title: QR correctness change and migration
docs.text:
Standard stamps omit Tag 9; simplified stamps require it. This follows the tag table in the published May 2023 security standard, section 4.1. That table lists Tags 7–8 generally. Section 2.2.1 assigns standard clearance stamping to the platform. Local standard signing remains an SDK preparation operation and does not imply clearance.

Signed parsing now verifies local cryptographic integrity and QR consistency. Existing Rust and binding signatures are unchanged. Consumers that previously imported altered, partially signed or historically generated standard documents containing Tag 9 will receive errors. Retain the original XML for diagnosis; use finalized parsing to inspect supported invoice fields. Correct source documents and sign again when authorized. Do not edit an already-cleared document to make it importable.

The signed QR accessor and CLI return the original embedded payload. They no longer construct it from normalized model totals. Certificate signature metadata is read from the certificate independently of Tag 9. Both monetary tags compare exact decimal values; the original XML and QR spelling remain unchanged.

Frozen SDK captures and their native SDK-profile expectations remain unchanged. SDK-QR-004 separates exact monetary equivalence from the additional Tag 4 formatting check. See QR comparison evidence for the current run and its limits.

docs.title: Connect to ZATCA APIs
docs.text:
Use the API client to submit invoices and inspect the gateway's response. This walkthrough reports a simplified invoice to the non-production environment and checks whether reporting was accepted. It requires network access and credentials.

For one runnable program covering creation through reporting, follow the sandbox walkthrough.

docs.title: Choose the operation
docs.text:
Your task Operation Credentials Test an invoice during onboarding Compliance check Compliance credentials Submit a simplified invoice Reporting Production-type credentials for the selected environment Submit a standard invoice Clearance Production-type credentials for the selected environment

A credential's type and its environment are separate. Production-type credentials can target non-production, simulation, or production; the client and credentials must agree. Every example below uses non-production. Changing only the client environment does not convert credentials issued for another environment.

docs.title: Obtain credentials
docs.text:
1. Generate a CSR and private key for the target environment.
  2. Obtain the onboarding one-time password (OTP) through the appropriate ZATCA flow, then submit the CSR to request compliance credentials.
  3. Use those credentials to complete the required invoice compliance checks.
  4. Request production-type credentials for that environment, then retain the returned token and secret for reporting or clearance.

See the credential endpoint reference and ZATCA developer portal for the request fields and environment-specific onboarding requirements. A successful compliance check alone is not reporting or clearance acceptance.

docs.title: Renew credentials or use your own HTTP client
docs.text:
The client also supports production-credential renewal with an existing credential, a new CSR, and an OTP. See renewal inputs. Store the returned credentials for subsequent submissions.

For applications with an existing HTTP stack, prepared requests expose the method, URL, headers, and body without sending a request. Send them with your transport, then decode the actual response status and bytes. See custom transport for credential handling and redirect behavior.

docs.title: Prepare the inputs
docs.text:
Use your own signed.xml: a simplified invoice signed with the certificate and key associated with your credentials. The offline guide's public test certificate is not a substitute for credentials issued to you.

Set ZATCA_TOKEN and ZATCA_SECRET in the environment of the process running the example. Do not paste credentials into source files. The example reads these names and fails before sending a request if either value is missing.

docs.title: Run the example
docs.text:
Choose your language, then follow its setup and run instructions.

RustPythonJavaScriptC#KotlinJavaC

Install Rust and Cargo, then create a project:

cargo new fatoority-guide
cd fatoority-guide
cargo add fatoora-core

Add the async runtime:

cargo add tokio --features macros,rt-multi-thread

Save the code below as src/main.rs. Put the input files in the project root and run:

cargo run

Download this example.

Set ZATCA_TOKEN and ZATCA_SECRET in your process environment before running. The example makes a real request to the non-production gateway.

use fatoora_core::api::{ClearanceMode, CsidCredentials, Production, ZatcaClient};
use fatoora_core::config::{Config, Environment};
use fatoora_core::invoice::xml::parse::parse_signed_invoice_xml;

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    let environment = Environment::NonProduction;
    let token = std::env::var("ZATCA_TOKEN")?;
    let secret = std::env::var("ZATCA_SECRET")?;
    let client = ZatcaClient::new(Config::new(environment))?;
    let credentials = CsidCredentials::<Production>::new(environment, None, token, secret);
    let xml = std::fs::read_to_string("signed.xml")?;
    let invoice = parse_signed_invoice_xml(&xml)?;
    let response = client.report_simplified_invoice(&invoice, &credentials, ClearanceMode::Disabled, Some("en")).await?;
    response.ensure_accepted()?;
    println!("Invoice reporting accepted");
    Ok(())
}

Install the package in your Python environment:

pip install fatoority

Save the code as api.py beside the input files, then run:

python api.py

Download this example. See Python setup for package details.

Set ZATCA_TOKEN and ZATCA_SECRET in your process environment before running. The example makes a real request to the non-production gateway.

This example uses a blocking request; run it away from your application's UI thread. In asyncio code, use AsyncZatcaClient from the fatoority[async] extra instead (download the async example).

import os
from fatoora import ClearanceMode, Config, Environment, ProductionCsid, SignedInvoice, ZatcaClient

# Use credentials issued for this same environment.
environment = Environment.NON_PRODUCTION
token = os.environ["ZATCA_TOKEN"]
secret = os.environ["ZATCA_SECRET"]
with Config(environment) as config, ZatcaClient(config) as client:
    with ProductionCsid(environment, token=token, secret=secret) as credentials:
        with SignedInvoice.from_file("signed.xml") as invoice:
            with client.report_simplified_invoice(
                invoice, credentials, clearance=ClearanceMode.DISABLED, accept_language="en"
            ) as response:
                response.ensure_accepted()
                print("Invoice reporting accepted:", response.reporting_status)

Use Node.js 22 or later. In a new working folder, install the package:

npm install fatoority

Save the code as api.mjs beside the input files, then run:

node api.mjs

Download this example. These examples run in Node.js and can also be adapted to TypeScript. In a browser, replace filesystem reads with your application's file input and configure the WASM asset as described in the browser setup. Keep objects in the WASM instance that created them; do not pass them between workers.

Set ZATCA_TOKEN and ZATCA_SECRET in your process environment before running. The example makes a real request to the non-production gateway.

Browser requests also depend on gateway CORS. Keep private credentials on a trusted server.

import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { ClearanceMode, Config, ProductionCsid, Environment, SignedInvoice, ZatcaClient } from 'fatoority';

const environment = Environment.NonProduction; // Credentials must match.
const token = process.env.ZATCA_TOKEN;
const secret = process.env.ZATCA_SECRET;
if (!token || !secret) throw new Error('Set ZATCA_TOKEN and ZATCA_SECRET first');
const client = new ZatcaClient(Config.create(environment));
const credentials = ProductionCsid.create(environment, null, token, secret);
const invoice = SignedInvoice.fromXml(readFileSync('signed.xml', 'utf8'));
const response = await client.reportSimplifiedInvoice(invoice, credentials, ClearanceMode.Disabled, 'en');
response.ensureAccepted();
console.log('Invoice reporting accepted');

Use the .NET 8 SDK or later. Create a console application:

dotnet new console -n FatoorityGuide
cd FatoorityGuide
dotnet add package Fatoority

Save the code as Program.cs. Put the input files beside the project file, then run:

dotnet run

Download this example. The using declarations release native objects. Check the supported .NET platforms before deployment.

Set ZATCA_TOKEN and ZATCA_SECRET in your process environment before running. The example makes a real request to the non-production gateway.

This example uses a blocking request; run it away from your application's UI thread.

using Fatoora;

const ZatcaEnvironment environment = ZatcaEnvironment.NonProduction; // Credentials must match.
string token = Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("ZATCA_TOKEN")
    ?? throw new InvalidOperationException("Set ZATCA_TOKEN first");
string secret = Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("ZATCA_SECRET")
    ?? throw new InvalidOperationException("Set ZATCA_SECRET first");
using var config = Config.Create(environment);
using var client = ZatcaClient.Create(config);
using var credentials = ProductionCsid.Create(environment, null, token, secret);
using var invoice = SignedInvoice.FromXml(File.ReadAllText("signed.xml"));
using var response = client.ReportSimplifiedInvoice(invoice, credentials, ClearanceMode.Disabled, "en");
response.EnsureAccepted();
Console.WriteLine("Invoice reporting accepted");

For this desktop example, use JDK 17+ and Gradle 8. Create an empty project folder and download build.gradle.kts and settings.gradle.kts into it. The build uses Maven Central and includes the JSON library needed by the validation example.

Save the code as src/main/kotlin/Main.kt (create the folders first). Put the input files in the project root and run:

gradle run

Download this example. use releases each native object. For an existing project, or Android's separate artifact and file handling, follow Kotlin setup. The binding also supports Maven; its dependency coordinates are listed there.

Set ZATCA_TOKEN and ZATCA_SECRET in your process environment before running. The example makes a real request to the non-production gateway.

This example uses a blocking request; run it away from your application's UI thread. The binding also provides reportSimplifiedInvoiceAsync for coroutine callers.

import com.fatoora.*
import java.io.File

fun main(args: Array<String>) {
    val environment = Environment.NonProduction // Credentials must match.
    val token = requireNotNull(System.getenv("ZATCA_TOKEN")) { "Set ZATCA_TOKEN first" }
    val secret = requireNotNull(System.getenv("ZATCA_SECRET")) { "Set ZATCA_SECRET first" }
    Config.create(environment).use { config ->
        ZatcaClient.create(config).use { client ->
            ProductionCsid.create(environment, null, token, secret).use { credentials ->
                SignedInvoice.fromXml(File("signed.xml").readText()).use { invoice ->
                    client.reportSimplifiedInvoice(invoice, credentials, ClearanceMode.Disabled, "en").use { response ->
                        response.ensureAccepted()
                        println("Invoice reporting accepted")
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

Use JDK 17+ and Maven for this walkthrough. In an empty project folder, save this pom.xml. It includes the library, a JSON parser for the validation example, and the plugin used by the run command.

Save the code as src/main/java/Guide.java (create the folders first). Put the input files beside pom.xml, then run:

mvn compile exec:java

Download this example. Try-with-resources releases native objects. The library itself supports Java 8+; see Java setup for platform prerequisites, Gradle installation, and Android configuration.

Set ZATCA_TOKEN and ZATCA_SECRET in your process environment before running. The example makes a real request to the non-production gateway.

This example uses a blocking request; run it away from your application's UI thread.

import com.fatoora.*;
import java.nio.file.*;
import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets;

public class Guide {
    static String read(String path) throws java.io.IOException {
        return new String(Files.readAllBytes(Paths.get(path)), StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
    }
    static void write(String path, String text) throws java.io.IOException {
        Files.write(Paths.get(path), text.getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8));
    }
    public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
        Environment environment = Environment.NonProduction; // Credentials must match.
        String token = java.util.Objects.requireNonNull(System.getenv("ZATCA_TOKEN"), "Set ZATCA_TOKEN first");
        String secret = java.util.Objects.requireNonNull(System.getenv("ZATCA_SECRET"), "Set ZATCA_SECRET first");
        try (Config config = Config.create(environment);
             ZatcaClient client = ZatcaClient.create(config);
             ProductionCsid credentials = ProductionCsid.create(environment, null, token, secret);
             SignedInvoice invoice = SignedInvoice.fromXml(read("signed.xml"));
             ValidationResponse response = client.reportSimplifiedInvoice(invoice, credentials, ClearanceMode.Disabled, "en")) {
            response.ensureAccepted();
            System.out.println("Invoice reporting accepted");
        }
    }
}

Download and extract the fatoora-ffi-* archive for your platform from GitHub Releases. Save the example as api.c in the extracted folder, beside the input files.

On Linux, compile the example and the supplied adapter, then run:

cc -std=c11 -Iinclude api.c src/fatoora.c -L. -lfatoora_ffi -Wl,-rpath,'$ORIGIN' -o api
./api signed.xml

Download this example. For other platforms, follow the C installation and linking reference. The cleanup section releases handles and returned strings, including on failure.

Set ZATCA_TOKEN and ZATCA_SECRET in your process environment before running. The example makes a real request to the non-production gateway.

This example uses a blocking request; run it away from your application's UI thread.

#include "fatoora.h"
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

int main(int argc, char **argv) {
    if (argc != 2) {
        fprintf(argc == 1 ? stdout : stderr,
            "Usage: %s signed-invoice.xml\n"
            "Submits a simplified invoice to the non-production gateway.\n", argv[0]);
        return argc == 1 ? 0 : 1;
    }
    const char *token = getenv("ZATCA_TOKEN"), *secret = getenv("ZATCA_SECRET");
    if (!token || !secret) { fputs("Set ZATCA_TOKEN and ZATCA_SECRET first.\n", stderr); return 1; }
    FatooraConfig *config = NULL;
    FatooraSignedInvoice *invoice = NULL;
    FatooraProductionCsid *credentials = NULL;
    FatooraZatcaClient *client = NULL;
    FatooraValidationResponse *response = NULL;
    FatooraError *error = NULL;
    FatooraStatus status = FATOORA_OK;
    int exit_code = 1;
#define TRY(call) do { status = (call); if (status != FATOORA_OK) goto cleanup; } while (0)
    TRY(fatoora_signed_invoice_from_file(argv[1], &invoice, &error));
    TRY(fatoora_config_new(FATOORA_NON_PRODUCTION, &config, &error));
    TRY(fatoora_zatca_client_new(config, &client, &error));
    TRY(fatoora_production_csid_new(FATOORA_NON_PRODUCTION, NULL,
        token, secret, &credentials, &error));
    TRY(fatoora_zatca_client_report_simplified_invoice(client, invoice,
        credentials, FATOORA_CLEARANCE_DISABLED, "en", &response, &error));
    /* Receiving a response does not establish acceptance. */
    TRY(fatoora_validation_response_ensure_accepted(response, &error));
    puts("Invoice reporting accepted.");
    exit_code = 0;
cleanup:
    if (exit_code) fprintf(stderr, "Error %d: %s\n%s\n", (int)status,
        fatoora_error_message(error), fatoora_error_details_json(error));
    fatoora_validation_response_free(response);
    fatoora_zatca_client_free(client);
    fatoora_production_csid_free(credentials);
    fatoora_signed_invoice_free(invoice);
    fatoora_config_free(config);
    fatoora_error_free(error);
    return exit_code;
}

docs.title: Check the result
docs.text:
The example prints Invoice reporting accepted only after checking the reporting outcome. An HTTP 2xx response that decodes successfully does not by itself mean the invoice was accepted.

Outcome What to do Accepted Record the response and retain warnings. For compliance, this means only that the compliance check passed. Rejected Inspect validation messages and correct the invoice before another submission. Unknown Inspect the original status fields; missing, unfamiliar, or contradictory evidence cannot establish acceptance.

Non-2xx responses are errors and retain HTTP status and response details when available. Avoid blind retries when the result of a submission is uncertain.

docs.title: Use clearance for a standard invoice
docs.text:
Choose the clearance operation with a standard invoice and credentials for the same environment. Check the clearance outcome, then retrieve the returned cleared invoice if your workflow needs the gateway document. Save that XML directly.

Acceptance does not guarantee the optional cleared document is present or decodable. Decoding the field establishes UTF-8 text only; it does not parse XML or verify a signature. The clearance reference describes the operation and response accessors.

docs.title: If something goes wrong
docs.text:
Symptom What to check Missing credential variable Set both named environment variables in the process that runs the example. Authentication or authorization error Check the token, secret, credential type, and environment together. Invoice rejected Read the gateway's validation messages and compare them with local validation. Network error or timeout Check connectivity and the selected endpoint; determine whether a request reached the gateway before retrying. Accepted clearance without usable XML Handle the missing or invalid document explicitly; do not silently substitute the submitted XML.

See the API reference for onboarding, renewal, compliance, reporting, clearance, and complete response contracts.

docs.title: Use the fatoora command-line tool
docs.text: Run invoice tasks from your terminal without writing an application. This guide starts with a local schema check, then shows CSR generation, signing, and QR operations. The executable is named fatoora; the installable crate is fatoora-cli.

docs.title: Install and check the command
docs.text:
Choose one installation method:

  • With Rust and Cargo, run cargo install fatoora-cli.
  • Download the fatoora-cli-* archive for your platform from GitHub Releases. Extract it and add the folder containing fatoora (or fatoora.exe) to your PATH.

Release archives use .tar.gz on Linux/macOS and .zip on Windows. They include license texts and rule notices under licenses/zatca/.

Open a terminal and check the installation:

fatoora --help

You should see the command list. Use fatoora <command> --help for that command's options, for example fatoora sign --help.

docs.title: Validate your first invoice
docs.text:
Save sample-invoice.xml in your working folder, open a terminal there, and run:

fatoora validate --invoice sample-invoice.xml

Expected output:

OK

This checks the bundled UBL schema locally. It does not run the full ZATCA profile or submit the invoice. No account or credentials are needed.

docs.title: Run local ZATCA checks
docs.text:
For a practice report, download invoice.xml and previous-hash.txt. This unsigned sample passes the schema check but can produce signature and QR findings under the full profile. The predecessor file is context for this sample only.

Linux / macOS shellPowerShell 
fatoora validate --invoice invoice.xml --profile zatca --format json \
  --previous-invoice-hash "$(cat previous-hash.txt)"

fatoora validate --invoice invoice.xml --profile zatca --format json `
  --previous-invoice-hash (Get-Content -Raw previous-hash.txt).Trim()

For real invoices, obtain the predecessor hash from trusted invoice history. Read is_valid, is_complete, and the stage findings in the JSON output. A complete local check still does not establish gateway acceptance or certificate issuer trust. See invoice validation for interpreting the report.

Use --evaluated-at with an RFC3339 timestamp only when you need a fixed evaluation time, such as a reproducible historical test. Otherwise the command uses the current clock.

docs.title: Generate a CSR and private key
docs.text:
Download csr.properties for a non-production practice run, then run:

fatoora csr --csr-config csr.properties --generated-csr csr.pem --private-key key.pem --pem

This writes csr.pem and key.pem. Keep the key private. Before onboarding your own device, replace the sample properties using the CSR guide.

--pem selects PEM text; without it, output is base64 DER. Without output-file options, the command writes the CSR and key to standard output.

docs.title: Sign invoice XML
docs.text:
For a local example, download invoice.xml, certificate.pem, and private-key.pem. The certificate and key are public demonstration fixtures, not credentials for your business.

fatoora sign --invoice invoice.xml --cert certificate.pem --key private-key.pem --signed-invoice signed.xml

The command writes signed.xml. Use your own matching certificate and key in an integration. The signing guide explains their origin and the next validation step. Certificate and key formats must match: both PEM, or both DER with --cert-format der --key-format der.

Output-file commands can replace existing files; choose paths appropriate to your workflow.

docs.title: Read or generate QR payloads
docs.text:
To read the payload already embedded in signed.xml:

fatoora qr-read --invoice signed.xml

To generate a payload from an unsigned invoice:

fatoora qr --invoice invoice.xml

qr returns the existing payload for valid signed XML. Generation requires unsigned input without an existing nonempty QR payload; partial stamps and failed signed imports are rejected. Add --fail-on-signed when your workflow should reject signed input. Output is base64-encoded text; redirect it to qr.txt if needed. The QR guide explains how to pass it to an image renderer.

docs.title: Compute a hash or prepare a request payload
docs.text:
fatoora generate-hash --invoice invoice.xml

This hashes the supplied XML using ZATCA exclusions, for both signed and unsigned documents. It does not reserialize an invoice model or verify a signature.

This prints a base64 invoice hash. For signed XML, it prints the signed hash; otherwise it hashes finalized invoice XML.

fatoora invoice-request --invoice signed.xml --api-request request.json

This writes a request payload to request.json. It does not submit it. Continue with the API integration guide to handle credentials and acceptance.

docs.title: Interpret validation exit codes
docs.text:
The default schema command and the ZATCA profile have different exit contracts:

Mode Exit code Meaning Schema check 0 Schema valid; prints OK Schema check 1 Validation or execution failure ZATCA profile 0 Valid, including complete coverage; warnings can remain ZATCA profile 2 Invoice rejected ZATCA profile 3 Execution failure; inspect any partial report ZATCA profile 4 Incomplete coverage Command usage 2 Invalid arguments; read the usage message

Do not interpret code 2 without considering whether arguments were accepted and a validation report was produced.

docs.title: If something goes wrong
docs.text:
Symptom What to check Command not found Extract the release archive, update PATH, and open a new terminal. Input file not found Run from the input folder or use an absolute path. Certificate/key error Check that the pair matches and both files use the selected format. Incomplete report Supply trusted predecessor context and inspect missing stages.

For a full walkthrough of a specific task, continue with CSR generation, signing, or validation.

docs.title: Generate a ZATCA CSR and private key
docs.text: A certificate signing request (CSR) contains the identity and public key of your invoicing device. Use it during onboarding to request credentials from ZATCA. This walkthrough creates a CSR and its matching private key locally.

docs.title: Prepare the inputs
docs.text:
Download csr.properties into a working folder. The sample contains demonstration values and targets the non-production environment. You can run it unchanged to learn the workflow.

For your own device, replace the sample values:

Property What to supply csr.common.name Your device or solution common name csr.serial.number The solution serial number in ZATCA's required format csr.organization.identifier Your organization's VAT identifier csr.organization.unit.name The branch or organizational unit csr.organization.name The legal organization name csr.country.name The country code, such as SA csr.invoice.type The invoice-type capability code required for your device csr.location.address The business location csr.industry.business.category The business activity

Use the current field requirements from the ZATCA developer portal when onboarding a real device. The sample values are not a registration for your business. Keep the CSR environment consistent with the API environment you will use next. The examples replace csr.pem and key.pem if those files already exist.

docs.title: Run the example
docs.text:
Choose your language, then follow its setup and run instructions.

RustPythonJavaScriptC#KotlinJavaCCLI

Install Rust and Cargo, then create a project:

cargo new fatoority-guide
cd fatoority-guide
cargo add fatoora-core

Save the code below as src/main.rs. Put the input files in the project root and run:

cargo run

Download this example.

use fatoora_core::config::Environment;
use fatoora_core::csr::{CsrProperties, SigningKey};

fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    let properties = CsrProperties::from_file("csr.properties")?;
    let key = SigningKey::generate();
    let csr = properties.build(&key, Environment::NonProduction)?;
    std::fs::write("csr.pem", csr.to_pem()?)?;
    std::fs::write("key.pem", key.to_pem()?)?;
    println!("Saved csr.pem and key.pem");
    Ok(())
}

Install the package in your Python environment:

pip install fatoority

Save the code as csr.py beside the input files, then run:

python csr.py

Download this example. See Python setup for package details.

from pathlib import Path
from fatoora import CsrProperties, Environment, SigningKey

with CsrProperties.from_file("csr.properties") as properties:
    with SigningKey.generate() as key:
        with properties.build(key, Environment.NON_PRODUCTION) as csr:
            Path("csr.pem").write_text(csr.to_pem(), encoding="utf-8")
            Path("key.pem").write_text(key.to_pem(), encoding="utf-8")
print("Saved csr.pem and key.pem")

Use Node.js 22 or later. In a new working folder, install the package:

npm install fatoority

Save the code as csr.mjs beside the input files, then run:

node csr.mjs

Download this example. These examples run in Node.js and can also be adapted to TypeScript. In a browser, replace filesystem reads with your application's file input and configure the WASM asset as described in the browser setup. Keep objects in the WASM instance that created them; do not pass them between workers.

import { readFileSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { CsrProperties, Environment, SigningKey } from 'fatoority';

const properties = CsrProperties.fromStr(readFileSync('csr.properties', 'utf8'));
const key = SigningKey.generate();
const csr = properties.build(key, Environment.NonProduction);
writeFileSync('csr.pem', csr.toPem());
writeFileSync('key.pem', key.toPem());
console.log('Saved csr.pem and key.pem');

Use the .NET 8 SDK or later. Create a console application:

dotnet new console -n FatoorityGuide
cd FatoorityGuide
dotnet add package Fatoority

Save the code as Program.cs. Put the input files beside the project file, then run:

dotnet run

Download this example. The using declarations release native objects. Check the supported .NET platforms before deployment.

using Fatoora;

using var properties = CsrProperties.FromStr(File.ReadAllText("csr.properties"));
using var key = SigningKey.Generate();
using var csr = properties.Build(key, ZatcaEnvironment.NonProduction);
File.WriteAllText("csr.pem", csr.ToPem());
File.WriteAllText("key.pem", key.ToPem());
Console.WriteLine("Saved csr.pem and key.pem");

For this desktop example, use JDK 17+ and Gradle 8. Create an empty project folder and download build.gradle.kts and settings.gradle.kts into it. The build uses Maven Central and includes the JSON library needed by the validation example.

Save the code as src/main/kotlin/Main.kt (create the folders first). Put the input files in the project root and run:

gradle run

Download this example. use releases each native object. For an existing project, or Android's separate artifact and file handling, follow Kotlin setup. The binding also supports Maven; its dependency coordinates are listed there.

import com.fatoora.*
import java.io.File

fun main(args: Array<String>) {
    CsrProperties.fromStr(File("csr.properties").readText()).use { properties ->
        SigningKey.generate().use { key ->
            properties.build(key, Environment.NonProduction).use { csr ->
                File("csr.pem").writeText(csr.toPem())
                File("key.pem").writeText(key.toPem())
            }
        }
    }
    println("Saved csr.pem and key.pem")
}

Use JDK 17+ and Maven for this walkthrough. In an empty project folder, save this pom.xml. It includes the library, a JSON parser for the validation example, and the plugin used by the run command.

Save the code as src/main/java/Guide.java (create the folders first). Put the input files beside pom.xml, then run:

mvn compile exec:java

Download this example. Try-with-resources releases native objects. The library itself supports Java 8+; see Java setup for platform prerequisites, Gradle installation, and Android configuration.

import com.fatoora.*;
import java.nio.file.*;
import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets;
