public class Guide {
    static String read(String path) throws java.io.IOException {
        return new String(Files.readAllBytes(Paths.get(path)), StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
    }
    static void write(String path, String text) throws java.io.IOException {
        Files.write(Paths.get(path), text.getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8));
    }
    public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
        try (CsrProperties properties = CsrProperties.fromStr(read("csr.properties"));
             SigningKey key = SigningKey.generate();
             Csr csr = properties.build(key, Environment.NonProduction)) {
            write("csr.pem", csr.toPem());
            write("key.pem", key.toPem());
        }
        System.out.println("Saved csr.pem and key.pem");
    }
}

Download and extract the fatoora-ffi-* archive for your platform from GitHub Releases. Save the example as csr.c in the extracted folder, beside the input files.

On Linux, compile the example and the supplied adapter, then run:

cc -std=c11 -Iinclude csr.c src/fatoora.c -L. -lfatoora_ffi -Wl,-rpath,'$ORIGIN' -o csr
./csr csr.properties

Download this example. For other platforms, follow the C installation and linking reference. The cleanup section releases handles and returned strings, including on failure.

The example saves key.pem and csr.pem. Keep the key private.

#include "fatoora.h"
#include <stdio.h>

static int write_pem(const char *path, const char *pem) {
    FILE *file = fopen(path, "wb");
    if (!file) return 0;
    int written = fputs(pem, file) >= 0;
    return fclose(file) == 0 && written;
}

int main(int argc, char **argv) {
    if (argc != 2) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Usage: %s csr.properties\n", argv[0]);
        return 1;
    }
    FatooraCsrProperties *properties = NULL;
    FatooraSigningKey *key = NULL;
    FatooraCsr *csr = NULL;
    FatooraError *error = NULL;
    char *csr_pem = NULL, *key_pem = NULL;
    FatooraStatus status = FATOORA_OK;
    int exit_code = 1;
#define TRY(call) do { status = (call); if (status != FATOORA_OK) goto cleanup; } while (0)
    TRY(fatoora_csr_properties_from_file(argv[1], &properties, &error));
    TRY(fatoora_signing_key_generate(&key, &error));
    TRY(fatoora_csr_properties_build(properties, key, FATOORA_NON_PRODUCTION, &csr, &error));
    TRY(fatoora_csr_to_pem(csr, &csr_pem, &error));
    TRY(fatoora_signing_key_to_pem(key, &key_pem, &error));
    if (!write_pem("key.pem", key_pem) || !write_pem("csr.pem", csr_pem)) {
        fputs("Unable to write key.pem or csr.pem.\n", stderr);
        goto cleanup;
    }
    puts("Saved csr.pem and key.pem");
    exit_code = 0;
cleanup:
    if (status != FATOORA_OK) fprintf(stderr, "Error %d: %s\n", (int)status, fatoora_error_message(error));
    fatoora_string_free(key_pem);
    fatoora_string_free(csr_pem);
    fatoora_csr_free(csr);
    fatoora_signing_key_free(key);
    fatoora_csr_properties_free(properties);
    fatoora_error_free(error);
    return exit_code;
}

Install the command-line tool with cargo install fatoora-cli, or extract a release binary and add it to your PATH. See the CLI guide for platform setup. Run beside your input files:

fatoora csr --csr-config csr.properties --generated-csr csr.pem --private-key key.pem --pem

docs.title: Check the result
docs.text:
You should have a CSR beginning with -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE REQUEST----- and a key beginning with -----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----. The selected example explains where it writes those blocks. The CSR can be submitted for onboarding; keep the private key for signing and do not send it as part of the CSR request.

The examples use PEM text. Some integrations expect base64 DER instead; choose the representation required by the receiving endpoint rather than encoding PEM again.

docs.title: If something goes wrong
docs.text:
Symptom What to check Configuration file not found Run from the folder containing csr.properties, or change the path in your example. Properties cannot be parsed Check spelling, missing values, and the property names in the table above. Onboarding rejects the request Check business identifiers, the required device fields, OTP, and environment against the portal response.

Next, request credentials and connect to ZATCA. See the CSR reference for additional formats and constructors.

docs.title: Create an invoice
docs.text:
Build a simplified invoice with two notebooks priced at SAR 50 each, excluding VAT. fatoority calculates SAR 15 VAT and a SAR 115 payable total, then writes invoice.xml. No certificate or API credentials are needed.

This example uses demonstration seller details, a fixed timestamp, and a sample previous-invoice hash. Replace them with your own data for an integration. Your application owns invoice numbering, UUIDs, counters, and predecessor history. Running the example replaces invoice.xml in the working folder.

For one runnable program covering creation through reporting, follow the sandbox walkthrough.

docs.title: Run the example
docs.text:
RustPython

Create a project and add the library:

cargo new fatoority-create
cd fatoority-create
cargo add fatoora-core

Save this code as src/main.rs and run cargo run. Download creation.rs.

use fatoora_core::invoice::{
    Address, CountryCode, InvoiceBuilder, InvoiceSubType, InvoiceType, LineItem, OtherId, Party,
    PaymentMeans, SellerRole, VatCategory, VatId,
};

fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    let seller = Party::<SellerRole>::new(
        "Example Store",
        Address::new(
            CountryCode::parse("SA")?,
            "Riyadh",
            "King Fahd Road",
            "1234",
            "12222",
        )
        .with_additional_number("5678")
        .with_district("Olaya"),
        VatId::parse("399999999900003")?,
        Some(OtherId::with_scheme("7003339333", "CRN")),
    );
    let item = LineItem::new(
        "Notebook",
        "2".parse()?,
        "PCE",
        "50".parse()?,
        "15".parse()?,
        VatCategory::Standard,
    )?;
    let invoice = InvoiceBuilder::new(InvoiceType::Tax(InvoiceSubType::Simplified))
        .id("INV-1001")
        .uuid("8e6000cf-1a98-4174-b3e7-b5d5954bc10d".parse()?)
        .issue_datetime("2026-10-26T09:00:00Z".parse()?)
        .currency("SAR".parse()?)
        // Demonstration predecessor; use your own invoice history in production.
        .previous_invoice_hash("NWZlY2ViNjZmZmM4NmYzOGQ5NTI3ODZjNmQ2OTZjNzljMmRiYzIzOWRkNGU5MWI0NjcyOWQ3M2EyN2ZiNTdlOQ==".parse()?)
        .invoice_counter(1)
        .seller(seller)
        .payment_means(PaymentMeans::new("10"))
        .vat_category(VatCategory::Standard)
        .line_item(item)
        .build()?;

    std::fs::write("invoice.xml", invoice.to_xml()?)?;
    println!("VAT: {} SAR", invoice.totals().tax_amount());
    println!("Payable: {} SAR", invoice.totals().payable_amount());
    println!("Saved invoice.xml");
    Ok(())
}

Install the package:

pip install fatoority

Save this code as creation.py and run python creation.py. Download creation.py.

from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path
from uuid import UUID
from fatoora import (Address, InvoiceBuilder, InvoiceSubType, InvoiceTypeKind,
                     PaymentMeans, VatCategory)

seller_address = Address(
    "SA", "Riyadh", "King Fahd Road", "1234", "12222",
    additional_number="5678", district="Olaya",
)
invoice = (
    InvoiceBuilder(
        InvoiceTypeKind.TAX, InvoiceSubType.SIMPLIFIED,
        id="INV-1001",
        uuid=UUID("8e6000cf-1a98-4174-b3e7-b5d5954bc10d"),
        issue_datetime=datetime(2026, 10, 26, 9, 0, tzinfo=timezone.utc),
        currency="SAR",
        # Demonstration predecessor; use your own invoice history in production.
        previous_invoice_hash="NWZlY2ViNjZmZmM4NmYzOGQ5NTI3ODZjNmQ2OTZjNzljMmRiYzIzOWRkNGU5MWI0NjcyOWQ3M2EyN2ZiNTdlOQ==",
        invoice_counter=1,
        vat_category=VatCategory.STANDARD,
    )
    .set_seller("Example Store", address=seller_address, vat_id="399999999900003",
                other_id="7003339333", other_id_scheme="CRN")
    .add_payment_means(PaymentMeans("10"))
    .add_line_item(description="Notebook", quantity="2", unit_code="PCE", unit_price="50",
                   vat_rate="15", vat_category=VatCategory.STANDARD)
    .build()
)
Path("invoice.xml").write_text(invoice.xml, encoding="utf-8")
totals = invoice.totals
print(f"VAT: {totals.tax_amount} SAR")
print(f"Payable: {totals.payable_amount} SAR")
print("Saved invoice.xml")

Expected output:

VAT: 15 SAR
Payable: 115 SAR
Saved invoice.xml

Open the XML to inspect the seller and line item, followed by the VAT breakdown and monetary totals. Decimal inputs keep their precision through calculation; XML monetary fields are written with two decimal places. See rounding for calculated and supplied amounts.

docs.title: Adapt it to your application
docs.text:
Use the pricing and invoice recipes for discounts, charges, mixed VAT, credit/debit notes, and prepayment adjustments. The invoice model reference covers additional fields and the language bindings. JavaScript/TypeScript, C#, Kotlin/Java, and C/C++ expose builders through the same core.

If your application already has XML, use XML import to inspect the supported fields or pass the document to the signing guide. Unsigned model serialization may normalize formatting and omit unsupported extensions. Signed import retains the original XML and checks its local integrity.

docs.title: Sign and validate
docs.text:
Building checks the model's fields and arithmetic. Run the validation guide for schema and local ZATCA rules. An unsigned document has no signature to verify; after signing with your certificate and matching key, validate that signed document before submission. The validation guide uses an unsigned fixture named invoice.xml; to check the document you just signed, point the CLI at signed.xml:

fatoora validate --invoice signed.xml --profile zatca --format json \
  --previous-invoice-hash "$PREVIOUS_INVOICE_HASH"

Set PREVIOUS_INVOICE_HASH to the expected predecessor from your invoice history. For this demonstration, use the sample predecessor supplied to the builder. Keep signed.xml intact when validating or submitting it.

The example creates UBL XML. PDF rendering is on the project roadmap.

docs.title: Pricing and invoice recipes
docs.text: Start with the runnable invoice creation example. The Rust fragments below replace its line item or extend its builder. Use the advanced binding methods for the corresponding operations in other languages.

docs.title: Price per pack and a line discount
docs.text:
A price base expresses how much quantity the quoted price covers. Here, SAR 100 buys ten units. Selling 25 units gives SAR 250 before a SAR 10 line allowance: line net is SAR 240, VAT is SAR 36, and line gross is SAR 276.

Replace the example's let item = ... with:

use fatoora_core::invoice::Adjustment;

let item = LineItem::builder()
    .item_name("Notebook")
    .invoiced_quantity("25".parse()?)
    .invoiced_quantity_unit_code("PCE")
    .item_net_price("100".parse()?)
    .item_price_base_quantity("10".parse()?)
    .vat_category(VatCategory::Standard)
    .vat_rate("15".parse()?)
    .allowance(Adjustment::amount("10".parse()?).with_reason("Volume discount"))
    .build()?;

Use .charge(...) for a line surcharge. An Adjustment::percent_of(base, percent) calculates an adjustment using the supplied base. For example, a 10% allowance on SAR 250 is Adjustment::percent_of("250".parse()?, "10".parse()?).

For gross pricing, supply .item_gross_price(...) and .item_price_discount(...). The builder derives the net price and checks it if you also supply .item_net_price(...). Price-base division retains exact rational precision until the line net is rounded at the calculation boundary.

docs.title: Document discounts and charges
docs.text:
Each document adjustment carries its VAT category and rate. To subtract SAR 10 from the creation example's SAR 100 taxable amount, add this call before .build():

.allowance(fatoora_core::invoice::DocumentAdjustment::new(
    fatoora_core::invoice::Adjustment::amount("10".parse()?).with_reason("Loyalty discount"),
    VatCategory::Standard,
    "15".parse()?,
))

The resulting VAT is SAR 13.50 and payable is SAR 103.50. Use .charge(...) for shipping or another document charge with its own tax treatment. Repeated calls append adjustments.

DocumentAdjustment also takes a .with_reason_code(...), a .with_exemption(...) for non-standard categories, and Adjustment::percent_of(base, percent) for a percentage of a base amount. An out-of-scope entry can omit its rate with .omit_vat_rate().

The scalar invoice_level_discount, invoice_level_charge and allowance_reason setters were removed in 0.7; see migrating to 0.7.

docs.title: Mixed VAT categories and rates
docs.text:
Assign each line its category and rate. The builder groups accepted line net amounts by both values, applies each group's document adjustments, and calculates the VAT breakdown. Document VAT is the sum of breakdown taxes.

For example, SAR 100 at 15% plus SAR 50 at 0% gives SAR 15 VAT and SAR 165 payable before other adjustments. Use VatCategory::Zero for the zero-rated line. Exempt and OutOfScope are also available; those categories use a zero rate.

Set exemption metadata where the invoice's tax treatment requires it. A line builder accepts .exemption(TaxExemption::default().with_reason_code(code).with_reason(text)); document breakdown metadata uses .tax_exemption(category, rate, exemption) on the invoice builder. Both fields are optional strings in the model. Choose the applicable code and explanation for the transaction, then run local business validation.

docs.title: Credit and debit notes
docs.text:
Use InvoiceType::CreditNote(InvoiceSubType::Simplified) or InvoiceType::DebitNote(InvoiceSubType::Simplified) in place of the tax-invoice type. Both also support Standard. Add the original invoice reference and a payment instruction explaining the correction:

.billing_reference(fatoora_core::invoice::OriginalInvoiceRef::new("INV-1001"))
.payment_instruction("Return of goods")

Keep line quantities and amounts positive. The document type identifies the correction. Set a new ID, UUID, issue timestamp, counter, and predecessor hash for the note. Repeated .billing_reference(...) calls preserve multiple references.

docs.title: Prepayments and final payable amounts
docs.text:
Use InvoiceType::Prepayment(subtype) to create a prepayment invoice. On an invoice that deducts an advance payment, .prepaid_amount(...) subtracts the supplied amount from the tax-inclusive total. .payable_rounding_amount(...) applies a signed rounding adjustment:

Payable = tax-inclusive total − prepaid amount + payable rounding

A SAR 115 tax-inclusive total with SAR 23 prepaid has SAR 92 payable. This amount also supplies QR Tag 4.

To represent an advance payment of SAR 20 plus SAR 3 VAT, insert this declaration before let invoice = ... in the creation example:

use fatoora_core::invoice::{InvoiceTime, OriginalInvoiceRef, VatBreakdown};

let advance = LineItem::builder()
    .item_name("Advance payment adjustment")
    .invoiced_quantity("0".parse()?)
    .invoiced_quantity_unit_code("PCE")
    .item_net_price("0".parse()?)
    .vat_category(VatCategory::Standard)
    .vat_rate("15".parse()?)
    .document_reference(
        OriginalInvoiceRef::new("PRE-1001")
            .with_uuid("b2a43c49-3aab-4e3b-9d67-0da45a5e33cc".parse()?)
            .with_issue_date("2026-10-25".parse()?)
            .with_issue_time(InvoiceTime::parse("09:00:00Z")?)
            .with_document_type_code("386"),
    )
    .tax_subtotal(VatBreakdown::new(
        VatCategory::Standard,
        "15".parse()?,
        "20".parse()?,
        "3".parse()?,
    )?)
    .build()?;

Keep the sale's .line_item(item) call and add these calls before the invoice's .build():

.line_item(advance)
.prepaid_amount("23".parse()?)

The result has SAR 15 document VAT and SAR 92 payable. Replace the sample reference with the prepayment invoice's actual identity and issue date/time.

with_document_type_code("386") marks the reference as a prepayment. Without it, the model treats the line as an ordinary sale. Adjustment lines must have zero quantity, price, line net, and line VAT; the advance amounts belong in their VAT subtotals. Their combined taxable and tax subtotals must equal prepaid_amount. Setting that amount alone does not create references or adjustment lines. See the model contract for the calculation checks.

Application data Rust builder API Purchase order or contract purchase_order_id(...), contract_id(...) Actual/latest delivery dates delivery(Delivery::default().with_actual_date(date).with_latest_date(date)) Payment code with instructions and account payment_means(PaymentMeans::new(code).with_instruction_note(text).with_payee_financial_account(account)) Additional party identifiers seller_identifier(...), buyer_identifier(...) Item identifiers Line builder item_seller_identifier(...), item_buyer_identifier(...), item_standard_identifier(...) Notes in different languages Repeated note(InvoiceNote::new(language, text)) calls

Use collection getters when reading repeated values; convenience getters expose the first entry. XML import preserves the supported fields, subject to the documented normalization and unsupported-content policy.

docs.title: Sign ZATCA invoice XML
docs.text:
Sign an invoice using a certificate and its matching private key, then save the result as signed.xml. Signing generates signature material; run validation separately to check the invoice's local rule and integrity results.

Need an invoice first? Create one from application data, then use its invoice.xml with the signing code below.

docs.title: Prepare the inputs
docs.text:
For a local practice run, save these files in one folder:

  • invoice.xml, an unsigned simplified invoice.
  • certificate.pem, a demonstration certificate.
  • private-key.pem, its matching demonstration key.

These are public test fixtures, suitable only for local examples. For your integration, use your own invoice and the certificate issued for the private key created during CSR generation. See API onboarding for the next steps. Do not pair a newly generated key with an unrelated certificate.

The examples write signed.xml in your working folder, replacing that file if it exists.

#include "fatoora.h"
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

/* Read a PEM file into a NUL-terminated string. */
static char *read_pem(const char *path) {
    FILE *file = fopen(path, "rb");
    if (!file) return NULL;
    char *data = NULL;
    if (fseek(file, 0, SEEK_END)) goto done;
    long size = ftell(file);
    if (size <= 0 || size > 1024 * 1024) goto done;
    rewind(file);
    data = malloc((size_t)size + 1);
    if (!data) goto done;
    if (fread(data, 1, (size_t)size, file) != (size_t)size) {
        free(data);
        data = NULL;
    } else {
        data[size] = '\0';
    }
done:
    fclose(file);
    return data;
}

int main(int argc, char **argv) {
    if (argc != 4) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Usage: %s invoice.xml certificate.pem private-key.pem\n", argv[0]);
        return 1;
    }
    char *cert = read_pem(argv[2]);
    char *key = read_pem(argv[3]);
    if (!cert || !key) {
        fputs("Unable to read certificate or private key PEM.\n", stderr);
        free(cert);
        free(key);
        return 1;
    }
    FatooraInvoiceSigner *signer = NULL;
    FatooraFinalizedInvoice *invoice = NULL;
    FatooraSignedInvoice *signed_invoice = NULL;
    FatooraError *error = NULL;
    char *xml = NULL;
    FatooraStatus status = FATOORA_OK;
    int exit_code = 1;
#define TRY(call) do { status = (call); if (status != FATOORA_OK) goto cleanup; } while (0)
    TRY(fatoora_invoice_signer_from_pem(cert, key, &signer, &error));
    TRY(fatoora_finalized_invoice_from_file(argv[1], &invoice, &error));
    /* Signing consumes invoice's inner state; its outer handle still needs free. */
    TRY(fatoora_invoice_signer_sign(signer, invoice, &signed_invoice, &error));
    TRY(fatoora_signed_invoice_into_xml(signed_invoice, &xml, &error));
    puts(xml);
    exit_code = 0;
cleanup:
    if (exit_code) fprintf(stderr, "Error %d: %s\n", (int)status, fatoora_error_message(error));
    fatoora_string_free(xml);
    fatoora_signed_invoice_free(signed_invoice);
    fatoora_finalized_invoice_free(invoice);
    fatoora_invoice_signer_free(signer);
    fatoora_error_free(error);
    free(cert);
    free(key);
    return exit_code;
}

Install the command-line tool with cargo install fatoora-cli, or extract a release binary and add it to your PATH. See the CLI guide for platform setup. Run beside your input files:

fatoora sign --invoice invoice.xml --cert certificate.pem --key private-key.pem --signed-invoice signed.xml

docs.title: Check the result
docs.text:
Open signed.xml. It should contain invoice XML with signature material and QR data. The examples save the full XML rather than just a hash or signature string. Keep the resulting document intact when storing or submitting it.

Signing alone does not establish business-rule compliance or gateway acceptance. Next, validate the original signed XML before reporting or clearance.

docs.title: If something goes wrong
docs.text:
Symptom What to check Certificate/key parsing fails Match the input format shown in the selected example; PEM and DER are different representations. Certificate/key mismatch Use the private key corresponding to the certificate, not a key from a later CSR attempt. XML cannot be parsed Check that you supplied a supported invoice document, with its required fields and amounts. Signed XML fails local validation Inspect individual findings; adding a signature does not repair invoice data.

See the signing reference for signature metadata, formats, and lower-level operations.

docs.title: Generate and read ZATCA QR payloads
docs.text: A ZATCA invoice QR code contains a base64-encoded TLV (tag-length-value) payload. fatoority exposes that text so you can store it or pass it to a QR image renderer. This walkthrough reads an existing payload from a signed invoice and saves qr.txt.

docs.title: Prepare the input
docs.text: Download signed.xml into a working folder, or use an invoice you created with the signing guide. The download is a public demonstration fixture. Signed imports check local integrity; this establishes neither certificate issuer trust nor acceptance by ZATCA.

docs.title: Choose the operation
docs.text: Read the embedded payload when you want exactly what an existing signed invoice contains. When creating a new signed invoice, signing also produces its QR data; sign first, then read that payload. The command-line example additionally shows how to generate payloads from unsigned XML.

#include "fatoora.h"
#include <stdio.h>

int main(int argc, char **argv) {
    if (argc != 2) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Usage: %s signed-invoice.xml\n", argv[0]);
        return 1;
    }
    FatooraSignedInvoice *invoice = NULL;
    FatooraError *error = NULL;
    char *qr = NULL;
    FatooraStatus status = fatoora_signed_invoice_from_file(argv[1], &invoice, &error);
    if (status == FATOORA_OK)
        status = fatoora_signed_invoice_qr_code(invoice, &qr, &error);
    if (status == FATOORA_OK) puts(qr);
    else fprintf(stderr, "Error %d: %s\n", (int)status, fatoora_error_message(error));
    fatoora_string_free(qr);
    fatoora_signed_invoice_free(invoice);
    fatoora_error_free(error);
    return status == FATOORA_OK ? 0 : 1;
}

docs.title: Check the result
docs.text: The example writes qr.txt, containing the base64-encoded payload. It is text, not a PNG or SVG. Tags 1–5 carry seller and amount data; signing tags are present when supplied by the invoice. The encoded payload must fit the supported size limit.

docs.title: Render a QR image
docs.text:
Read the payload from qr.txt, removing any trailing line break from terminal output. Pass that base64 text directly to your application's QR rendering library. Do not base64-encode the text again. Select the image size and output format for your receipt or invoice layout, then scan the rendered image to confirm it decodes to the same payload.

Image rendering is a separate step; fatoority does not produce an image file here.

docs.title: If something goes wrong
docs.text:
Symptom What to check No embedded payload can be read Use signed XML that contains QR data, or create a signed invoice first. Generation reports missing seller fields Supply the seller name and VAT identifier in the invoice. Payload exceeds a length limit Check field byte lengths, including UTF-8 text, and the encoded payload length. QR scanning returns unexpected text Feed the encoded payload directly to the renderer; avoid extra encoding or wrapping.

Next, validate the invoice's QR and signature checks. See the QR reference for payload limits and error types.

docs.title: Report your first sandbox invoice
docs.text:
Pick Python, C#, or TypeScript and run one program that creates a simplified invoice for SAR 115, signs it, validates the signed XML, and reports it to ZATCA's Integration Sandbox. It saves the response and checks whether reporting was accepted. Each language follows the same steps and uses the same input file.

You need a sandbox certificate and its matching private key. Reporting also needs the sandbox token and secret issued for that device. Without credentials, you can run the local steps with the public test certificate below; that run sends nothing.

docs.title: Where this fits in the ZATCA journey
docs.text:
An EGS is your electronic invoice generation system. Onboarding identifies each EGS unit and gives it credentials. Once onboarded, it can submit invoices and notes.

flowchart TD
    A[Select environment and EGS] --> B[Private key, CSR and OTP]
    B --> C[Compliance credentials]
    C --> D[Check invoice and note samples]
    D --> E{Checks pass?}
    E -->|No| F[Correct and restart onboarding]
    F --> B
    E -->|Yes| G[Production-type credentials]
    G --> H[Create invoice and record history]
    H --> I{Subtype}
    I -->|Simplified| J[Sign and validate]
    J --> K[Issue to customer and report]
    I -->|Standard| L[Prepare XML and validate]
    L --> M[Request clearance before issue]
    K --> N{API outcome}
    M --> N
    N -->|Accepted| O[Store XML and response]
    O --> P[Standard only: deliver cleared XML]
    N -->|Rejected| Q[Follow correction procedure]
    N -->|Unknown| R[Reconcile before retry]

Keep credentials under lifecycle management too: renew them before expiry and revoke them when the EGS unit is retired or its credentials must be withdrawn. A connection failure can leave the API outcome unknown.

The runnable examples cover the simplified branch: creation through reporting. In live operation, simplified documents are reported within 24 hours. Standard documents follow clearance before customer delivery; retain the returned cleared XML. These are separate submission paths. ZATCA describes both in sections 4.3.1 and 4.3.2 of its Detailed Technical Guidelines.

Local validation catches problems before an API call. ZATCA still makes the submission decision, and a sandbox result is only a test result.

docs.title: 1. Get the sandbox inputs
docs.text:
If you already have sandbox production-type credentials, continue to the files below. Otherwise, use the ZATCA Developer Portal to complete this sequence for your test EGS unit:

  1. Generate a private key and CSR using the non-production environment and your test seller identity. Keep the private key. The CSR guide has runnable commands; declare the document types your unit supports.
  2. Send the CSR with the sandbox's OTP through Compliance CSID (POST /compliance). Retain the returned compliance token, secret, certificate, and request ID.
  3. Sign and submit the required samples to Compliance Invoice (POST /compliance/invoices) using the compliance credentials. The checks cover invoice and credit/debit note types declared in the CSR. One successful invoice check does not complete all onboarding checks.
  4. Use the compliance credentials and returned request ID to request Production CSID (POST /production/csids). Save that response's token and secret, and the issued certificate corresponding to your private key.

The library exposes these operations as request_compliance_csid, check_invoice_compliance, and request_production_csid, with corresponding methods in the other bindings. ZATCA documents the onboarding sequence in section 3.3 of the Detailed Technical Guidelines.

“Production CSID” is the credential's role. A production-type CSID issued by the Integration Sandbox belongs to the sandbox. It cannot authenticate against the live production environment. See ZATCA's Developer Portal Manual.

Prepare these inputs:

Input What to use certificate.pem PEM certificate issued for the sandbox device. private-key.pem The private key used to create that device's CSR. ZATCA_TOKEN binarySecurityToken from the sandbox production-CSID response, unchanged. ZATCA_SECRET secret from that same response. input.json Seller details matching your test device, plus invoice identity and trusted predecessor context.

The token is an API credential; the signing examples expect a PEM certificate file. Export the issued certificate in PEM format. A newly generated key will not match a certificate issued for an earlier CSR.

docs.title: 2. Download one complete example
docs.text:
Download one project and extract it into an empty working folder. Each archive contains the complete source, project configuration, and input.json. Open a terminal in that folder.

Edit the seller in input.json to match your sandbox onboarding identity. The sample contains demonstration data. invoice_counter is a decimal string to avoid JavaScript integer precision loss; use the next counter for your EGS unit. The predecessor hash must come from your trusted invoice history. The sample value is for the demonstration's initial invoice, not a value to reuse for every invoice. Each run generates a new UUID and the current UTC issue time.

PythonC#TypeScript

Download the Python project

Use CPython 3.13 for this walkthrough. Version 0.7.0 publishes wheels for CPython 3.10–3.13; Python 3.14 needs a source build and is outside this setup. Individual files: main.py and requirements.txt.

python3.13 -m venv .venv
. .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt

On Windows PowerShell, create the environment with py -3.13 -m venv .venv and activate it with .venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1.

Complete Python program 
"""One simplified invoice: create, sign, validate, report, inspect the result."""
import argparse
from datetime import datetime, timezone
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import sys
from uuid import uuid4

from fatoora import (Address, ClearanceMode, Config, Environment, InvoiceBuilder, InvoiceSigner,
                     InvoiceSubType, InvoiceTypeKind, PaymentMeans, ProductionCsid, VatCategory,
                     ZatcaClient, validate_zatca)
from fatoora.errors import FatooraError

ENVIRONMENT = Environment.NON_PRODUCTION  # Integration Sandbox only.


def required(name):
    value = os.environ.get(name, "").strip()
    if not value:
        raise ValueError(f"Set {name} first")
    return value


def save_json(path, value):
    path.write_text(json.dumps(value, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")


def messages(items):
    result = []
    for item in items:
        with item:
            result.append({"code": item.code, "message": item.message})
    return result


def handle_response(response, output):
    with response.validation_results as results:
        summary = {
            "http_status": response.http_status,
            "outcome": response.outcome.name,
            "reporting_status": response.reporting_status,
            "validation_status": results.status,
            "info": messages(results.info_messages),
            "warnings": messages(results.warning_messages),
            "errors": messages(results.error_messages),
        }
    save_json(output / "response.json", summary)
    print(json.dumps(summary, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False))
    response.ensure_accepted()  # A successful HTTP status alone is insufficient.
    print("Sandbox reporting accepted. Keep any warnings in response.json.")


def run(input_path, submit):
    # Read credentials before creating an invoice; never write them into artifacts.
    certificate = Path(required("ZATCA_CERT_PATH")).read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    key = Path(required("ZATCA_KEY_PATH")).read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    token, secret = (required("ZATCA_TOKEN"), required("ZATCA_SECRET")) if submit else (None, None)
    data = json.loads(Path(input_path).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    seller = data["seller"]
    invoice_uuid = uuid4()
    output = Path("runs") / str(invoice_uuid)
    output.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False)
    print(f"Artifacts: {output}")
    state = {"uuid": str(invoice_uuid), "invoice_id": data["invoice_id"], "stage": "create", "submitted": False}
    save_json(output / "state.json", state)
    try:
        address = Address(
            "SA", seller["city"], seller["street"], seller["building_number"], seller["postal_code"],
            district=seller["district"], additional_number=seller["additional_number"],
        )
        with InvoiceBuilder(
            InvoiceTypeKind.TAX, InvoiceSubType.SIMPLIFIED,
            id=data["invoice_id"],
            uuid=invoice_uuid,
            issue_datetime=datetime.now(timezone.utc),
            currency="SAR",
            invoice_counter=int(data["invoice_counter"]),
            previous_invoice_hash=data["previous_invoice_hash"],
            vat_category=VatCategory.STANDARD,
        ) as builder:
            (builder
                .set_seller(seller["name"], address=address, vat_id=seller["vat_id"],
                            other_id=seller["crn"], other_id_scheme="CRN")
                .add_payment_means(PaymentMeans("10"))
                .add_line_item("دفتر", "2", "PCE", "50", "15", VatCategory.STANDARD))
            with builder.build() as invoice, InvoiceSigner.from_pem(certificate, key) as signer:
                (output / "invoice.xml").write_text(invoice.xml, encoding="utf-8")
                print("Created: SAR 100 net + SAR 15 VAT = SAR 115 payable")
                state["stage"] = "sign"
                with invoice.sign(signer) as signed:
                    signed_xml = signed.xml
                    (output / "signed.xml").write_text(signed_xml, encoding="utf-8")
                    state["invoice_hash"] = signed.invoice_hash
                    state["stage"] = "validate"
                    report = validate_zatca(
                        signed_xml, previous_invoice_hash=data["previous_invoice_hash"],
                    )
                    save_json(output / "validation.json", report.to_dict())
                    if not report.is_valid:
                        raise ValueError("Local validation failed; inspect validation.json. Nothing was submitted.")
                    print("Local validation passed; inspect validation.json for warnings")
                    if not submit:
                        state["stage"] = "local_only"
                        print("Local run complete. No reporting request sent. Use --submit with sandbox credentials.")
                        return
                    state["stage"] = "report"
                    state["submitted"] = True  # Attempted; outcome may be unknown if the connection fails.
                    save_json(output / "state.json", state)
                    with ProductionCsid(ENVIRONMENT, token=token, secret=secret) as credentials, \
                            Config(ENVIRONMENT) as config, ZatcaClient(config) as client:
                        with client.report_simplified_invoice(signed, credentials, clearance=ClearanceMode.DISABLED, accept_language="en") as response:
                            handle_response(response, output)
                    state["stage"] = "accepted"
    except Exception as error:
        state["error_type"] = type(error).__name__
        if isinstance(error, FatooraError):
            save_json(output / "error.json", {"code": error.code, "details": error.details})
        raise
    finally:
        save_json(output / "state.json", state)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--input", default="input.json")
    parser.add_argument("--submit", action="store_true", help="Report to the Integration Sandbox")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    try:
        run(args.input, args.submit)
    except Exception as error:
        print(f"Stopped: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
        print("No automatic retry. Inspect saved artifacts before another run.", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)

Download the C# project

Requires the .NET 8 SDK and a supported native platform. Individual files: Program.cs and Journey.csproj.

dotnet restore

The project enables nullable references and imports the Fatoora namespace.

Complete C# program 
using System.Text.Json;
using System.Globalization;
using Fatoora;

public static class Program
{
    private const ZatcaEnvironment Sandbox = ZatcaEnvironment.NonProduction; // Integration Sandbox only.
    private static readonly JsonSerializerOptions JsonOptions = new() { WriteIndented = true };
    private static string Required(string name) =>
        !string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable(name))
            ? Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable(name)!.Trim()
            : throw new InvalidOperationException($"Set {name} first");
    private static void Save(string path, object value) =>
        File.WriteAllText(path, JsonSerializer.Serialize(value, JsonOptions) + "\n");
    private static object[] Messages(nuint count, Func<nuint, ValidationMessage> get)
    {
        var result = new List<object>();
        for (nuint i = 0; i < count; i++)
        {
            using var message = get(i);
            result.Add(new { code = message.Code, message = message.Message });
        }
        return result.ToArray();
    }
    public static void HandleResponse(ValidationResponse response, string output)
    {
        using var results = response.ValidationResults();
        var summary = new {
            http_status = response.HttpStatus, outcome = response.Outcome.ToString(),
            reporting_status = response.ReportingStatusRaw,
            validation_status = results.StatusRaw,
            info = Messages(results.InfoLen, results.InfoMessage),
            warnings = Messages(results.WarningLen, results.WarningMessage),
            errors = Messages(results.ErrorLen, results.ErrorMessage),
        };
        Save(Path.Combine(output, "response.json"), summary);
        Console.WriteLine(JsonSerializer.Serialize(summary, JsonOptions));
        response.EnsureAccepted(); // A successful HTTP status alone is insufficient.
        Console.WriteLine("Sandbox reporting accepted. Keep any warnings in response.json.");
    }
    public static void Run(string inputPath, bool submit)
    {
        string certificate = File.ReadAllText(Required("ZATCA_CERT_PATH"));
        string key = File.ReadAllText(Required("ZATCA_KEY_PATH"));
        string token = submit ? Required("ZATCA_TOKEN") : "";
        string secret = submit ? Required("ZATCA_SECRET") : "";
        using var input = JsonDocument.Parse(File.ReadAllText(inputPath));
        var data = input.RootElement;
        var seller = data.GetProperty("seller");
        string Field(JsonElement parent, string name) => parent.GetProperty(name).GetString()
            ?? throw new InvalidOperationException($"Missing input field: {name}");
        string uuid = Guid.NewGuid().ToString();
        string output = Path.Combine("runs", uuid);
        if (Directory.Exists(output)) throw new IOException("Output directory already exists");
        Directory.CreateDirectory(output);
        Console.WriteLine($"Artifacts: {output}");
        var state = new Dictionary<string, object> {
            ["uuid"] = uuid, ["invoice_id"] = Field(data, "invoice_id"),
            ["stage"] = "create", ["submitted"] = false,
        };
        Save(Path.Combine(output, "state.json"), state);
        try
        {
            using var builder = InvoiceBuilder.Create(InvoiceTypeKind.Tax, InvoiceSubType.Simplified, null, null, null, null);
            builder.SetId(Field(data, "invoice_id"));
            builder.SetUuid(uuid);
            builder.SetIssueDatetime(DateTime.UtcNow.ToString("yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss'Z'", CultureInfo.InvariantCulture));
            builder.SetCurrency("SAR");
            builder.SetInvoiceCounter(ulong.Parse(Field(data, "invoice_counter")));
            builder.SetPreviousInvoiceHash(Field(data, "previous_invoice_hash"));
            using (var means = PaymentMeans.Create("10", null))
                builder.AddPaymentMeans(means);
            builder.SetVatCategory(VatCategory.Standard);
            using var address = Address.Create("SA", Field(seller, "city"), Field(seller, "street"),
                Field(seller, "building_number"), Field(seller, "postal_code"), null,
                Field(seller, "additional_number"), Field(seller, "district"));
            builder.SetSeller(Field(seller, "name"), address, Field(seller, "vat_id"), Field(seller, "crn"), "CRN");
            builder.AddLineItem("دفتر", 2m, "PCE", 50m, 15m, VatCategory.Standard);
            using var invoice = builder.Build();
            File.WriteAllText(Path.Combine(output, "invoice.xml"), invoice.Xml);
            Console.WriteLine("Created: SAR 100 net + SAR 15 VAT = SAR 115 payable");
            state["stage"] = "sign";
            using var signer = InvoiceSigner.FromPem(certificate, key);
            using var signed = signer.Sign(invoice);
            string signedXml = signed.Xml;
            File.WriteAllText(Path.Combine(output, "signed.xml"), signedXml);
            state["invoice_hash"] = signed.InvoiceHash;
            state["stage"] = "validate";
            using var report = Xml.ValidateZatca(signedXml, JsonSerializer.Serialize(new {
                previous_invoice_hash = Field(data, "previous_invoice_hash"),
            }));
            File.WriteAllText(Path.Combine(output, "validation.json"), report.ToJson());
            if (!report.IsValid)
                throw new InvalidOperationException("Local validation failed; inspect validation.json. Nothing was submitted.");
            Console.WriteLine("Local validation passed; inspect validation.json for warnings");
            if (!submit)
            {
                state["stage"] = "local_only";
                Console.WriteLine("Local run complete. No reporting request sent. Use --submit with sandbox credentials.");
                return;
            }
            state["stage"] = "report";
            state["submitted"] = true; // Attempted; a failed connection can leave the outcome unknown.
            Save(Path.Combine(output, "state.json"), state);
            using var credentials = ProductionCsid.Create(Sandbox, null, token, secret);
            using var config = Config.Create(Sandbox);
            using var client = ZatcaClient.Create(config);
            using var response = client.ReportSimplifiedInvoice(signed, credentials, ClearanceMode.Disabled, "en");
            HandleResponse(response, output);
            state["stage"] = "accepted";
        }
        catch (Exception error)
        {
            state["error_type"] = error.GetType().Name;
            if (error is FatooraException native) // InvalidInputException, NetworkException, ...
            {
                using var details = JsonDocument.Parse(native.DetailsJson);
                Save(Path.Combine(output, "error.json"), new { code = native.Code, kind = native.Kind?.ToString(), details = details.RootElement });
            }
            throw;
        }
        finally { Save(Path.Combine(output, "state.json"), state); }
    }
    public static int Main(string[] args)
    {
        try
        {
            string input = "input.json";
            bool submit = false;
            for (int i = 0; i < args.Length; i++)
            {
                if (args[i] == "--submit") submit = true;
                else if (args[i] == "--input" && i + 1 < args.Length) input = args[++i];
                else throw new ArgumentException("Usage: dotnet run -- [--input input.json] [--submit]");
            }
            Run(input, submit);
            return 0;
        }
        catch (Exception error)
        {
            Console.Error.WriteLine($"Stopped: {error.Message}");
            Console.Error.WriteLine("No automatic retry. Inspect saved artifacts before another run.");
            return 1;
        }
    }
}

Download the TypeScript project

Requires Node.js 22+ and npm. This is a server-side Node program. Individual files: main.ts, package.json, and tsconfig.json.

npm install
npm run build

Keep the installed package's WASM file with its generated modules. Node loads it through the package; no browser asset setup is needed for this program.

Complete TypeScript program 
import { mkdirSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { randomUUID } from 'node:crypto';
import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url';
import { resolve } from 'node:path';
import {
  Address, ClearanceMode, Config, Environment, FatooraError, InvoiceBuilder, InvoiceSigner,
  InvoiceSubType, InvoiceTypeKind, PaymentMeans, ProductionCsid, VatCategory, Xml, ZatcaClient,
  type ValidationResponse, type ValidationMessage, type ZatcaValidationReport,
} from 'fatoority';

const ENVIRONMENT = Environment.NonProduction; // Integration Sandbox only.
interface Input {
  invoice_id: string;
  invoice_counter: string;
  previous_invoice_hash: string;
  seller: { name: string; vat_id: string; crn: string; city: string; street: string;
    building_number: string; postal_code: string; additional_number: string; district: string };
}
function required(name: string): string {
  const value = process.env[name]?.trim();
  if (!value) throw new Error(`Set ${name} first`);
  return value;
}
function saveJson(path: string, value: unknown): void {
  writeFileSync(path, JSON.stringify(value, null, 2) + '\n');
}
function messages(count: number, get: (index: number) => ValidationMessage) {
  return Array.from({ length: count }, (_, index) => {
    const item = get(index);
    return { code: item.code, message: item.message };
  });
}
export function handleResponse(response: ValidationResponse, output: string): void {
  const results = response.validationResults();
  const summary = {
    http_status: response.httpStatus, outcome: response.outcome.value,
    reporting_status: response.reportingStatusRaw,
    validation_status: results.statusRaw,
    info: messages(results.infoLen, i => results.infoMessage(i)),
    warnings: messages(results.warningLen, i => results.warningMessage(i)),
    errors: messages(results.errorLen, i => results.errorMessage(i)),
  };
  saveJson(`${output}/response.json`, summary);
  console.log(JSON.stringify(summary, null, 2));
  response.ensureAccepted(); // A successful HTTP status alone is insufficient; throws ApiError.
  console.log('Sandbox reporting accepted. Keep any warnings in response.json.');
}

function printFindings(report: ZatcaValidationReport): void {
  for (const stage of report.stages) {
    for (const finding of stage.findings) {
      console.log(`${finding.severity} ${stage.stage}/${finding.code}: ${finding.message}`);
    }
  }
}

export async function run(inputPath: string, submit: boolean, transport?: typeof fetch): Promise<void> {
  const certificate = readFileSync(required('ZATCA_CERT_PATH'), 'utf8');
  const key = readFileSync(required('ZATCA_KEY_PATH'), 'utf8');
  const token = submit ? required('ZATCA_TOKEN') : '';
  const secret = submit ? required('ZATCA_SECRET') : '';
  const data: Input = JSON.parse(readFileSync(inputPath, 'utf8'));
  const seller = data.seller;
  const uuid = randomUUID();
  const output = `runs/${uuid}`;
  mkdirSync('runs', { recursive: true });
  mkdirSync(output); // A new directory preserves earlier attempts.
  console.log(`Artifacts: ${output}`);
  const state: Record<string, unknown> = {
    uuid, invoice_id: data.invoice_id, stage: 'create', submitted: false,
  };
  saveJson(`${output}/state.json`, state);
  try {
    const builder = InvoiceBuilder.create(InvoiceTypeKind.Tax, InvoiceSubType.Simplified, null, null, null, null);
    builder.setId(data.invoice_id);
    builder.setUuid(uuid);
    builder.setIssueDatetime(new Date().toISOString().replace(/\.\d{3}Z$/, 'Z'));
    builder.setCurrency('SAR');
    builder.setInvoiceCounter(BigInt(data.invoice_counter));
    builder.setPreviousInvoiceHash(data.previous_invoice_hash);
    builder.addPaymentMeans(PaymentMeans.create('10', null));
    builder.setVatCategory(VatCategory.Standard);
    const address = Address.create('SA', seller.city, seller.street, seller.building_number,
      seller.postal_code, null, seller.additional_number, seller.district);
    builder.setSeller(seller.name, address, seller.vat_id, seller.crn, 'CRN');
    builder.addLineItem('دفتر', '2', 'PCE', '50', '15', VatCategory.Standard);
    const invoice = builder.build();
    writeFileSync(`${output}/invoice.xml`, invoice.xml);
    console.log('Created: SAR 100 net + SAR 15 VAT = SAR 115 payable');
    state.stage = 'sign';
    const signed = InvoiceSigner.fromPem(certificate, key).sign(invoice);
    const signedXml = signed.xml;
    writeFileSync(`${output}/signed.xml`, signedXml);
    state.invoice_hash = signed.invoiceHash;
    state.stage = 'validate';
    const report = Xml.validateZatca(signedXml, {
      previousInvoiceHash: data.previous_invoice_hash,
    });
    saveJson(`${output}/validation.json`, report);
    printFindings(report);
    if (!report.isValid) throw new Error('Local validation failed; inspect validation.json. Nothing was submitted.');
    console.log('Local validation passed; inspect validation.json for warnings');
    if (!submit) {
      state.stage = 'local_only';
      console.log('Local run complete. No reporting request sent. Use --submit with sandbox credentials.');
      return;
    }
    state.stage = 'report';
    state.submitted = true; // Attempted; a failed connection can leave the outcome unknown.
    saveJson(`${output}/state.json`, state);
    const client = new ZatcaClient(Config.create(ENVIRONMENT), transport ? { fetch: transport } : {});
    const credentials = ProductionCsid.create(ENVIRONMENT, null, token, secret);
    const response = await client.reportSimplifiedInvoice(signed, credentials, ClearanceMode.Disabled, 'en');
    handleResponse(response, output);
    state.stage = 'accepted';
  } catch (error) {
    state.error_type = error instanceof Error ? error.name : 'UnknownError';
    if (error instanceof FatooraError) {
      saveJson(`${output}/error.json`, { code: error.code, kind: error.kind, message: error.message, details: error.details });
    }
    throw error;
  } finally {
    saveJson(`${output}/state.json`, state);
  }
}

if (process.argv[1] && import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(resolve(process.argv[1])).href) {
  const args = process.argv.slice(2);
  let input = 'input.json';
  let submit = false;
  let valid = true;
  for (let i = 0; i < args.length; i++) {
    if (args[i] === '--submit') submit = true;
    else if (args[i] === '--input' && args[i + 1]) input = args[++i];
    else valid = false;
  }
  if (!valid) {
    console.error('Usage: npm start -- [--input input.json] [--submit]');
    process.exitCode = 1;
  } else {
    run(input, submit).catch(error => {
      console.error(`Stopped: ${error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)}`);
      console.error('No automatic retry. Inspect saved artifacts before another run.');
      process.exitCode = 1;
    });
  }
}

docs.title: 3. Run creation, signing and validation locally
docs.text:
Set the certificate and private-key paths. Use absolute paths if you keep them outside the working folder.

Bash / zshPowerShell 
export ZATCA_CERT_PATH="$PWD/certificate.pem"
export ZATCA_KEY_PATH="$PWD/private-key.pem"

$env:ZATCA_CERT_PATH = Join-Path $PWD "certificate.pem"
$env:ZATCA_KEY_PATH = Join-Path $PWD "private-key.pem"

For a run without sandbox credentials, download the public test certificate and matching test key, keeping those filenames. Use the unmodified demonstration input.json with them. These files are for local testing; replace them with your issued sandbox pair before reporting.

PythonC#TypeScript 
python main.py

dotnet run

npm start

Expected output, with a different UUID on each run:

Artifacts: runs/<uuid>
Created: SAR 100 net + SAR 15 VAT = SAR 115 payable
Local validation passed; inspect validation.json for warnings
Local run complete. No reporting request sent. Use --submit with sandbox credentials.

Open runs/<uuid>/signed.xml and validation.json. The validation report checks the exact signed XML, including the applicable signature and QR checks, using the predecessor supplied independently in input.json. If it fails, the program exits with a nonzero status before constructing a reporting request.

docs.title: 4. Report with your sandbox credentials
docs.text:
Use your issued sandbox certificate/key pair and matching seller data. Load ZATCA_TOKEN and ZATCA_SECRET into the process environment through your shell or secret manager. They must come from the production-type sandbox response, not the compliance-CSID response. Do not put credentials in input.json.

Bash / zshPowerShell 
export ZATCA_TOKEN='<binarySecurityToken from sandbox production CSID>'
export ZATCA_SECRET='<secret from that same response>'

$env:ZATCA_TOKEN = '<binarySecurityToken from sandbox production CSID>'
$env:ZATCA_SECRET = '<secret from that same response>'

Run one command for the complete workflow:

PythonC#TypeScript 
python main.py --submit

dotnet run -- --submit

npm start -- --submit

This creates a new invoice and sends one reporting request. It does not submit the previous local run's artifact. Before repeated submissions, allocate a new invoice ID and counter and supply the correct predecessor in input.json. The examples do not maintain an invoice ledger or automatically advance those fields.

docs.title: 5. Read the response and keep the artifacts
docs.text:
The program saves response.json before calling the library's acceptance check. It prints gateway messages alongside the HTTP status and reporting outcome. For an accepted response, the last line is:

Sandbox reporting accepted. Keep any warnings in response.json.
Result What the example does What to do next Accepted Exits successfully and sets state.json stage to accepted. Store the invoice and response together. Accepted with warnings Succeeds and retains the warnings. Review the warning codes; acceptance does not erase them. Rejected or unknown outcome in a decoded response Saves response.json, then exits nonzero. Read the findings and resolve the outcome before creating another invoice. HTTP error, such as 400 or 401 Exits nonzero; binding diagnostics go to error.json. Inspect status/body details; correct the reported issue or credentials. Connection failure or unreadable response Exits nonzero; state.json records the attempted stage. Treat acceptance as unresolved. Reconcile the attempt before retrying. Local validation failure Saves validation.json and sends nothing. Fix the input indicated by the local findings.

HTTP 200 alone is insufficient. Each example calls ensure_accepted or EnsureAccepted/ensureAccepted, which checks the operation's reporting status and validation results. The API decoder raises an exception for non-2xx responses; such errors may have error.json instead of response.json.

Every run writes to a new runs/<uuid>/ directory:

  • invoice.xml: unsigned XML created from the input.
  • signed.xml: exact signed XML used for validation and reporting.
  • validation.json: local rule findings and stage coverage.
  • response.json: decoded reporting result, when one was returned.
  • error.json: structured binding diagnostics, when available.
  • state.json: invoice identity/hash and the last workflow stage.

In state.json, submitted: true means a reporting call was attempted. It does not mean accepted. Preserve these files after a failure. The program has no retry loop, and running it again creates a different invoice. Protect invoice artifacts and error bodies as business data; the examples do not write credentials into them.

docs.title: What changes for production
docs.text:
Area Sandbox walkthrough Production integration Environment NonProduction / 0, the developer-portal endpoint. Complete the required testing and onboarding for the live environment; configure Production / 2, the core endpoint. Simulation / 1 is a separate test environment. Credentials Test device's certificate/key pair and API token/secret. Credentials issued for the live EGS unit. Changing an environment number does not convert credentials. Invoice data Fixed two-item SAR 115 sale and editable demonstration identity. Real seller/customer data, items, tax treatment, and applicable invoice subtype. History Manually supplied ID, counter, and previous hash. Durable per-unit sequencing and invoice history, safe under concurrent creation. History follows generated invoices; do not advance it only when reporting succeeds. Submission One blocking/awaited sandbox call. Durable submission records and response reconciliation. A retry policy must distinguish rejection from an unknown outcome and preserve invoice identity for retries. Operations Local files and process environment. Managed key storage, credential renewal/revocation, access controls, backups, and monitoring of pending submissions and warnings.

Keep environment selection consistent in the client, credentials, and CSR creation. The example constants deliberately select the sandbox. Before adapting them for production, implement the history and submission behavior above and use the current ZATCA developer materials for your integration requirements.

For standard invoices, supply the required buyer data and use the clearance operation. The library accepts a SignedInvoice for that call; ZATCA clearance produces the document to deliver. Inspect clearance_status. On successful clearance, save cleared_invoice_xml / ClearedInvoiceXml / clearedInvoiceXml and use the returned document for customer delivery. The API reference explains those return types and the nullable cleared-document field.

docs.title: Validate ZATCA invoice XML
docs.text:
Check an invoice before submission and inspect the results to decide what needs fixing. Choose a schema check for XML structure, or the local ZATCA profile for business rules and applicable integrity checks.

Check What it tells you UBL schema Whether the XML conforms to the bundled invoice schema Local ZATCA profile Business-rule findings, applicable signature/QR checks, and which stages were covered

Neither check establishes ZATCA gateway acceptance or certificate issuer trust. Building, parsing, or signing an invoice does not automatically run the full local profile.

docs.title: Prepare the inputs
docs.text:
Save invoice.xml in your working folder. For the local ZATCA check, also save previous-hash.txt. This file supplies the known predecessor context for this demonstration invoice. For real invoices, use the previous invoice's hash from your trusted invoice history; do not copy the current document's claimed predecessor value as independent evidence.

Validate the original XML. Parsing and reserializing it first can change the document being checked. All schemas are bundled; the check does not contact a gateway.

The sample is unsigned: it is useful for a successful schema check and for exploring ZATCA findings. Do not expect its full local report to pass signature checks.

docs.title: Run the example
docs.text:
Choose your language, then follow its setup and run instructions.

RustPythonJavaScriptC#KotlinJavaCCLI

Install Rust and Cargo, then create a project:

cargo new fatoority-guide
cd fatoority-guide
cargo add fatoora-core

Also add the JSON serializer used to print the report:

cargo add serde_json

Save the code below as src/main.rs. Put the input files in the project root and run:

cargo run

Download this example.

use fatoora_core::invoice::validation::{Validator, ZatcaValidationOptions};

fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    let validator = Validator::new();
    let xml = std::fs::read_to_string("invoice.xml")?;
    if std::env::args().any(|arg| arg == "--zatca") {
        let options = ZatcaValidationOptions {
            previous_invoice_hash: Some(std::fs::read_to_string("previous-hash.txt")?.parse()?),
            ..Default::default()
        };
        let report = validator.validate_zatca(&xml, &options)?;
        println!("{}", serde_json::to_string_pretty(&report)?);
        if !report.is_valid() { std::process::exit(1); }
    } else {
        validator.validate_xml(&xml)?;
        println!("XSD valid");
    }
    Ok(())
}

Run the local ZATCA checks

cargo run -- --zatca

The example prints the JSON report and exits nonzero when is_valid is false. Inspect stages for the findings rather than treating all failures as execution errors.

Install the package in your Python environment:

pip install fatoority

Save the code as validation.py beside the input files, then run:

python validation.py

Download this example. See Python setup for package details.

from pathlib import Path
import sys
from fatoora import validate_xml, validate_zatca

xml = Path("invoice.xml").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
if "--zatca" in sys.argv:
    report = validate_zatca(
        xml, previous_invoice_hash=Path("previous-hash.txt").read_text().strip(),
    )
    for finding in report.findings:
        print(finding.severity.value, finding.code, finding.message)
    print(report.to_json())
    sys.exit(0 if report.is_valid else 1)
validate_xml(xml)
print("XSD valid")

Run the local ZATCA checks

python validation.py --zatca

The example prints each finding and the JSON report, and exits nonzero when report.is_valid is false. Inspect report.stages for the findings rather than treating all failures as execution errors.

In a browser, replace filesystem reads with your application's file input and configure the WASM asset as described in the browser setup. Keep objects in the WASM instance that created them; do not pass them between workers.

For this desktop example, use JDK 17+ and Gradle 8. Create an empty project folder and download build.gradle.kts and settings.gradle.kts into it. The build uses Maven Central and includes the JSON library needed by the validation example.

Save the code as src/main/kotlin/Main.kt (create the folders first). Put the input files in the project root and run:

Download this example. use releases each native object. For an existing project, or Android's separate artifact and file handling, follow Kotlin setup. The binding also supports Maven; its dependency coordinates are listed there.

import com.fatoora.*
import java.io.File
import kotlinx.serialization.json.*

fun main(args: Array<String>) {
    val xml = File("invoice.xml").readText()
    if (args.contains("--zatca")) {
        val hash = File("previous-hash.txt").readText().trim()
        val options = buildJsonObject { put("previous_invoice_hash", JsonPrimitive(hash)) }.toString()
        Xml.validateZatca(xml, options).use { report ->
            println(report.toJson())
            if (!report.isValid) kotlin.system.exitProcess(1)
        }
    } else {
        Xml.validate(xml)
        println("XSD valid")
    }
}

Use JDK 17+ and Maven for this walkthrough. In an empty project folder, save this pom.xml. It includes the library, a JSON parser for the validation example, and the plugin used by the run command.

Save the code as src/main/java/Guide.java (create the folders first). Put the input files beside pom.xml, then run:

mvn compile exec:java

Download this example. Try-with-resources releases native objects. The library itself supports Java 8+; see Java setup for platform prerequisites, Gradle installation, and Android configuration.

import com.fatoora.*;
import java.nio.file.*;
import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets;

public class Guide {
    static String read(String path) throws java.io.IOException {
        return new String(Files.readAllBytes(Paths.get(path)), StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
    }
    public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
        String xml = read("invoice.xml");
        if (java.util.Arrays.asList(args).contains("--zatca")) {
            com.google.gson.JsonObject options = new com.google.gson.JsonObject();
            options.addProperty("previous_invoice_hash", read("previous-hash.txt").trim());
            try (ZatcaValidationReport report = Xml.validateZatca(xml, options.toString())) {
                System.out.println(report.toJson());
                if (!report.isValid()) System.exit(1);
            }
        } else {
            Xml.validate(xml);
            System.out.println("XSD valid");
        }
    }
}

Run the local ZATCA checks

mvn compile exec:java -Dexec.args="--zatca"

Download and extract the fatoora-ffi-* archive for your platform from GitHub Releases. Save the example as validation.c in the extracted folder, beside the input files.

On Linux, compile the example and the supplied adapter, then run:

cc -std=c11 -Iinclude validation.c src/fatoora.c -L. -lfatoora_ffi -Wl,-rpath,'$ORIGIN' -o validation
./validation invoice.xml

Download this example. For other platforms, follow the C installation and linking reference. The cleanup section releases handles and returned strings, including on failure.

#include "fatoora.h"
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

static char *read_xml(const char *path) {
    FILE *file = fopen(path, "rb");
    if (!file) return NULL;
    char *xml = NULL;
    if (fseek(file, 0, SEEK_END)) goto done;
    long size = ftell(file);
    if (size < 0 || size > 1024 * 1024) goto done;
    rewind(file);
    xml = malloc((size_t)size + 1);
    if (!xml) goto done;
    if (fread(xml, 1, (size_t)size, file) != (size_t)size) {
        free(xml);
        xml = NULL;
    } else {
        xml[size] = '\0';
    }
done:
    fclose(file);
    return xml;
}

int main(int argc, char **argv) {
    if (argc != 2 && argc != 3) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Usage: %s invoice.xml [validation-options.json]\n", argv[0]);
        return 1;
    }
    FatooraError *error = NULL;
    char *xml = read_xml(argv[1]);
    if (!xml) {
        fputs("Unable to read invoice XML.\n", stderr);
        return 1;
    }
    bool valid = false, complete = false;
    char *options = NULL, *json = NULL;
    FatooraZatcaValidationReport *report = NULL;
    FatooraStatus status = FATOORA_OK;
#define TRY(call) do { status = (call); if (status != FATOORA_OK) goto cleanup; } while (0)
    /* Validate original XML; parsing/reserializing would change the input. */
    if (argc == 3) {
        options = read_xml(argv[2]);
        if (!options) { fputs("Unable to read validation options.\n", stderr); goto cleanup; }
        TRY(fatoora_xml_validate_zatca(xml, options, &report, &error));
        TRY(fatoora_zatca_validation_report_is_valid(report, &valid, &error));
        TRY(fatoora_zatca_validation_report_is_complete(report, &complete, &error));
        TRY(fatoora_zatca_validation_report_to_json(report, &json, &error));
        puts(json);
        printf("valid: %s, complete: %s\n", valid ? "true" : "false", complete ? "true" : "false");
        /* Exit 0 means the report was produced, not that the invoice passed. */
        valid = true;
    } else {
        TRY(fatoora_xml_validate(xml, &valid, &error));
        printf("XSD valid: %s\n", valid ? "true" : "false");
    }
cleanup:
    if (status != FATOORA_OK)
        fprintf(stderr, "Error %d: %s\n", (int)status, fatoora_error_message(error));
    free(options);
    fatoora_string_free(json);
    fatoora_zatca_validation_report_free(report);
    free(xml);
    fatoora_error_free(error);
    return status == FATOORA_OK && valid ? 0 : 1;
}

Run the local ZATCA checks

Save validation-options.json beside the input. It contains predecessor context for the sample only.

./validation invoice.xml validation-options.json

The example prints the JSON report. Exit 0 here means a report was produced; parse is_valid and is_complete with your application's JSON parser before accepting the invoice.

Install the command-line tool with cargo install fatoora-cli, or extract a release binary and add it to your PATH. See the CLI guide for platform setup. Run beside your input files:

fatoora validate --invoice invoice.xml

For local ZATCA rules, use your shell to pass the predecessor hash. In a POSIX shell:

fatoora validate --invoice invoice.xml --profile zatca --format json \
  --previous-invoice-hash "$(cat previous-hash.txt)"

In PowerShell:

fatoora validate --invoice invoice.xml --profile zatca --format json `
  --previous-invoice-hash (Get-Content -Raw previous-hash.txt).Trim()

The schema command prints OK. The ZATCA command prints a report and returns 0 for valid, 2 for rejected, 3 for execution failure, or 4 for incomplete coverage.

docs.title: Interpret the result
docs.text:
A successful schema check prints a success message. It says nothing about business rules or gateway acceptance. A local ZATCA check prints a structured report:

Result How to use it is_valid: true The invoice passes the configured local profile with complete coverage. Keep any warnings. is_valid: false, is_complete: true Inspect stage findings and correct the rejected invoice data. is_complete: false Required context or a validation stage is missing. Resolve the gap before treating the invoice as checked. Execution error The check could not finish normally. Inspect the error and any attached partial report.

Findings include a stage, code, and message. Warnings alone do not make an otherwise valid report fail. Do not discard them or reduce every failure to a generic “invalid invoice.”

docs.title: Understand the coverage
docs.text:
The local profile implements the pinned SDK 238-R3.4.8 adaptations of CEN and Saudi rules: 105 CEN assertion sites and 152 Saudi sites. It runs without an external SDK runtime and uses the same profile in every API environment.

Under this profile, standard invoices skip signature and QR checks. Simplified invoices check the embedded certificate's key, reference digests, signature, and QR fields. These establish local integrity, not certificate issuer trust.

The default evaluation time is a single current UTC snapshot. For a reproducible historical test, supply an explicit evaluation time as documented in the validation options. A fixed demonstration clock should not become the default for your live integration.

docs.title: If something goes wrong
docs.text:
Symptom What to check Schema rejection Read the XML/schema error and correct the indicated structure or value. Incomplete predecessor check Supply the trusted previous-invoice hash from your invoice history. Signature/QR findings on the sample The downloaded invoice.xml is unsigned. To examine signed input, replace it with your signed XML and its matching predecessor context. Different results after editing XML Run checks on the exact document you plan to submit; edits can invalidate signature material.

Next, submit the invoice and check gateway acceptance. The validation reference covers report fields and error contracts; SDK compatibility records differences from the SDK.

docs.title: Migrate from 0.5 to 0.6
docs.text:
0.6 is a breaking release for every package. The Rust core renames items for consistency and replaces strings and Booleans with typed values; every language package now uses those names, takes enums instead of integer codes, and drops the Config argument from validation. Upgrade the language package and its native library together: all packages are released as 0.6.0.

Pick your language:

Language Package Deprecated 0.5 names Migration page Rust fatoora-core = "0.6.0" Renamed items warn until 0.7; retyped items break Rust Python pip install "fatoority==0.6.0" Renamed names warn until 0.7; getters becoming properties breaks Python JavaScript / TypeScript npm install fatoority@0.6.0 new_ (use create) and the renamed adjustment members; getters becoming properties and other renames break JavaScript/TypeScript Kotlin / Java com.fatoority:fatoority:0.6.0 0.5 getter functions, String amount overloads and the renamed adjustment members warn until 0.7; other renames break Kotlin/Java C# / .NET Fatoority 0.6.0 New (use Create) and the renamed adjustment members; other changes break C#/.NET C / C++ Release archives None; every change breaks C/C++

Where a language keeps deprecated names, they forward to the new ones and are removed in 0.7. A good order of work is to fix the compile errors (or, in Python and plain JavaScript, the property calls) first, then turn deprecation warnings into errors and replace what remains.

In every language, builders use set* to replace a value and add* to append one, so flags, set_tax_exemption, set_note and set_payment_means_code become set_flags, add_tax_exemption, add_note and add_payment_means. The 0.5 aggregate allowance setters (invoice_level_discount, invoice_level_charge, allowance_reason, set_allowance) are replaced by allowance/charge entries with an explicit VAT category and rate.

docs.title: What changed per language
docs.text:
• Rust: invoice inputs and getters use typed wrappers (InvoiceUuid, InvoiceTimestamp, CurrencyCode, InvoiceHash, VatId); the fields of invoice value types such as Address are private; Environment is #[non_exhaustive]; serialized adjustments use "kind" instead of "charge". See Rust.
  • Python: getters become properties; invoice data becomes frozen dataclasses (Address, Party, Adjustment, Identifier, ...); dates become datetime/date; keyword-only arguments are enforced. See Python.
  • JavaScript/TypeScript: value getters become read-only properties; optional text is string | null; amounts stay decimal strings; library failures throw FatooraError subclasses; validateZatca returns a plain object; new_ becomes create. See JavaScript/TypeScript.
  • Kotlin/Java: value getters become properties; amounts are BigDecimal; optional text is String?; failures throw BindingException subclasses. See Kotlin/Java.
  • C#/.NET: scalar getters become properties; amounts are decimal; optional text is string?; BindingErrorException becomes FfiException and its subclasses. See C#/.NET.
  • C/C++: functions are renamed with the core types, enums are typed and ZATCA validation returns a report object. See C/C++.

The CLI's commands and flags are unchanged; a blank --previous-invoice-hash is now rejected as invalid options (exit code 3). The full list of changes, including additions, is in the changelog.

docs.title: Migrate from 0.5 to 0.6: C and C++
docs.text: The C facade (fatoora.h) and the C++ headers follow the core names in 0.6 and use typed enums. There are no compatibility aliases: rebuild against the 0.6 headers and fix each compile error. Take fatoora.h, fatoora.c, the generated headers and the shared library from the same 0.6.0 release assets; mixing 0.5 headers with a 0.6 library, or the reverse, is not supported.

docs.title: Upgrade checklist
docs.text:
1. Rename the functions and types in the table below.
  2. Drop the FatooraConfig * argument from fatoora_xml_validate and fatoora_xml_validate_zatca. Validation never depended on the environment.
  3. Read the ZATCA validation result from the returned FatooraZatcaValidationReport * instead of parsing JSON, or call fatoora_zatca_validation_report_to_json for the 0.5 text.
  4. Pass FATOORA_CLEARANCE_DISABLED/FATOORA_CLEARANCE_ENABLED instead of false/true, and update output variables to the typed enums, such as FatooraVatCategory instead of uint8_t.
  5. Update response status reads: the status getters now write an enum plus bool *has_value; the new _raw getters return the 0.5 text.

The existing constants (FATOORA_NON_PRODUCTION, FATOORA_TAX, FATOORA_VAT_STANDARD, FATOORA_FLAG_EXPORT, ...) keep their values, so code that already used them only needs the renames. Passing 0/1 or false/true still compiles; any value that is not a declared enumerator returns FATOORA_INVALID_INPUT.

The builder's aggregate setters are replaced by explicit entries:
