docs.title: C++
docs.text: The C++ headers under bindings/cpp are generated from the same bridge and follow the same renames in snake_case: fatoora::InvoiceSigner, fatoora::ComplianceCsid, fatoora::ProductionCsid, ZatcaClient::request_compliance_csid, CsrProperties::from_str, FinalizedInvoice::hash, InvoiceBuilder::set_flags, add_allowance and add_charge, ZatcaClient::new_ (formerly create), Adjustment::percent_of, supplied_amount and percentage, and omit_vat_rate. Enum parameters take fatoora::Environment, fatoora::VatCategory, fatoora::ClearanceMode and the other enum classes instead of integers. fatoora::Xml::validate(xml) and fatoora::Xml::validate_zatca(xml, options_json) take no Config, and the latter returns a fatoora::ZatcaValidationReport. The raw Diplomat headers do not validate enum values: passing a value that is not a declared enumerator is undefined behaviour.

docs.title: Migrate from 0.5 to 0.6: C# and .NET
docs.text:
The Fatoority NuGet package is an idiomatic C# facade in 0.6. Integer codes and Booleans become enums, class and method names follow the Rust core, scalar getters become read-only properties, amounts are decimal, optional text is string?, and native failures throw one exception class per error code. C# cannot overload a method with a property or by return type, so most changes are hard breaks with no deprecated alias: work through the compiler errors. The New factory methods, now Create, and a few renamed adjustment members keep [Obsolete] aliases until 0.7.

dotnet add package Fatoority --version 0.6.0

The package bundles its native libraries. Native objects still implement IDisposable; keep your using declarations.

docs.title: Upgrade checklist
docs.text:
1. Replace integer codes and Booleans with enums: ZatcaEnvironment.NonProduction for 0 (named to avoid clashing with System.Environment), InvoiceTypeKind.Tax and InvoiceSubType.Simplified for 0, 1, VatCategory.Standard for 1, ClearanceMode.Disabled for false. The enum values equal the old codes.
  2. Rename classes and methods (see the table below): Signer to InvoiceSigner, CsidCompliance/CsidProduction to ComplianceCsid/ProductionCsid, PostCsrForCcsid/PostCcsidForPcsid to RequestComplianceCsid/RequestProductionCsid, FromPropertiesStr to FromStr, HashBase64() to Hash.
  3. Drop the parentheses from scalar getters: address.City() becomes address.City, response.Outcome() becomes response.Outcome. Getters that return a disposable snapshot stay methods: invoice.Data(), invoice.Totals(), response.ValidationResults(), request.Body().
  4. Pass and read amounts as decimal (2m, 50m) instead of strings.
  5. Replace Text? handling with string?, and BindingErrorException with FfiException or one of its subclasses.
  6. Replace X.New(...) with X.Create(...), as ZatcaClient.Create and the credential classes already use. New still compiles with an obsolete warning.

docs.title: Build an invoice
Sign, validate and report
Errors
docs.text: BindingErrorException and the public BindingError are replaced by FatooraException > FfiException > one class per error code: InvalidInputException, ValidationException, ParseException, XmlException, CryptoException, IoException, NetworkException, UnauthorizedException, InternalException and ApiException. The exception exposes Code, Kind (FfiErrorKind) and DetailsJson directly and holds no native resources, so there is nothing to dispose. If you also import System.Xml or System.ComponentModel.DataAnnotations, qualify Fatoora.XmlException or Fatoora.ValidationException.

docs.title: Migrate from 0.5 to 0.6: JavaScript and TypeScript
docs.text:
In 0.6 the fatoority npm package takes the same shape as the Kotlin and C# packages: value getters become read-only properties (invoice.xml, address.city, totals.taxAmount, response.reportingStatus) and optional text is a plain string or null instead of a Text object. Amounts stay exact decimal strings. Integer codes become enums, class and method names follow the Rust core, failures throw typed errors, and local validation returns a plain report object. Except for new_ and the renamed adjustment members, the 0.5 names are removed, not deprecated, so TypeScript reports each one.

npm install fatoority@0.6.0

The WebAssembly module ships inside the package.

docs.title: Upgrade checklist
docs.text:
1. Drop the parentheses from value getters and the .value() from optional text: invoice.xml() becomes invoice.xml, address.district()?.value() becomes address.district. See Getters become properties. TypeScript flags every call ("This expression is not callable because it is a 'get' accessor"); in JavaScript the old call throws TypeError: ... is not a function.
  2. Replace integer codes and Booleans with enums: Environment.NonProduction for 0, InvoiceTypeKind.Tax and InvoiceSubType.Simplified for 0, 1, VatCategory.Standard for 1, AdjustmentKind.Charge for true. The enum discriminants equal the old codes.
  3. Rename classes and methods: Signer to InvoiceSigner, CsidCompliance/CsidProduction to ComplianceCsid/ProductionCsid, postCsrForCcsid/postCcsidForPcsid to requestComplianceCsid/requestProductionCsid, fromPropertiesStr to fromStr, hashBase64() to hash. The full table is below.
  4. Replace X.new_(...) with X.create(...). new_ still works and is marked @deprecated in the TypeScript declarations; it has no runtime warning.
  5. Drop the Config argument from Xml.validate and Xml.validateZatca, and read the report as an object instead of parsing JSON.
  6. Catch FatooraError (or a subclass such as InvalidInputError) instead of checking error.cause instanceof BindingError.

docs.title: Build an invoice
Sign, validate and report
Validation report
docs.text: From the package root, Xml.validateZatca(xml, options?) returns plain data with camelCase fields (isValid, isComplete, hasErrors, evaluatedAt, stages[].findings[]). Enumerated fields are variant-name strings such as 'Error' or 'BusinessRules'. options is { previousInvoiceHash, evaluatedAt } or the 0.5 options JSON string. The report can be passed to JSON.stringify directly. The snake_case JSON of 0.5 is still available from the native report on fatoority/raw, whose Xml.validateZatca(xml, optionsJson) returns a ZatcaValidationReport with toJson(); unlike the package root, it requires an explicit evaluated_at in the options.

docs.title: Response statuses
docs.text: reportingStatus, clearanceStatus, results.status, message.messageType and message.status are an enum (with Unknown for values this version does not recognise) or null, instead of a Text. The new reportingStatusRaw, clearanceStatusRaw, statusRaw and messageTypeRaw properties hold the exact wire value as a string or null.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: Every library failure throws a FatooraError subclass chosen by error code: InvalidInputError, ValidationError, ParseError, XmlError, CryptoError, IoError, NetworkError, UnauthorizedError, InternalError or ApiError. Each has code, kind, message and details (parsed JSON). error.cause is still the BindingError, so error.cause.code() keeps working: BindingError keeps its methods. TransportError, thrown for network and abort failures, now extends NetworkError.

docs.title: Getters become properties
docs.text:
Every zero-argument getter that returns a string, number, bigint, boolean, enum or optional text is a read-only property, on the package root and on fatoority/raw. This is the rule the Kotlin and C# packages follow.

0.5 0.6 invoice.xml(), invoice.qrCode(), invoice.hash() invoice.xml, invoice.qrCode, invoice.hash data.id(), data.invoiceCounter(), data.vatCategory() data.id, data.invoiceCounter, data.vatCategory address.city(), address.district()?.value() ?? null address.city, address.district totals.taxAmount(), totals.payableAmount() totals.taxAmount, totals.payableAmount response.httpStatus(), response.outcome(), response.reportingStatusRaw()?.value() response.httpStatus, response.outcome, response.reportingStatusRaw results.errorLen(), message.code()?.value() results.errorLen, message.code credentials.binarySecurityToken(), credentials.requestId()?.value() credentials.binarySecurityToken, credentials.requestId request.method(), request.url(), request.headersJson() request.method, request.url, request.headersJson paymentMeans.instructionNoteAt(i).value() paymentMeans.instructionNoteAt(i) (methods with arguments return string) InvoiceFlag.Export.bit() InvoiceFlag.Export.bit

These stay methods: members that take arguments (lineItem(i), identifier(i)), return another native object (invoice.data(), invoice.totals(), data.seller(), response.validationResults(), request.body()), convert or consume (toPem(), toXmlBase64(), intoXml(), withReason(...), omitVatRate(), build()), act (ensureAccepted()), and the collection members len() and isEmpty(). BindingError (the cause of a FatooraError) also keeps its methods.

This change has no deprecation period. A property cannot also be callable, and returning a callable string object would break ===, typeof and JSON.stringify. The TypeScript compiler finds every call site; in plain JavaScript, search for the getter names above. Assigning to a property throws a TypeError.

Optional text is now a string or null everywhere, including methods with arguments, so drop ?.value() and .value(). Text is still exported, only for the deprecated adjustment.percent(). Amounts stay exact decimal strings, such as '1.15', in both directions. JavaScript has no decimal type and number would round money, so pass the strings to a decimal library such as decimal.js for arithmetic.

docs.title: Renamed members with deprecated aliases
docs.text:
These members are renamed to the Rust core names. The 0.5 names still work, are marked @deprecated in the TypeScript declarations and are removed in 0.7.

0.5 0.6 Adjustment.percentage(base, percent) Adjustment.percentOf(base, percent) adjustment.withSuppliedAmount(amount) adjustment.suppliedAmount(amount) adjustment.percent() the adjustment.percentage property (percent() still returns the 0.5 Text) allowanceCharge.withoutVatRate(), vatBreakdown.withoutVatRate() omitVatRate()

(new_ deprecated) CsidCompliance, CsidProduction ComplianceCsid, ProductionCsid client.postCsrForCcsid(csr, otp), postCcsidForPcsid(ccsid) client.requestComplianceCsid(csr, otp), requestProductionCsid(ccsid) Signer InvoiceSigner CsrProperties.fromPropertiesStr(text) CsrProperties.fromStr(text) invoice.hashBase64() invoice.hash (signed.invoiceHash is the stored digest) builder.flags(mask), data.flagsRaw() builder.setFlags(mask), data.flags builder.setTaxExemption(category, rate, exemption) builder.addTaxExemption(category, rate, exemption) builder.addDocumentAdjustment(charge, adjustment, category, rate, exemption) builder.addAllowance(adjustment, category, rate, exemption) or addCharge(...) builder.setNote(language, text), setNoteWithoutLanguage(text) builder.addNote(language, text), with null for no language builder.setPaymentMeansCode(code) builder.addPaymentMeans(PaymentMeans.create(code, null)) builder.setAllowance(reason, amount), allowanceReason, invoiceLevelCharge, invoiceLevelDiscount addAllowance/addCharge with Adjustment.amount(amount).withReason(reason, null) charge.isCharge(), item.adjustmentIsCharge(i) charge.kind, item.adjustmentKind(i) returning AdjustmentKind config.env(), data.vatCategory(), ... returning numbers config.env, data.vatCategory, ... holding the enums Xml.validate(config, xml) Xml.validate(xml) Xml.validateZatca(config, xml, optionsJson) returning JSON text Xml.validateZatca(xml, options) returning a plain report

Credential requestId is null when the credentials have no request ID. Boolean getters such as PaymentMeans.hasAccount and VatBreakdown.hasVatRate are now true/false instead of 1/0.

Each enum also has a string-literal union type named with a Value suffix (EnvironmentValue, VatCategoryValue, SeverityValue, ...), matching the enum's .value, for typing plain data such as the validation report.

docs.title: Migrate from 0.5 to 0.6: Kotlin and Java
docs.text:
The com.fatoora API changes in four ways in 0.6: integer codes and Booleans become enums, class and method names follow the Rust core, value getters become Kotlin properties with BigDecimal amounts, and native failures throw one BindingException subclass per error code. The 0.5 getter functions, String amount overloads, Boolean coroutine overloads and the renamed adjustment members remain as @Deprecated members with ReplaceWith hints until 0.7. Other renamed classes and methods do not, so the compiler reports each one.

Gradle (Kotlin DSL)Maven 
dependencies {
    implementation("com.fatoority:fatoority:0.6.0")
    // Android: com.fatoority:fatoority-android:0.6.0
}

<dependency>
  <groupId>com.fatoority</groupId>
  <artifactId>fatoority</artifactId>
  <version>0.6.0</version>
</dependency>

The JAR and AAR bundle their native libraries.

docs.title: Upgrade checklist
docs.text:
1. Replace integer codes and Booleans with enums: Environment.NonProduction for 0, InvoiceTypeKind.Tax and InvoiceSubType.Simplified for 0, 1, VatCategory.Standard for 1, ClearanceMode.Disabled for false. The enum discriminants equal the old codes.
  2. Rename classes and methods (see the table below): Signer to InvoiceSigner, CsidCompliance/CsidProduction to ComplianceCsid/ProductionCsid, postCsrForCcsid/postCcsidForPcsid to requestComplianceCsid/requestProductionCsid (and their *Async helpers), fromPropertiesStr to fromStr, hashBase64() to hash.
  3. Drop the Config argument from Xml.validate and Xml.validateZatca, and read the returned ZatcaValidationReport instead of parsing JSON.
  4. Build once and work through the deprecation warnings. In Kotlin, address.city() becomes address.city; in Java it becomes address.getCity(). Optional text is a String? instead of a closeable Text. Pass BigDecimal amounts instead of strings.
  5. Kotlin only: isValid(), isComplete(), hasErrors(), hasVatRate() and the other is*/has* getters are properties with no deprecated function (it would clash with the Java getter), so drop the parentheses. Java callers keep report.isValid().

docs.title: Build an invoice
Sign, validate and report
Errors
docs.text: BindingException is now open and gains kind: ErrorKind?. Native failures throw the subclass for their code: InvalidInputException, ValidationException, ParseException, XmlException, CryptoException, IoException, NetworkException, UnauthorizedException, InternalException or ApiException. Existing catch (BindingException) blocks keep catching everything; add narrower catch clauses before it where you handle a specific failure.

Credential requestId is null when the credentials have no request ID.

docs.title: Migrate from 0.5 to 0.6: Python
docs.text:
The fatoority package (imported as fatoora) adopts the core names with a Pythonic surface. Most renamed 0.5 names still work in 0.6 and emit a DeprecationWarning naming their replacement; 0.7 removed them. A few changes are hard breaks, listed first below.

Upgrading to 0.7

0.7 removed every name this page marks as deprecated, so on 0.7 use the 0.6 replacement. Migrate from 0.6 to 0.7 lists the removed names.

pip install "fatoority==0.6.0"

The wheel bundles its native library, so no separate native upgrade is needed.

docs.title: Upgrade checklist
docs.text:
1. Drop the parentheses from getters: invoice.id() becomes invoice.id, response.reporting_status() becomes response.reporting_status. Calling a property fails like calling its value (TypeError: 'str' object is not callable).
  2. Pass the arguments that 0.5.1 warned about by keyword: everything after name in set_seller/set_buyer, language in add_note, every CsrProperties field, and the clearance flag and accept_language in report_simplified_invoice and clear_standard_invoice. Positional use now raises TypeError.
  3. Expect datetime/date values where 0.5 returned text: issue_datetime, signing_time and ZatcaReport.evaluated_at are timezone-aware UTC datetimes; issue_date, the delivery dates and OriginalInvoiceRef.issue_date are datetime.dates.
  4. Expect tuples where 0.5 returned lists: party.identifiers and payment_means.instruction_notes.
  5. Run your tests with python -W error::DeprecationWarning (or pytest's filterwarnings = ["error::DeprecationWarning"]) and replace each name the warnings point at.

The Python reference lists the hard breaks, and Migrate from 0.6 to 0.7 lists every renamed name with its replacement.

docs.title: Build an invoice
docs.text:
InvoiceBuilder(...) replaces InvoiceBuilder.new(...) and takes the header fields as keywords. Setters return the builder, so calls chain. Dates and UUIDs accept datetime, date and uuid.UUID values as well as strings; a naive datetime raises ValueError. Address, PaymentMeans, Party, Adjustment and the other invoice values are frozen dataclasses built with their constructors.

0.50.6 
from pathlib import Path
from fatoora import InvoiceBuilder, InvoiceSubType, InvoiceTypeKind, VatCategory

builder = InvoiceBuilder.new(InvoiceTypeKind.TAX, InvoiceSubType.SIMPLIFIED)
builder.set_id("INV-1001")
builder.set_uuid("8e6000cf-1a98-4174-b3e7-b5d5954bc10d")
builder.set_issue_datetime("2026-10-26T09:00:00Z")
builder.set_currency("SAR")
builder.set_previous_invoice_hash(
    "NWZlY2ViNjZmZmM4NmYzOGQ5NTI3ODZjNmQ2OTZjNzljMmRiYzIzOWRkNGU5MWI0NjcyOWQ3M2EyN2ZiNTdlOQ=="
)
builder.set_invoice_counter(1)
builder.set_payment_means_code("10")
builder.set_vat_category(VatCategory.STANDARD)
builder.set_seller(
    name="Example Store", country_code="SA", city="Riyadh",
    street="King Fahd Road", building_number="1234", postal_code="12222",
    district="Olaya", additional_number="5678", vat_id="399999999900003",
    other_id="7003339333", other_id_scheme="CRN",
)
builder.add_line_item(
    description="Notebook", quantity="2", unit_code="PCE", unit_price="50",
    vat_rate="15", vat_category=VatCategory.STANDARD,
)
invoice = builder.build()
Path("invoice.xml").write_text(invoice.to_xml(), encoding="utf-8")
totals = invoice.totals()
print(f"Payable: {totals.payable_amount} SAR")

from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path
from uuid import UUID
from fatoora import (Address, InvoiceBuilder, InvoiceSubType, InvoiceTypeKind,
                     PaymentMeans, VatCategory)

seller_address = Address(
    "SA", "Riyadh", "King Fahd Road", "1234", "12222",
    additional_number="5678", district="Olaya",
)
invoice = (
    InvoiceBuilder(
        InvoiceTypeKind.TAX, InvoiceSubType.SIMPLIFIED,
        id="INV-1001",
        uuid=UUID("8e6000cf-1a98-4174-b3e7-b5d5954bc10d"),
        issue_datetime=datetime(2026, 10, 26, 9, 0, tzinfo=timezone.utc),
        currency="SAR",
        previous_invoice_hash="NWZlY2ViNjZmZmM4NmYzOGQ5NTI3ODZjNmQ2OTZjNzljMmRiYzIzOWRkNGU5MWI0NjcyOWQ3M2EyN2ZiNTdlOQ==",
        invoice_counter=1,
        vat_category=VatCategory.STANDARD,
    )
    .set_seller("Example Store", address=seller_address, vat_id="399999999900003",
                other_id="7003339333", other_id_scheme="CRN")
    .add_payment_means(PaymentMeans("10"))
    .add_line_item(description="Notebook", quantity="2", unit_code="PCE", unit_price="50",
                   vat_rate="15", vat_category=VatCategory.STANDARD)
    .build()
)
Path("invoice.xml").write_text(invoice.xml, encoding="utf-8")
totals = invoice.totals
print(f"Payable: {totals.payable_amount} SAR")

set_payment_means_code(code) still works with a warning, but it now appends a payment means instead of changing the code of an existing one.

docs.title: Document allowances and charges
docs.text:
add_allowance and add_charge append one entry each, in the VAT category and at the rate you pass. The 0.5 aggregate setters (set_allowance, invoice_level_discount, invoice_level_charge, allowance_reason) are deprecated. They still produce one allowance and one charge in the document VAT category, applied by build(), which raises ValueError if that category's lines have more than one VAT rate or if they are combined with add_allowance, add_charge or add_adjustment.

0.50.6 
builder.set_vat_category(VatCategory.STANDARD)
builder.invoice_level_discount("10")
builder.allowance_reason("Loyalty discount")

from fatoora import Adjustment, VatCategory

builder.add_allowance(
    Adjustment("10", reason="Loyalty discount"), VatCategory.STANDARD, "15",
)

Adjustment is the one allowance and charge model, for lines, for the document and for the values read back from invoice.adjustments. Adjustment.amount(v) becomes Adjustment(v), Adjustment.percentage(base, percent) becomes Adjustment.percent_of(base, percent), .value becomes .amount and .percent becomes .percentage. AllowanceCharge(...) and add_document_adjustment(charge, ...) are deprecated.

docs.title: Request credentials and report an invoice
docs.text:
ComplianceCsid and ProductionCsid replace CsidCompliance and CsidProduction, and are built with their constructors: ProductionCsid(env, token=..., secret=..., request_id=None) replaces ProductionCsid.new(env, token, secret, request_id) (the arguments after env are keyword-only, so their order no longer matters). request_compliance_csid and request_production_csid replace post_csr_for_ccsid and post_ccsid_for_pcsid. The Clearance-Status header is a ClearanceMode, as in the other languages: clearance=ClearanceMode.DISABLED replaces clearance_status=False. Everything is importable from the fatoora package root.

0.50.6 
from pathlib import Path
import os
from fatoora.api import CsidProduction, ZatcaClient
from fatoora.config import Config, Environment
from fatoora.invoice import parse_signed_invoice_xml

environment = Environment.NON_PRODUCTION
token = os.environ["ZATCA_TOKEN"]
secret = os.environ["ZATCA_SECRET"]
with Config(environment) as config, ZatcaClient(config) as client:
    with CsidProduction.new(environment, token, secret, None) as credentials:
        with parse_signed_invoice_xml(Path("signed.xml").read_text(encoding="utf-8")) as invoice:
            with client.report_simplified_invoice(invoice, credentials, clearance_status=False, accept_language="en") as response:
                response.ensure_accepted()
                print("Invoice reporting accepted:", response.reporting_status())

import os
from fatoora import (ClearanceMode, Config, Environment, ProductionCsid, SignedInvoice,
                     ZatcaClient)

environment = Environment.NON_PRODUCTION
token = os.environ["ZATCA_TOKEN"]
secret = os.environ["ZATCA_SECRET"]
with Config(environment) as config, ZatcaClient(config, timeout=30) as client:
    with ProductionCsid(environment, token=token, secret=secret) as credentials:
        with SignedInvoice.from_file("signed.xml") as invoice:
            with client.report_simplified_invoice(
                invoice, credentials, clearance=ClearanceMode.DISABLED, accept_language="en"
            ) as response:
                response.ensure_accepted()
                print("Invoice reporting accepted:", response.reporting_status)

timeout is new and optional: seconds (int/float) or a datetime.timedelta bounding each request. A request that exceeds it raises NetworkError; the default None applies no timeout. clearance_status=False and ProductionCsid.new(...) keep working with a DeprecationWarning. reporting_status is a ReportingStatus (and clearance_status a ClearanceStatus): str enums, so comparing with "REPORTED" and printing still work. ComplianceCsid.request_id and ProductionCsid.request_id are None instead of "" when absent.

docs.title: Validate and hash an invoice
docs.text:
Validation no longer takes a Config. validate_zatca returns a frozen ZatcaReport instead of a dictionary; report.to_dict() returns the 0.5 dictionary shape and report.to_json() the JSON text.

0.50.6 
from pathlib import Path
from fatoora import invoice_hash_base64_from_xml_str
from fatoora.config import Config, Environment
from fatoora.validation import validate_xml_invoice_from_str, validate_zatca_invoice_from_str

xml = Path("invoice.xml").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
with Config(Environment.NON_PRODUCTION) as config:
    validate_xml_invoice_from_str(config, xml)
    report = validate_zatca_invoice_from_str(
        config, xml, previous_invoice_hash=Path("previous-hash.txt").read_text().strip(),
    )
    if not report["is_valid"]:
        raise SystemExit(1)
next_previous_hash = invoice_hash_base64_from_xml_str(xml)

from pathlib import Path
from fatoora import hash_xml, validate_xml, validate_zatca

xml = Path("invoice.xml").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
validate_xml(xml)
report = validate_zatca(
    xml, previous_invoice_hash=Path("previous-hash.txt").read_text().strip(),
)
for finding in report.findings:
    print(finding.severity.value, finding.code, finding.message)
if not report.is_valid:
    raise SystemExit(1)
next_previous_hash = hash_xml(xml)

On a parsed or built invoice, hash() replaces hash_base64(); signed.invoice_hash is the hash stored in the signature. SignedInvoice.from_xml and from_file (and the same on FinalizedInvoice) replace the parse_*_invoice_xml[_file] functions, and the xml property replaces to_xml()/into_xml().

docs.title: Read a ZATCA response
docs.text:
0.50.6 
with response.validation_results() as results:
    summary = {
        "http_status": response.http_status(),
        "outcome": response.outcome().name,
        "reporting_status": response.reporting_status(),
        "validation_status": results.status(),
        "warnings": [(m.code(), m.message()) for m in results.warning_messages()],
    }

with response.validation_results as results:
    summary = {
        "http_status": response.http_status,
        "outcome": response.outcome.name,
        "reporting_status": response.reporting_status,
        "validation_status": results.status,
        "warnings": [(m.code, m.message) for m in results.warning_messages],
    }

Validation statuses and message types are str enums too (ValidationStatus.PASS, MessageType.WARNING). A status this version does not recognize keeps the exact text ZATCA sent, in a value whose name is "OTHER".

docs.title: Migrate from 0.5 to 0.6: Rust
docs.text:
This page covers the fatoora-core crate. The language packages have their own pages: Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, Kotlin/Java, C#/.NET and C/C++. The overview lists what changed in every language.

Update Cargo.toml:

[dependencies]
fatoora-core = "0.6.0"

0.6 renames items for consistency, replaces strings and Booleans with typed values, and makes the fields of invoice value types private. Each change below is one of two kinds:

  • Deprecated: in 0.6 the old name still compiles, with a deprecation warning, and forwards to the new one. 0.7 removed it.
  • Breaking: the old form no longer compiles. The type, signature or field changed in place, so there is no deprecation period.

A practical order of work: fix the breaking errors until the project compiles, then run cargo build (or cargo clippy) and work through the deprecated warnings, each of which names its replacement. Adding #![deny(deprecated)] to your crate root while you migrate turns the remaining old names into errors.

Upgrading to 0.7

0.7 removed every item marked Deprecated on this page, so on 0.7 use the replacement in the 0.6 column. Migrate from 0.6 to 0.7 lists the removed items.

The full list of changes, including additions, is in the changelog.

docs.title: Changed items
docs.text: Paths are relative to fatoora_core. Status is Deprecated (compiles with a warning in 0.6, removed in 0.7) or Breaking (fails to compile).

AdjustmentKind::from_charge_indicator(flag) converts a 0.5 charge Boolean and kind.is_charge() reads one back.

The deprecated invoice_level_discount, invoice_level_charge and allowance_reason keep their 0.5 behaviour: each call replaces a single aggregate entry in the document VAT category, with the rate taken from the first line in that category. allowance and charge append one entry per call with the VAT category and rate you pass, so a migrated invoice gets the same totals only if you pass that category and rate. Likewise, payment_means_code changes the code of the first payment means, while payment_means appends one.

docs.title: Validation and hashing
docs.text:
0.5 0.6 Status invoice::validation::validate_xml_invoice_from_str(xml, &config) Validator::new().validate_xml(xml) Deprecated invoice::validation::validate_xml_invoice_report_from_str(xml, &config) Validator::new().validate_xml_report(xml) Deprecated invoice::validation::validate_zatca_invoice_from_str(xml, &config, &options) Validator::new().validate_zatca(xml, &options) Deprecated invoice::sign::invoice_hash_base64_from_xml_str(xml) -> Result<String, _> invoice::hash_xml(xml) -> Result<InvoiceHash, _> Deprecated FinalizedInvoice::hash_base64() -> Result<String, SigningError> FinalizedInvoice::hash() -> Result<InvoiceHash, SigningError> Deprecated SignedInvoice::hash_base64() -> Result<String, SigningError> SignedInvoice::hash() -> Result<InvoiceHash, SigningError> Deprecated ZatcaValidationOptions { previous_invoice_hash: Option<String>, .. } previous_invoice_hash: Option<InvoiceHash> Breaking

Validation never depended on the environment, so Validator takes no Config. The deprecated functions ignore their Config argument, and invoice_hash_base64_from_xml_str and the deprecated hash_base64 methods still return a String.

Set previous_invoice_hash from an InvoiceHash: the value returned by hash() or hash_xml, data.previous_invoice_hash().clone(), or text.parse()?. Parsing trims surrounding whitespace and rejects blank text; validate_zatca still checks the digest format. Deserialized options (for example from JSON) go through the same parsing.

docs.title: Behaviour and data format changes
docs.text:
These compile unchanged but can change what your program sees:

  • InvoiceBuilder::build no longer reports Empty or InvalidFormat issues for the UUID, issue date-time, currency or previous invoice hash. An invalid value now fails earlier, where you parse it into its typed wrapper; build only reports these four fields as Missing.
  • A DocumentAdjustment whose amount calculation is invalid is reported with the other adjustment checks in build, after missing or invalid fields, instead of before them.
  • Serialized AllowanceCharge and LineAdjustment values, and therefore serialized InvoiceData and LineItem values, use a "kind" field with the values "allowance"/"charge" instead of the Boolean "charge" field. JSON written by 0.5 is still accepted on read: a legacy "charge": true reads as a charge and "charge": false as an allowance. Serialization writes only "kind", so data saved again is in the 0.6 format. Input with both fields is accepted when they agree and rejected when they conflict. The other serde field names are unchanged.
  • The JSON of ZATCA responses and the InvoiceOutcome returned by ValidationResponse::outcome() are unchanged.

Request CSIDs and report an invoice
Read response statuses
Validate and hash an invoice
Migrate from 0.6 to 0.7
docs.text:
0.7 is a breaking release. Most of it removes the names that 0.6 kept as deprecated aliases. Each one forwarded to a replacement that already exists in 0.6, so you can migrate on 0.6 first: build against 0.6 with deprecation warnings turned into errors, replace every name the warnings point at, and then upgrade. Each warning names its replacement.

The other changes have no deprecation step in 0.6. Make them while upgrading; each language page lists them after the removed names.

Language Package Migration page Rust fatoora-core = "0.7.0" Rust Python pip install "fatoority==0.7.0" Python JavaScript / TypeScript fatoority@0.7.0 on npm JavaScript / TypeScript Kotlin / Java com.fatoority:fatoority:0.7.0 Kotlin / Java C# / .NET Fatoority 0.7.0 C# / .NET C / C++ fatoora.h and the C++ headers from the 0.7.0 release assets C / C++

docs.title: Changes by language
docs.text:
A dash means the language is unaffected.

Change Rust Python JavaScript / TypeScript Kotlin / Java C# / .NET C / C++ Names deprecated in 0.6 are removed Yes Yes Yes Yes Yes - (none were deprecated) One error hierarchy - FfiError → FatooraError, FfiErrorKind → ErrorKind ErrorCode → ErrorKind, TransportError → NetworkError BindingException → FatooraException FfiException → FatooraException, FfiErrorKind → ErrorKind - Client timeout Zero is ZatcaError::InvalidTimeout - (ValueError, as in 0.6) - (no client timeout) Duration instead of Long ms TimeSpan instead of uint ms Zero returns FATOORA_INVALID_INPUT Clearance mode - clearance=ClearanceMode... required ClearanceMode required, parameter clearanceMode Boolean coroutine overloads removed - - Text handle removed; strings are plain or nullable - - Text export removed com.fatoora.Text removed Fatoora.Text removed C++ fatoora::Text removed Binary output - - Bytes.asSlice() → Bytes.toUint8Array(), Uint8Array inputs Bytes.asSlice() → Bytes.toByteArray() Bytes.AsSlice() → Bytes.ToArray() - InvoiceData stores document-level allowances and charges only as entries Yes - - - - - Supported runtimes - Python 3.10 or newer - - - - New features - AsyncZatcaClient - - - -

The CLI is unaffected. The bindings are now generated with Diplomat 0.17; that changes only the generated low-level layers listed above.

If you are still on 0.5, follow Migrate from 0.5 to 0.6 first, using the 0.6 replacement for every item marked deprecated there.

The full list of changes is in the changelog.

docs.title: Migrate from 0.6 to 0.7: C and C++
docs.text:
This page covers the C facade (fatoora.h), the generated C headers and the C++ headers. The overview lists the other languages.

Take fatoora.h, fatoora.c, the generated headers and the shared library from the same 0.7.0 release assets; mixing 0.6 headers with a 0.7 library, or the reverse, is not supported. 0.6 deprecated nothing in C or C++, so there are no removed aliases.

docs.title: C facade
docs.text: Every fatoora.h function keeps its 0.6 signature and behavior, with one exception.

docs.title: Zero timeout is invalid input
docs.text: fatoora_zatca_client_with_timeout(config, 0, &client, &error) returns FATOORA_INVALID_INPUT (details type invalid_timeout) instead of FATOORA_INTERNAL. Use fatoora_zatca_client_new for no client-side timeout.

docs.title: C++ strings replace Text
docs.text:
The fatoora::Text class and its header are removed. Every getter that returned a Text returns a string:

  • Optional text returns std::optional<std::string> and no longer fails: std::nullopt means absent. This covers getters such as Address::district(), Adjustment::reason(), ComplianceCsid::request_id() and the ValidationResponse *_raw() statuses.
  • ValidationResponse::cleared_invoice_xml() and SignedInvoice::zatca_key_signature() return diplomat::result<std::string, ...> and fail when the value is absent. Check cleared_invoice_xml_present() or zatca_key_signature_present() first.
-std::unique_ptr<fatoora::Text> district = address->district().ok().value();
-if (district) {
-    std::string text = district->value().ok().value();
-}
+std::optional<std::string> district = address->district();
+if (district) {
+    std::string text = *district;
+}

-std::unique_ptr<fatoora::Text> xml = response->cleared_invoice_xml().ok().value();
-if (xml) {
-    save(xml->value().ok().value());
-}
+if (response->cleared_invoice_xml_present()) {
+    save(response->cleared_invoice_xml().ok().value());
+}

A _write(W&) overload of each getter writes into your own buffer.

docs.title: Generated C headers
docs.text: Code that calls the generated bindings/c/generated functions directly, rather than fatoora.h, sees the same change: Text.h is removed, and each optional text getter takes a DiplomatWrite * and returns a result whose is_ok is false when the value is absent. The facade handles this for you.

docs.title: Migrate from 0.6 to 0.7: C# and .NET
docs.text:
This page covers the Fatoority NuGet package. The overview lists the other languages.

dotnet add package Fatoority --version 0.7.0

0.7 removes every member that 0.6 marked [Obsolete]. Each replacement below already exists in 0.6, so the simplest path is to turn obsolete warnings into errors while still on 0.6, fix them, and then upgrade:

<PropertyGroup>
  <WarningsAsErrors>$(WarningsAsErrors);CS0618</WarningsAsErrors>
</PropertyGroup>

On 0.7 the same calls fail with CS0117 (no static member New) or CS1061 (no instance member).

docs.title: New factory methods
docs.text:
The static New factory on each class below is removed. Call Create with the same arguments.

Removed Use instead Address.New(...) Address.Create(...) AllowanceCharge.New(...) AllowanceCharge.Create(...) Config.New(env) Config.Create(env) CsrProperties.New(...) CsrProperties.Create(...) InvoiceBuilder.New(...) InvoiceBuilder.Create(...) InvoiceLineItem.New(...) InvoiceLineItem.Create(...) LineItemBuilder.New() LineItemBuilder.Create() OriginalInvoiceRef.New(...) OriginalInvoiceRef.Create(...) PaymentMeans.New(code, instruction) PaymentMeans.Create(code, instruction) TaxExemption.New(code, reason) TaxExemption.Create(code, reason) VatBreakdown.New(...) VatBreakdown.Create(...)

ZatcaClient, ComplianceCsid and ProductionCsid already used Create in 0.5 and are unchanged.

docs.title: Adjustments and VAT rates
docs.text: Removed Use instead adjustment.WithSuppliedAmount(amount) adjustment.SuppliedAmount(amount) adjustment.Percent (property) adjustment.Percentage (property) allowanceCharge.WithoutVatRate() allowanceCharge.OmitVatRate() vatBreakdown.WithoutVatRate() vatBreakdown.OmitVatRate()

docs.title: Changed signatures
docs.text: These changes have no 0.6 equivalent to migrate to first; update the call when you upgrade.

docs.title: Client timeout
docs.text:
ZatcaClient.WithTimeout takes a TimeSpan instead of a uint millisecond count. The timeout is rounded up to whole milliseconds; zero, negative (including Timeout.InfiniteTimeSpan) and over-uint.MaxValue-millisecond values throw ArgumentOutOfRangeException. Use ZatcaClient.Create(config) for no client-side timeout.

0.6 0.7 ZatcaClient.WithTimeout(config, 30_000) ZatcaClient.WithTimeout(config, TimeSpan.FromSeconds(30))

docs.title: Binary output
docs.text:
Bytes.AsSlice(), which returned a disposable DiplomatBorrowedSpan<byte> view, is replaced by Bytes.ToArray(), which returns a new byte[]. The array stays valid after the Bytes owner is disposed, so there is no view to dispose and no WithSpan() read. The Fatoora.Diplomat byte-view types are no longer public.

0.6 0.7 using var view = bytes.AsSlice(); byte[] der = view.Clone(); byte[] der = bytes.ToArray(); view.WithSpan(span => ...) ReadOnlySpan<byte> span = bytes.ToArray();

docs.title: Text class
docs.text: The Fatoora.Text class is removed. No public member returned it in 0.6: optional text was already string?.

docs.title: Error classes
docs.text:
0.7 gives every language the same error hierarchy: a base FatooraException, one ErrorKind enum, and one subclass per kind named <Kind>Exception. See errors and diagnostics. These names change in 0.7 with no deprecated alias in 0.6, so update them while upgrading.

0.6 0.7 FfiException FatooraException, which now carries Code, Kind and DetailsJson FfiErrorKind ErrorKind (same members and values) FfiException.Create(code, message, detailsJson) FatooraException.FromCode(code, message, detailsJson) new InvalidInputException(message, code, detailsJson) (any subclass) new InvalidInputException(message, detailsJson); the code comes from the class new FatooraException(message), new FatooraException(message, inner) new FatooraException(message, code, detailsJson)

The subclasses (InvalidInputException, ..., ApiException) keep their names. A catch (FfiException error) becomes catch (FatooraException error).

docs.title: Example
Migrate from 0.6 to 0.7: JavaScript and TypeScript
docs.text:
This page covers the fatoority npm package and its fatoority/raw entry point. The overview lists the other languages.

npm install fatoority@0.7.0

0.7 removes every name marked @deprecated in the 0.6 TypeScript declarations. Each replacement below already exists in 0.6, so you can switch to it first and then upgrade. TypeScript reports each removed name as a missing property; in JavaScript a call throws TypeError: ... is not a function.

docs.title: new_ constructors
docs.text:
The generated new_ name of every Rust new constructor is removed from the package root and from fatoority/raw. Call create with the same arguments.

Removed Use instead Address.new_(...) Address.create(...) AllowanceCharge.new_(...) AllowanceCharge.create(...) ComplianceCsid.new_(...) ComplianceCsid.create(...) Config.new_(env) Config.create(env) CsrProperties.new_(...) CsrProperties.create(...) InvoiceBuilder.new_(...) InvoiceBuilder.create(...) InvoiceLineItem.new_(...) InvoiceLineItem.create(...) LineItemBuilder.new_() LineItemBuilder.create() OriginalInvoiceRef.new_(...) OriginalInvoiceRef.create(...) PaymentMeans.new_(code, instruction) PaymentMeans.create(code, instruction) ProductionCsid.new_(...) ProductionCsid.create(...) TaxExemption.new_(code, reason) TaxExemption.create(code, reason) VatBreakdown.new_(...) VatBreakdown.create(...) ZatcaClient.new_(config) (fatoority/raw) ZatcaClient.create(config) (fatoority/raw), or new ZatcaClient(config) from the package root

docs.title: Adjustments and VAT breakdowns
docs.text:
Removed Use instead Adjustment.percentage(base, percent) Adjustment.percentOf(base, percent) adjustment.withSuppliedAmount(value) adjustment.suppliedAmount(value) adjustment.percent() (returned Text \| null) adjustment.percentage property (string \| null) allowanceCharge.withoutVatRate() allowanceCharge.omitVatRate() vatBreakdown.withoutVatRate() vatBreakdown.omitVatRate()

adjustment.percentage is a read-only property of an instance, while Adjustment.percentage(...) was a static factory, so code that reads the property needs no change.

docs.title: Text class
docs.text: Text is no longer exported from the package root or from fatoority/raw. No member returned it in 0.6: optional text was already string | null, so only code that imported the class itself, for example for instanceof checks, needs a change.

docs.title: Clearance mode is required and must be a ClearanceMode
docs.text:
ZatcaClient.reportSimplifiedInvoice and ZatcaClient.clearStandardInvoice no longer accept a boolean or the variant name ('Enabled'/'Disabled') for the Clearance-Status header, and the argument no longer has a default (false for reporting, true for clearance). Pass ClearanceMode.Disabled or ClearanceMode.Enabled, as every other binding does. Any other value, including an omitted argument, rejects with a TypeError. The parameter is now named clearanceMode, like the fatoority/raw prepare* methods, so it is not confused with response.clearanceStatus.

0.6 0.7 client.reportSimplifiedInvoice(invoice, credentials) client.reportSimplifiedInvoice(invoice, credentials, ClearanceMode.Disabled) client.reportSimplifiedInvoice(invoice, credentials, false, ...) client.reportSimplifiedInvoice(invoice, credentials, ClearanceMode.Disabled, ...) client.clearStandardInvoice(invoice, credentials) client.clearStandardInvoice(invoice, credentials, ClearanceMode.Enabled) client.clearStandardInvoice(invoice, credentials, true, ...) client.clearStandardInvoice(invoice, credentials, ClearanceMode.Enabled, ...) 'Enabled' / 'Disabled' ClearanceMode.Enabled / ClearanceMode.Disabled ClearanceModeInput type ClearanceMode

docs.title: Binary data is a Uint8Array
docs.text:
Bytes.asSlice(), which returned a copied number[], is replaced by Bytes.toUint8Array(), which returns a new Uint8Array that stays valid after its owner is collected. The rename applies to the package root and to fatoority/raw, and matches C# Bytes.ToArray(). Byte arguments (SigningKey.fromDer, Csr.fromDer, InvoiceSigner.fromDer and the prepared requests' decode) are typed to accept a Uint8Array, including a Node.js Buffer, as well as an array of byte numbers, so the [...buffer] spread is no longer needed.

0.6 0.7 bytes.asSlice() (number[]) bytes.toUint8Array() (Uint8Array) Uint8Array.from(bytes.asSlice()) bytes.toUint8Array() Buffer.from(request.body().asSlice()) Buffer.from(request.body().toUint8Array()) SigningKey.fromDer([...der]) SigningKey.fromDer(der) request.decode(status, [...body]) request.decode(status, body)

toUint8Array() has no 0.6 alias, so rename the calls while upgrading. Code that needs a plain array can call Array.from(bytes.toUint8Array()).

docs.title: Error classes
docs.text:
0.7 gives every language the same error hierarchy: a base FatooraError, one ErrorKind enum, and one subclass per kind named <Kind>Error. See errors and diagnostics. These names change in 0.7 with no deprecated alias in 0.6, so update them while upgrading.

0.6 0.7 ErrorCode (names to numbers) ErrorKind (names to names: ErrorKind.Network === 'Network'); compare error.kind with it. error.code is still the number errorClassForCode(code) FatooraError.fromCode(code, message, { details }) creates the error TransportError NetworkError, with the host error in cause transportError.httpStatus error.details.http_status; details.type is 'api_response_read' when a response arrived and 'network' when fetch failed

FatooraError, kind and the subclasses (InvalidInputError, ..., ApiError) are unchanged, so instanceof NetworkError checks keep working. The TypeScript type ErrorKind is unchanged.

// 0.6
if (error instanceof TransportError && error.httpStatus) retryLater();
if (error.code === ErrorCode.Unauthorized) renewCredentials();

// 0.7
if (error instanceof NetworkError && error.details.http_status) retryLater();
if (error.kind === ErrorKind.Unauthorized) renewCredentials();

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
// 0.6, with @deprecated warnings
import { Adjustment, Config, Environment, LineItemBuilder } from 'fatoority';

const config = Config.new_(Environment.NonProduction);
const line = LineItemBuilder.new_();
const rebate = Adjustment.percentage('250', '10').withSuppliedAmount('25');
const percent: string | undefined = rebate.percent()?.value();

// 0.7
import { Adjustment, Config, Environment, LineItemBuilder } from 'fatoority';

const config = Config.create(Environment.NonProduction);
const line = LineItemBuilder.create();
const rebate = Adjustment.percentOf('250', '10').suppliedAmount('25');
const percent: string | null = rebate.percentage;

docs.title: Migrate from 0.6 to 0.7: Kotlin and Java
docs.text:
This page covers the com.fatoority:fatoority and com.fatoority:fatoority-android packages. The overview lists the other languages.

Gradle (Kotlin DSL)Maven 
dependencies {
    implementation("com.fatoority:fatoority:0.7.0")
    // Android: com.fatoority:fatoority-android:0.7.0
}

<dependency>
  <groupId>com.fatoority</groupId>
  <artifactId>fatoority</artifactId>
  <version>0.7.0</version>
</dependency>

0.7 removes every @Deprecated member of the com.fatoora facade. Each replacement below already exists in 0.6, so the simplest path is to compile against 0.6 with warnings as errors (allWarningsAsErrors = true in Kotlin, -Xlint:deprecation -Werror in Java), apply each ReplaceWith hint, and then bump the version.

docs.text:
Every method that takes a quantity, price, rate or amount keeps only its java.math.BigDecimal overload. Wrap string literals in BigDecimal("...") (Java: new BigDecimal("...")); never go through Double.

docs.title: Boolean coroutine overloads
docs.text:
Removed Use instead client.reportSimplifiedInvoiceAsync(invoice, credentials, clearanceStatus: Boolean, acceptLanguage) client.reportSimplifiedInvoiceAsync(invoice, credentials, ClearanceMode.Enabled or ClearanceMode.Disabled, acceptLanguage) client.clearStandardInvoiceAsync(invoice, credentials, clearanceStatus: Boolean, acceptLanguage) client.clearStandardInvoiceAsync(invoice, credentials, ClearanceMode.Enabled or ClearanceMode.Disabled, acceptLanguage)

true maps to ClearanceMode.Enabled and false to ClearanceMode.Disabled, as in the blocking methods.

docs.title: Getter functions
docs.text:
The 0.5-style getter functions are gone; read the property of the same name instead. In Kotlin drop the parentheses (address.city() becomes address.city); in Java call the generated getter (address.getCity()). is* and has* getters had no deprecated function and are unchanged.

The property types differ from the removed functions in two ways:

  • Getters marked "was Text?" returned a closeable Text handle. The property is a nullable String, or a nullable BigDecimal for amounts (baseAmount, percentage, itemGrossPrice, itemPriceDiscount, itemPriceBaseQuantity, taxCurrencyAmount). Drop the .use { it.value() }.
  • Getters marked "was String" returned decimal text. The property is a BigDecimal; call toPlainString() where you need the text, and compare with compareTo, since returned values are normalized (10.50 reads back as 10.5).

docs.title: Text class
docs.text:
com.fatoora.Text is removed, along with the internal com.fatoora.raw.Text. Only the removed getter functions returned it; every optional text property is already a String? in 0.6, so replace text.value or text.value() with the string itself and drop the use { } block.

Code that calls the low-level com.fatoora.raw classes directly gets a String or String? wherever they returned Text. Their ValidationResponse.clearedInvoiceXml() and SignedInvoice.zatcaKeySignature() fail when the value is absent: check clearedInvoiceXmlPresent() or zatcaKeySignaturePresent() first. The com.fatoora properties are unchanged.

docs.title: Changed signatures
docs.text: These changes have no 0.6 equivalent to migrate to first; update the call when you upgrade.

docs.title: Client timeout
docs.text:
ZatcaClient.withTimeout takes a duration instead of a Long millisecond count: a java.time.Duration from Java or Kotlin, or a kotlin.time.Duration from Kotlin. The timeout is rounded up to whole milliseconds; zero, negative, infinite and longer-than-4294967.295-second values throw IllegalArgumentException. Use ZatcaClient.create(config) for no client-side timeout.

0.6 0.7 ZatcaClient.withTimeout(config, 30_000) Kotlin: ZatcaClient.withTimeout(config, 30.seconds) (import kotlin.time.Duration.Companion.seconds) ZatcaClient.withTimeout(config, 30000L) (Java) ZatcaClient.withTimeout(config, Duration.ofSeconds(30)) (import java.time.Duration)

docs.title: Binary output
docs.text:
Bytes.asSlice() is renamed Bytes.toByteArray(), the Kotlin name for a conversion that returns a new array. It still returns an independent copy that stays valid after the Bytes owner is closed.

0.6 0.7 bytes.asSlice() (Kotlin, ByteArray) bytes.toByteArray() bytes.asSlice() (Java, byte[]) bytes.toByteArray()

docs.title: Error classes
docs.text:
0.7 gives every language the same error hierarchy: a base FatooraException, one ErrorKind enum, and one subclass per kind named <Kind>Exception. See errors and diagnostics. These names change in 0.7 with no deprecated alias in 0.6, so update them while upgrading.

0.6 0.7 BindingException FatooraException (same code, kind, message and detailsJson) ErrorKind, ErrorKind.fromCode(code) Unchanged No public factory FatooraException.fromCode(code, message, detailsJson)

The subclasses (InvalidInputException, ..., ApiException) keep their names and constructors. A catch (error: BindingException) (Java catch (BindingException error)) becomes catch (error: FatooraException).

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
// 0.6, with deprecation warnings
val city: String = address.city()
val district: String? = address.district()?.use { it.value() }
val payable: String = invoice.totals().use { it.payableAmount() }
Adjustment.percentage(BigDecimal("200"), BigDecimal("10")).use { /* ... */ }
builder.addLineItem("Notebook", "2", "PCE", "50", "15", VatCategory.Standard)
client.reportSimplifiedInvoiceAsync(signed, credentials, false)

// 0.7
val city: String = address.city
val district: String? = address.district
val payable: BigDecimal = invoice.totals().use { it.payableAmount }
Adjustment.percentOf(BigDecimal("200"), BigDecimal("10")).use { /* ... */ }
builder.addLineItem("Notebook", BigDecimal("2"), "PCE", BigDecimal("50"), BigDecimal("15"), VatCategory.Standard)
client.reportSimplifiedInvoiceAsync(signed, credentials, ClearanceMode.Disabled)

// 0.7 (Java)
String city = address.getCity();
String district = address.getDistrict();
BigDecimal payable;
try (InvoiceTotals totals = invoice.totals()) {
    payable = totals.getPayableAmount();
}

docs.title: Migrate from 0.6 to 0.7: Python
docs.text:
This page covers the fatoority package (imported as fatoora). The overview lists the other languages.

pip install "fatoority==0.7.0"

0.7 removes every name that 0.6 kept with a DeprecationWarning, with no compatibility aliases left behind. Each replacement below already exists in 0.6, so the simplest path is to run your tests on 0.6 with python -W error::DeprecationWarning (or pytest's filterwarnings = ["error::DeprecationWarning"]), replace every name the warnings point at, and then upgrade. On 0.7 a removed name fails with ImportError, AttributeError or TypeError.

docs.title: Python 3.10 or newer
docs.text: 0.7 requires Python 3.10 or newer and ships no cp39 wheels; Python 3.9 reached end of life in October 2025. Upgrade the interpreter before upgrading the package; 0.6 stays installable on 3.9.

docs.title: Module names
docs.text:
These are no longer importable from fatoora, fatoora.invoice, fatoora.sign or fatoora.validation.

Removed Use instead Signer InvoiceSigner CsidCompliance / CsidProduction ComplianceCsid / ProductionCsid AllowanceCharge(charge, amount, category, rate, ...) Adjustment(amount, charge=..., category=..., rate=..., ...) DocumentReference(...) OriginalInvoiceRef(...), with the same arguments VatId(value), OtherId(value, scheme) Identifier(value), Identifier(value, scheme) parse_finalized_invoice_xml(xml) / parse_finalized_invoice_xml_file(path) FinalizedInvoice.from_xml(xml) / FinalizedInvoice.from_file(path) parse_signed_invoice_xml(xml) / parse_signed_invoice_xml_file(path) SignedInvoice.from_xml(xml) / SignedInvoice.from_file(path) invoice_hash_base64_from_xml_str(xml) hash_xml(xml) validate_xml_invoice_from_str(config, xml) validate_xml(xml) validate_zatca_invoice_from_str(config, xml, ...) validate_zatca(xml, ...), which returns a ZatcaReport; report.to_dict() gives the old dictionary

docs.title: Invoice builder
docs.text:
Removed Use instead builder.flags(value) builder.set_flags(value) set_note(language, text) add_note(text, language=language) set_note_without_language(text) add_note(text) set_payment_means_code(code) add_payment_means(PaymentMeans(code)) set_tax_exemption(category, rate, exemption) add_tax_exemption(category, rate, exemption) add_document_adjustment(charge, value, category, rate, exemption) add_charge(value, category, rate, exemption) when charge is true, otherwise add_allowance(...) invoice_level_discount(amount) add_allowance(Adjustment(amount), category, rate) invoice_level_charge(amount) add_charge(Adjustment(amount), category, rate) set_allowance(reason, amount) add_allowance(Adjustment(amount, reason=reason), category, rate) allowance_reason(reason) Adjustment(amount, reason=reason) on each entry

The aggregate setters (set_allowance, invoice_level_discount, invoice_level_charge, allowance_reason) added one allowance and one charge in the document VAT category, at the single VAT rate of that category's lines, when build() ran. add_allowance and add_charge append one entry per call in the category and at the rate you pass, so pass the document category and the line rate to keep the same totals.

The invoice properties invoice_level_discount, invoice_level_charge and allowance_reason stay: they report the totals and shared reason of the document-level entries.

docs.text:
Removed Use instead adjustment.value adjustment.amount adjustment.percent adjustment.percentage adjustment.with_supplied_amount(value) Adjustment.percent_of(base, percent, amount=value) value, scheme = identifier, identifier[0] identifier.value, identifier.scheme A (value, scheme) tuple for Party.vat_id, Party.identifiers or an item identifier Identifier(value, scheme) (a plain str value still works) close() or with on Address, Party, Identifier, InvoiceNote, OriginalInvoiceRef, PaymentMeans or Adjustment Nothing: they are plain frozen dataclasses with no cleanup

Passing a tuple where an identifier is expected now raises TypeError. Native owners such as Config, ZatcaClient, InvoiceBuilder and the invoice classes still support with and close().

docs.text:
Removed Use instead client.post_csr_for_ccsid(csr, otp) client.request_compliance_csid(csr, otp) client.post_ccsid_for_pcsid(ccsid) client.request_production_csid(ccsid) clearance_status=False / True on report_simplified_invoice and clear_standard_invoice clearance=ClearanceMode.DISABLED / ClearanceMode.ENABLED

clearance is now a required keyword-only argument of both methods.

docs.title: Error classes
docs.text:
0.7 gives every language the same error hierarchy: a base FatooraError, one ErrorKind enum, and one subclass per kind named <Kind>Error. See errors and diagnostics. These names change in 0.7 with no deprecated alias in 0.6, so update them while upgrading.

0.6 0.7 FfiError FatooraError; every library failure is a subclass of it FfiErrorKind ErrorKind (same members and values) fatoora.errors.error_class_for_code(code)(message, code, details) FatooraError.from_code(code, message, details) InvalidInputError(message, code, details) (any subclass) InvalidInputError(message, details=details); the code comes from the class, and code and details are keyword-only

The subclasses (InvalidInputError, ValidationError, ..., ApiError) keep their names and their ValueError/OSError bases. A code the package does not recognize now raises plain FatooraError instead of FfiError; its .kind is still None. Errors also gain .message.

# 0.6
from fatoora.errors import FfiError, FfiErrorKind
except FfiError as error:
    if error.kind == FfiErrorKind.NETWORK: ...

# 0.7
from fatoora import ErrorKind, FatooraError
except FatooraError as error:
    if error.kind == ErrorKind.NETWORK: ...

docs.title: New in 0.7
docs.text:
AsyncZatcaClient is an asyncio client with the methods of ZatcaClient, as coroutines. It needs httpx, from the optional async extra (pip install "fatoority[async]"); the base package still has no HTTP dependency. See asynchronous client.

async with AsyncZatcaClient(config, timeout=30) as client:
    response = await client.report_simplified_invoice(signed, pcsid, clearance=ClearanceMode.DISABLED)

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
# 0.6, with DeprecationWarnings
from fatoora import (InvoiceBuilder, InvoiceSubType, InvoiceTypeKind, VatCategory,
                     parse_signed_invoice_xml)

builder = InvoiceBuilder.new(InvoiceTypeKind.TAX, InvoiceSubType.SIMPLIFIED)
builder.set_vat_category(VatCategory.STANDARD)
builder.invoice_level_discount("10")
builder.allowance_reason("Loyalty discount")
builder.set_payment_means_code("10")

signed = parse_signed_invoice_xml(xml)
response = client.report_simplified_invoice(signed, pcsid, clearance_status=False)
print(signed.hash_base64(), signed.to_xml())

# 0.7
from fatoora import (Adjustment, ClearanceMode, InvoiceBuilder, InvoiceSubType, InvoiceTypeKind,
                     PaymentMeans, SignedInvoice, VatCategory)

builder = InvoiceBuilder(InvoiceTypeKind.TAX, InvoiceSubType.SIMPLIFIED)
builder.set_vat_category(VatCategory.STANDARD)
builder.add_allowance(Adjustment("10", reason="Loyalty discount"), VatCategory.STANDARD, "15")
builder.add_payment_means(PaymentMeans("10"))

signed = SignedInvoice.from_xml(xml)
response = client.report_simplified_invoice(signed, pcsid, clearance=ClearanceMode.DISABLED)
print(signed.hash(), signed.xml)

docs.title: Invoice builder, adjustments and payment means
docs.text:
Removed Use instead invoice::InvoiceTotalsData invoice::InvoiceTotals InvoiceBuilder::adjustment(entry) allowance(DocumentAdjustment::from(entry)) or charge(DocumentAdjustment::from(entry)), by entry.kind() InvoiceBuilder::invoice_level_discount(amount) allowance(DocumentAdjustment::new(Adjustment::amount(amount), category, rate)) InvoiceBuilder::invoice_level_charge(amount) charge(DocumentAdjustment::new(Adjustment::amount(amount), category, rate)) InvoiceBuilder::allowance_reason(text) DocumentAdjustment::with_reason(text) on each entry InvoiceBuilder::payment_means_code(code) InvoiceBuilder::payment_means(PaymentMeans::new(code)) PaymentMeans::instruction_note(text) PaymentMeans::with_instruction_note(text) Adjustment::allowance_charge_reason() Adjustment::reason() Adjustment::allowance_charge_reason_code() Adjustment::reason_code() Adjustment::calculation_base_amount() Adjustment::base_amount() Adjustment::calculation_percentage() Adjustment::percentage() VatBreakdown::without_vat_rate() VatBreakdown::omit_vat_rate()

The aggregate setters replaced one allowance and one charge in the document VAT category, with the rate taken from the first line in that category. allowance and charge append one entry per call with the category and rate you pass, so pass that category and rate to keep the same totals. Likewise, payment_means_code changed the code of the first payment means, while payment_means appends one.
