The replacements return an InvoiceHash instead of a String; call .as_str() or .to_string() where you need the text.

docs.title: InvoiceData keeps only adjustment entries
docs.text:
InvoiceData no longer stores the 0.5 aggregate fields invoice_level_discount, invoice_level_charge, adjustment_vat_rate and allowance_reason; document-level allowances and charges live only in adjustments(). The getters invoice_level_discount(), invoice_level_charge() and allowance_reason() stay: they report the totals and shared reason of those entries.

Invoice data serialized by 0.5 or 0.6 with an aggregate allowance or charge still deserializes and produces the same XML and hash: the amounts become entries in adjustments() with the document VAT category, the rate of the single line group in that category (or adjustment_vat_rate), and the old reason ("discount" or "charge" when none was set). If no line group or more than one matches, deserialization fails, as the 0.6 totals did. A reason with zero amounts needs no unique group and takes the rate from adjustment_vat_rate or the first line in the category, as 0.6 did; if that rate belongs to no line, 0.7 adds a zero VAT subtotal for it, where 0.6 wrote XML that fatoority's own parser rejects. Aggregate fields next to non-empty adjustments are ignored.

JSON and other human-readable formats written by 0.7 omit the four fields, so that JSON does not load in 0.6. bincode and other compact formats keep the 0.6 layout and stay readable in both directions.

docs.title: Zero request timeout is invalid input
docs.text: ZatcaClient::with_timeout(config, Duration::ZERO) returns the new ZatcaError::InvalidTimeout, classified as ErrorKind::InvalidInput, instead of ZatcaError::ClientState (ErrorKind::Internal). Code that matched ClientState or ErrorKind::Internal for this case should match the new variant or kind. The bindings report it with the invalid-input error code (1) and details type invalid_timeout.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
// 0.6, with deprecation warnings
let invoice = builder
    .invoice_level_discount(discount)
    .allowance_reason("Loyalty")
    .payment_means_code("10")
    .build()?;
let hash: String = invoice.hash_base64()?;

// 0.7
use fatoora_core::invoice::{Adjustment, DocumentAdjustment, PaymentMeans, VatCategory};

let invoice = builder
    .allowance(
        DocumentAdjustment::new(Adjustment::amount(discount), VatCategory::Standard, rate)
            .with_reason("Loyalty"),
    )
    .payment_means(PaymentMeans::new("10"))
    .build()?;
let hash: String = invoice.hash()?.to_string();

docs.title: ZATCA API client
docs.text: The API client requests credentials and submits signed invoices to the selected environment. For a runnable integration, start with the API guide. This reference describes inputs, returned data, and how to distinguish a completed request from an accepted invoice.

docs.title: Choose an operation
docs.text:
Operation Required input Returns Behavior Issue compliance credentials CSR and OTP Compliance credentials (CCSID) Sends the CSR as Base64-encoded PEM. Issue production credentials Compliance credentials with a request ID Production credentials (PCSID) Uses the compliance request ID to request production credentials. Renew production credentials Existing production credentials, new CSR, OTP, response language Production credentials Submits a renewal request. Check invoice compliance Signed invoice and compliance credentials Validation response Checks the invoice; a passing check does not establish reporting or clearance. Report a simplified invoice Signed simplified invoice, production credentials, clearance flag, response language Validation response Rejects standard invoices before sending. Clear a standard invoice Signed standard invoice, production credentials, clearance flag, response language Validation response Rejects simplified invoices before sending.

Credentials must match the client's environment. Production credentials describe the credential scope; they can belong to a test environment. The credential constructor stores supplied values; it does not authenticate them or obtain a certificate. Preserve the request ID returned during compliance onboarding.

docs.title: Input values
docs.text: Input Expected value Notes Configuration Selected environment Used for endpoints and credential environment checks. CSR Parsed or generated certificate signing request See CSR reference. Supply the matching private key separately when signing invoices. OTP Text supplied for the onboarding or renewal operation Sent in the OTP header. Invalid HTTP-header characters fail before transport. Token Binary security token returned by ZATCA Used with the secret for HTTP Basic authentication. Secret Credential secret returned by ZATCA Keep credentials out of logs. Request ID Optional text from credential issuance Required to request production credentials from compliance credentials. Invoice Signed invoice object The client sends its hash, UUID, and Base64 XML. Clearance flag ClearanceMode (Enabled/Disabled) in every language Sends Clearance-Status: 1 when enabled, 0 when disabled. It does not change the selected operation. Response language ar, en, or omitted Only the exact value ar selects Arabic; every other value sends English.

docs.title: Interpret an invoice response
docs.text:
A successful HTTP status means that a response body was decoded. Check acceptance before treating an invoice as reported or cleared. The acceptance helper fails for both rejected and unknown outcomes.

Invoked operation Accepted status Rejected status Reporting REPORTED NOT_REPORTED Clearance CLEARED NOT_CLEARED Compliance Validation status PASS or WARNING Validation status ERROR

Missing or unrecognized endpoint status produces an unknown outcome. A positive status accompanied by validation errors also produces an unknown outcome. Warnings alone do not prevent acceptance. Only the status for the operation actually invoked determines its outcome.

Returned field Value Meaning HTTP status Optional integer Actual response status, when attached by the client. Outcome Accepted, rejected, or unknown Classification for the invoked operation. Validation results Result object Contains message collections and optional overall status. Reporting / clearance status Optional status enum (Python: optional text) Gateway status for each operation; unrecognized values map to Other/Unknown, and the bindings' *_raw getters return the exact text. Seller / buyer QR status Optional text Raw QR status returned by the gateway. Cleared invoice Base64 Optional text Exact encoded invoice returned by clearance. Cleared invoice XML Optional decoded text Preserves returned text; does not parse XML or verify its signature.

Missing cleared XML is independent of acceptance. A present empty Base64 value, invalid Base64, NUL bytes, or invalid UTF-8 fails decoding.

Validation results contain information, warning, and error message collections, which can be empty, plus an optional status. Each message has optional type, code, category, message text, and status fields. Handle missing fields instead of assuming that every response contains a complete diagnostic.

docs.title: HTTP failures and custom transport
docs.text:
Invoice operations treat every non-2xx response as an error, including 400 and 409. A duplicate-reporting 409 does not establish that an earlier submission was rejected. A 208 clearance response follows the successful-response path and still requires an acceptance check. Redirects are not followed; a 303 does not trigger automatic reporting. A malformed successful body is a decoding error, and a failed body read is a transport error.

No client-side request timeout applies by default. Construct the client with a timeout to bound each request, from connecting until the response body is read. A request that exceeds it fails as a network (transport) error. A zero timeout is rejected as invalid input (ErrorKind::InvalidInput, details type invalid_timeout). JavaScript has no timeout option: its client sends through the fetch you supply, so bound requests there with an AbortSignal.

Credential issuance requires a successful response. Renewal additionally supports the gateway's 428 renewal response when it contains a decodable credential body.

Where exposed, prepared requests let you use your own HTTP transport. Preparing performs input checks and builds an owned request without sending it. Send its method, URL, headers, and body, then pass the actual HTTP status and response bytes to its decoder. Headers contain credentials. The decoder preserves the operation context needed for acceptance checks. Keep redirects disabled in custom transports.

docs.title: Language reference
docs.text:
RustPythonJavaScriptC#KotlinJavaC

Import client, credential, and response types from fatoora_core::api. ZatcaClient::new(config: Config) returns Result<ZatcaClient, ZatcaError>. ZatcaClient::with_timeout(config: Config, timeout: Duration) does the same with a per-request timeout; a timeout surfaces as ZatcaError::Http (or ZatcaError::ResponseRead mid-body), both ErrorKind::Network. A zero timeout returns ZatcaError::InvalidTimeout (ErrorKind::InvalidInput). HTTP methods are async; call them with .await. Inputs below are borrowed.

HTTP operations

Method on client Returns after .await request_compliance_csid(csr: &Csr, otp: &str) Result<ComplianceCsid, ZatcaError> request_production_csid(ccsid: &ComplianceCsid) Result<ProductionCsid, ZatcaError> renew_csid(pcsid: &CsidCredentials<Production>, csr: &Csr, otp: &str, accept_language: Option<&str>) Result<CsidCredentials<Production>, ZatcaError> check_invoice_compliance(invoice: &SignedInvoice, credentials: &CsidCredentials<Compliance>) Result<ValidationResponse, ZatcaError> report_simplified_invoice(invoice: &SignedInvoice, credentials: &CsidCredentials<Production>, clearance_mode: ClearanceMode, accept_language: Option<&str>) Result<ValidationResponse, ZatcaError> clear_standard_invoice(invoice: &SignedInvoice, credentials: &CsidCredentials<Production>, clearance_mode: ClearanceMode, accept_language: Option<&str>) Result<ValidationResponse, ZatcaError>

ClearanceMode::Enabled / ClearanceMode::Disabled send the Clearance-Status header as 1 / 0; ClearanceMode::from(flag) converts a bool. The prepare_report_simplified_invoice / prepare_clear_standard_invoice variants take the same arguments.

Credentials

CsidCredentials::<Compliance>::new(env, request_id, token, secret) creates compliance credentials; use Production for production scope. ComplianceCsid and ProductionCsid are aliases for CsidCredentials<Compliance> and CsidCredentials<Production>. Arguments are Environment, Option<String>, and two impl Into<String> values. Construction returns the credential object directly.

Accessor Returns credentials.env() Environment credentials.request_id() Option<&str> credentials.binary_security_token() / credentials.secret() &str

Responses

Method Returns response.http_status() Option<u16> response.outcome() InvoiceOutcome::{Accepted, Rejected, Unknown} response.ensure_accepted() Result<(), ZatcaError> response.validation_results() &ValidationResults response.reporting_status() Option<&ReportingStatus>: Reported, NotReported, Other(String) response.clearance_status() Option<&ClearanceStatus>: Cleared, NotCleared, Other(String) response.qr_seller_status() / qr_buyer_status() Option<&str> response.cleared_invoice_base64() Option<&str> response.cleared_invoice_xml() Result<Option<String>, ZatcaError> results.status() Option<&ValidationStatus>: Pass, Warning, Error, Other(String) results.info_messages() &MessageList: One, Many, or Empty results.warning_messages() / results.error_messages() &[ValidationMessage] message.message_type() Option<&MessageType>: Info, Warning, Error, Other(String) message.status() Option<&ValidationStatus> message.code() / category() / message() Option<&str>

The status enums are non-exhaustive. A value they do not recognize is kept verbatim in Other; as_str() and Display return the exact wire text. These getters borrow the response. Serializing and deserializing the response body does not preserve HTTP status or operation context; the deserialized outcome is Unknown. ZatcaError::NotAccepted retains the response. For HTTP failures, ZatcaError::http_status() provides the status when available; HttpResponseError::body() and validation_response() expose the retained body and optional parsed response. See error reference.

Prepared requests

Prefix each HTTP method above with prepare_ and use the same arguments. These synchronous methods return Result<ComplianceRequest, ZatcaError> for CSR issuance, Result<ProductionRequest, ZatcaError> for production issuance/renewal, and Result<InvoiceRequest, ZatcaError> for invoice operations.

prepared.request() borrows an HttpRequest. Its method() and url() return &str, headers() returns &[(String, String)], and body() returns &[u8]. prepared.decode(status: u16, body: &[u8]) returns the corresponding response or credentials in Result<_, ZatcaError>. Preparing and decoding do not consume inputs. The request owns its data and can outlive the client, invoice, and credentials.

Import ZatcaClient, ComplianceCsid, ProductionCsid, ClearanceMode, and InvoiceOutcome from fatoora. Construct ZatcaClient(config: Config, *, timeout=None); timeout is seconds (int/float) or a datetime.timedelta, and a request that exceeds it raises NetworkError. HTTP calls block until they finish and raise classified exceptions on failure; see errors.

HTTP operations

Method on client Returns request_compliance_csid(csr: Csr, otp: str) ComplianceCsid request_production_csid(ccsid: ComplianceCsid) ProductionCsid renew_csid(pcsid: ProductionCsid, csr: Csr, otp: str, accept_language: Optional[str] = None) ProductionCsid check_invoice_compliance(invoice: SignedInvoice, ccsid: ComplianceCsid) ValidationResponse report_simplified_invoice(invoice: SignedInvoice, pcsid: ProductionCsid, *, clearance: ClearanceMode, accept_language: Optional[str] = None) ValidationResponse clear_standard_invoice(invoice: SignedInvoice, pcsid: ProductionCsid, *, clearance: ClearanceMode, accept_language: Optional[str] = None) ValidationResponse

clearance (required) and accept_language are keyword-only. ClearanceMode.DISABLED sends Clearance-Status: 0 and ClearanceMode.ENABLED sends 1.

Credentials

ComplianceCsid(env: Environment, *, token: str, secret: str, request_id: Optional[str] = None) builds compliance credentials from stored values; ProductionCsid(...) takes the same arguments. The env property is an Environment; binary_security_token and secret are str; request_id is Optional[str], None when absent.

Responses

Property or method Value response.http_status Optional[int] response.outcome InvoiceOutcome.ACCEPTED, .REJECTED, or .UNKNOWN response.ensure_accepted() None; raises ApiError if not accepted. response.validation_results ValidationResults response.reporting_status Optional[ReportingStatus]: REPORTED, NOT_REPORTED response.clearance_status Optional[ClearanceStatus]: CLEARED, NOT_CLEARED response.qr_seller_status / qr_buyer_status Optional[str] response.cleared_invoice_base64 Optional[str] response.cleared_invoice_xml Optional[str]; raises ParseError for invalid content. results.status Optional[ValidationStatus]: PASS, WARNING, ERROR results.info_messages / warning_messages / error_messages list[ValidationMessage] message.message_type Optional[MessageType]: INFO, WARNING, ERROR message.status Optional[ValidationStatus] message.code / category / message Optional[str]

The status enums are str subclasses whose values are the wire text, so response.reporting_status == "REPORTED" holds. A value this version does not recognize is kept verbatim, like the core's Other(String): it is an instance of the enum whose name is "OTHER" and whose value is the text ZATCA sent.

Client, credential, response, result, and message objects support with and close(). Child results are independently owned. Calls do not consume their inputs. Prepared-request methods are not exposed by the Python facade.

Asynchronous client

AsyncZatcaClient(config: Config, *, timeout=None, http_client: Optional[httpx.AsyncClient] = None) has the HTTP operations above as async def methods with the same arguments, return types, and errors. It needs the async extra (pip install "fatoority[async]"), which adds httpx; the native library prepares and decodes each request and httpx sends it, without following redirects. Use async with or await client.aclose(); the client closes the httpx.AsyncClient it created, never one passed as http_client. A transport failure or timeout raises NetworkError. See the Python reference.

Import ZatcaClient, ComplianceCsid, ProductionCsid, and InvoiceOutcome from fatoority. Create new ZatcaClient(config, { fetch }); the second argument is optional and defaults to globalThis.fetch. Calls return promises; use await.

HTTP operations

Method on client Promise resolves to requestComplianceCsid(csr, otp, options = {}) ComplianceCsid requestProductionCsid(credentials, options = {}) ProductionCsid renewCsid(credentials, csr, otp, acceptLanguage = null, options = {}) ProductionCsid checkInvoiceCompliance(invoice, credentials, options = {}) ValidationResponse reportSimplifiedInvoice(invoice, credentials, clearanceMode, acceptLanguage = null, options = {}) ValidationResponse clearStandardInvoice(invoice, credentials, clearanceMode, acceptLanguage = null, options = {}) ValidationResponse

Pass Csr for csr, SignedInvoice for invoice, strings for OTP/language, and ClearanceMode.Disabled or ClearanceMode.Enabled for clearanceMode, which is required; any other value, including a boolean or the variant name, rejects with a TypeError. Compliance issuance uses no credential; compliance checks and production issuance take ComplianceCsid; reporting, clearance, and renewal take ProductionCsid. Each options accepts { signal: AbortSignal } for cancellation. Transport failures reject with NetworkError (host error in cause); response/acceptance failures reject with the FatooraError subclass for their code, such as ApiError or UnauthorizedError. See JavaScript HTTP setup for browser CORS and custom fetch behavior.

Credentials

ComplianceCsid.create(environment, requestId, token, secret) returns compliance credentials; ProductionCsid.create returns production credentials. Pass an Environment (Environment.NonProduction, .Simulation, or .Production), a string or null request ID, and string token/secret. The env property is the Environment; binarySecurityToken and secret are strings and requestId is a string or null.

Responses

Value getters are read-only properties; members with parentheses are methods.

Member Value response.httpStatus Number or null response.outcome InvoiceOutcome.Accepted, .Rejected, or .Unknown response.ensureAccepted() undefined; throws unless accepted. response.validationResults() ValidationResults response.reportingStatus ReportingStatus (Reported, NotReported, Unknown) or null response.clearanceStatus ClearanceStatus (Cleared, NotCleared, Unknown) or null response.reportingStatusRaw / clearanceStatusRaw / qrSellerStatus / qrBuyerStatus String or null response.clearedInvoiceBase64 / clearedInvoiceXml String or null; reading the XML can throw. results.status ValidationStatus (Pass, Warning, Error, Unknown) or null results.statusRaw String or null results.infoLen / warningLen / errorLen Number of messages results.infoMessage(index) / warningMessage(index) / errorMessage(index) ValidationMessage message.messageType MessageType (Info, Warning, Error, Unknown) or null message.status ValidationStatus or null message.messageTypeRaw / statusRaw / code / category / message String or null

Status enums are null when the field is absent and Unknown when it is present but not recognized by this binding version; the matching *Raw property holds the exact wire string. Compare with === ReportingStatus.Reported, or read the variant name from .value.

Message indexes are zero-based and must be less than the corresponding length. Child handles are independently owned. Calls do not consume inputs. See JavaScript resource handling for binary data lifetimes.

Prepared requests

For custom transport, import ZatcaClient as RequestClient from fatoority/raw and create it with RequestClient.create(config). Its synchronous methods are prepareRequestComplianceCsid, prepareRequestProductionCsid, prepareRenewCsid, prepareCheckInvoiceCompliance, prepareReportSimplifiedInvoice, and prepareClearStandardInvoice. They take the same operation arguments as above, without options; supply a ClearanceMode (not a boolean) and nullable language explicitly. They return ComplianceRequest, ProductionRequest, or InvoiceRequest according to the operation.

request.method, url, and headersJson are strings; body() returns Bytes; toUint8Array() copies it. request.decode(status, body) takes an HTTP status number and a Uint8Array and returns the corresponding credentials or validation response. Alternatively, await sendPrepared(request, { fetch, signal }) from fatoority sends and decodes the request. Preparation owns its data; it does not send HTTP.

Use the Fatoora namespace. ZatcaClient.Create(config: Config) returns a client; ZatcaClient.WithTimeout(config, timeout: TimeSpan) adds a per-request timeout, rounded up to whole milliseconds, that raises NetworkException when exceeded; a zero, negative, or over-uint.MaxValue-millisecond timeout throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException. Use zero-based java.math.BigInteger indexes below the corresponding message count. Child objects are independently owned. Methods do not consume their inputs.

Prepared requests

Use the six methods prepareRequestComplianceCsid, prepareRequestProductionCsid, prepareRenewCsid, prepareCheckInvoiceCompliance, prepareReportSimplifiedInvoice, and prepareClearStandardInvoice with the same inputs as their HTTP counterparts. They return ComplianceRequest for compliance credentials, ProductionRequest for production credentials/renewal, and InvoiceRequest for invoice operations, without sending HTTP.

request.getMethod(), getUrl(), and getHeadersJson() return String; body() returns owned Bytes. request.decode(status, body) accepts int HTTP status and byte[] response body, and returns the matching credential or response type. Prepared requests own their input data and may outlive the original client and inputs.

Include fatoora.h. Every operation returns FatooraStatus; FATOORA_OK means its output was written. Other statuses indicate failure; inspect the optional FatooraError. Calls borrow inputs and block while sending HTTP.

Environment values are FATOORA_NON_PRODUCTION, FATOORA_SIMULATION, and FATOORA_PRODUCTION. clearance_mode is FATOORA_CLEARANCE_DISABLED or FATOORA_CLEARANCE_ENABLED (the Clearance-Status header). Any other enum value returns FATOORA_INVALID_INPUT. Use NULL for absent request ID or language. Text inputs are UTF-8 strings. Credential getters start with fatoora_compliance_csid_ or fatoora_production_csid_, take const credential pointer, output pointer, and FatooraError **error. env writes FatooraEnvironment; request_id, binary_security_token, and secret write owned char *, with NULL for absent request ID.

Responses

Each getter takes const FatooraValidationResponse *self, the output argument below, then FatooraError **error. ensure_accepted takes only self and error.

Function Output fatoora_validation_response_http_status uint16_t *out, bool *has_value fatoora_validation_response_outcome FatooraInvoiceOutcome *out fatoora_validation_response_ensure_accepted No output; FATOORA_OK only if accepted. fatoora_validation_response_validation_results FatooraValidationResults **out fatoora_validation_response_reporting_status FatooraReportingStatus *out, bool *has_value fatoora_validation_response_reporting_status_raw char **out fatoora_validation_response_clearance_status FatooraClearanceStatus *out, bool *has_value fatoora_validation_response_clearance_status_raw char **out fatoora_validation_response_qr_seller_status char **out fatoora_validation_response_qr_buyer_status char **out fatoora_validation_response_cleared_invoice_base64 char **out fatoora_validation_response_cleared_invoice_xml char **out; decoding can fail.

Optional text returns NULL for absence, distinct from a present empty string. Status enum getters set *has_value to false when the field is absent; a present value this binding version does not recognize is written as the *_UNKNOWN enumerator (such as FATOORA_REPORTING_STATUS_UNKNOWN), and the _raw getter returns the exact wire string. Result getters use the fatoora_validation_results_ prefix: status(self, FatooraValidationStatus *out, bool *has_value, error) returns the optional status and status_raw(self, char **out, error) its text; info_len, warning_len, and error_len use size_t *out; info_message, warning_message, and error_message take self, zero-based size_t index, FatooraValidationMessage **out, and error. Indexes must be below the corresponding length.

Message getters use fatoora_validation_message_ with suffixes message_type_raw, code, category, message, and status_raw. Each takes self, char **out, and error, returning optional owned text. message_type writes FatooraMessageType *out and status writes FatooraValidationStatus *out, each with bool *has_value.

Prepared requests

Add prepare_ after fatoora_zatca_client_ in the six HTTP function names above. Inputs are identical; the output changes to FatooraComplianceRequest ** for CSR issuance, FatooraProductionRequest ** for production issuance/renewal, or FatooraInvoiceRequest ** for invoice operations.

Request accessors use fatoora_compliance_request_, fatoora_production_request_, or fatoora_invoice_request_. method, url, and headers_json take self, char **out, and error; body uses FatooraBytes **out. decode takes self, uint16_t status, const uint8_t *body, size_t body_len, the matching credential/response output pointer, and error. The request owns its data and does not send HTTP until your transport does so.

Ownership

Outputs and response children are independent owned copies. Release text with fatoora_string_free; release handles with their matching _free function, such as fatoora_zatca_client_free, fatoora_compliance_csid_free, fatoora_production_csid_free, fatoora_validation_response_free, fatoora_validation_results_free, fatoora_validation_message_free, or fatoora_invoice_request_free. See C ownership and errors.

docs.text: Configuration selects the ZATCA API environment. Use the same environment for CSR generation, credentials, and the client that sends requests.

Environment Purpose API base URL Non-production Integration sandbox for initial testing https://gw-fatoora.zatca.gov.sa/e-invoicing/developer-portal/ Simulation Testing the integration before production https://gw-fatoora.zatca.gov.sa/e-invoicing/simulation/ Production Live invoice operations https://gw-fatoora.zatca.gov.sa/e-invoicing/core/

The environment also selects the CSR certificate-template extension. Choosing an environment does not obtain credentials or establish that an invoice is accepted. Clients reject credentials issued for a different environment before sending a request.

docs.title: CSR and private keys
docs.text: A certificate signing request (CSR) binds a device identity to a public key. Create properties, generate or load a private key, then build the CSR for the selected environment. For a complete runnable workflow, follow Generate a CSR and private key.

docs.title: Property values
docs.text:
Every field is required. The constructor and properties-file parser apply the same validation. Supply your own registered identity values for onboarding; the example properties file contains demonstration data.

Field / properties-file key Expected value common_name / csr.common.name Device or solution common name. serial_number / csr.serial.number Solution serial number in the format required for your device. organization_identifier / csr.organization.identifier Organization VAT identifier. organization_unit_name / csr.organization.unit.name Branch or organizational unit. organization_name / csr.organization.name Legal organization name. country_name / csr.country.name Exactly two ASCII letters, such as SA. invoice_type / csr.invoice.type Exactly four 0 or 1 digits, such as 1100. location_address / csr.location.address Business location. industry_business_category / csr.industry.business.category Business activity.

Text fields must contain non-whitespace text and cannot contain ! @ # $ % & * _ <. Country and invoice-type fields have the stricter formats above. Values are not trimmed or normalized by the constructor. Country validation checks the two-letter format, not membership in the ISO country list. Serial numbers and organization identifiers are not checked against registration records. Passing local validation does not guarantee that ZATCA accepts the identity.

Properties text uses key=value entries. Missing required keys fail; unknown keys are ignored and repeated keys use their last value. File-loading methods read UTF-8.

docs.title: Operations and formats
docs.text:
Operation Input Result and behavior Create properties The nine fields above, in table order Validated properties, or a validation error. Parse properties Properties text or a file path Validated properties; fails on unreadable files, malformed text, or missing fields. Generate a key No input A new random secp256k1 private key. Load a key PKCS#8 PEM text or DER bytes Private key; malformed or incompatible key material fails. Build a CSR Properties, private key, environment New CSR signed by the supplied key; properties and key remain usable. Load a CSR DER bytes Parsed CSR; this does not establish gateway approval. Read subject CSR Formatted distinguished-name text. Read extensions CSR Collection of encoded extension values for inspection. Output format Contents Typical use Key PEM / DER PKCS#8 private-key material Save or reload the signing key. CSR PEM Text with certificate-request delimiters Save a readable csr.pem file. CSR DER Binary certificate request Binary storage or parsing. CSR Base64 Base64 of DER bytes Consumers that explicitly require encoded DER. CSR PEM Base64 Base64 of complete PEM text ZATCA credential requests; the API client performs this conversion.

Keep the private key: the CSR contains its public key, not the private key needed for invoice signing. Serialization returns data and does not write files.

docs.text: Use the CSR with the API client to request credentials, then use your matching private key and issued certificate for invoice signing.

docs.title: Errors and diagnostics
docs.text: Use error codes and structured fields to decide how to recover. Messages are intended for display and can change; do not parse their wording.

docs.title: Shared classification
docs.text:
Every failure has one ErrorKind with a stable numeric code. Each binding throws one class per kind under a common base, with the same names in every language:

Code ErrorKind Python JavaScript C# Kotlin / Java C status Meaning (base) FatooraError FatooraError FatooraException FatooraException Every library failure; also thrown alone for an unknown code 1 InvalidInput InvalidInputError InvalidInputError InvalidInputException InvalidInputException FATOORA_INVALID_INPUT An argument, key, certificate, option or context is invalid 2 Validation ValidationError ValidationError ValidationException ValidationException FATOORA_VALIDATION A model validation failure or interrupted rule evaluation 3 Parse ParseError ParseError ParseException ParseException FATOORA_PARSE Structured data, a successful API response, or returned cleared XML could not be decoded 4 Xml XmlError XmlError XmlException XmlException FATOORA_XML An XML operation failed 5 Crypto CryptoError CryptoError CryptoException CryptoException FATOORA_CRYPTO A cryptographic operation failed 6 Io IoError IoError IoException IoException FATOORA_IO A file or other I/O operation failed 7 Network NetworkError NetworkError NetworkException NetworkException FATOORA_NETWORK A network operation failed 8 Unauthorized UnauthorizedError UnauthorizedError UnauthorizedException UnauthorizedException FATOORA_UNAUTHORIZED The service rejected authorization 9 Internal InternalError InternalError InternalException InternalException FATOORA_INTERNAL An internal operation failed 10 Api ApiError ApiError ApiException ApiException FATOORA_API A non-authorization API response or acceptance check failed

Every error object carries the same data, spelled in each language's style:

Data Rust Python JavaScript C# Kotlin (Java) C Kind kind() → ErrorKind .kind → ErrorKind (IntEnum, INVALID_INPUT) .kind → ErrorKind string ('InvalidInput') Kind → ErrorKind? kind (getKind()) → ErrorKind? — Code kind() as i32 .code .code Code code (getCode()) fatoora_error_code() Message Display .message, str(error) .message Message message (getMessage()) fatoora_error_message() Details details_json() .details (dict) .details (object) DetailsJson (string) detailsJson (getDetailsJson()) fatoora_error_details_json() Create by code — FatooraError.from_code(code, message, details) FatooraError.fromCode(code, message, { details }) FatooraException.FromCode(code, message, detailsJson) FatooraException.fromCode(code, message, detailsJson) —

Kind is null (None) only for a code this version does not recognize; the error is then the base class and keeps its code and details.

Classification follows the cause: an XML failure during signing is Xml, while a file-read failure is Io. Preserve unknown numeric codes and provide a generic fallback. An Internal failure may leave an operation consumed; discard affected operation handles.

docs.title: Handle an error
JSON details
docs.text:
Every details object contains a type string. The schema is explicitly mapped from errors rather than language-specific serialization. Existing field meanings and discriminator strings are stable. Additional fields and types may be added. Consumers must ignore unknown fields and handle unknown types. Messages are for display and must not be parsed for classification.

An invoice validation failure looks like this:

{
  "type": "invoice_validation",
  "issues": [
    {
      "field": "line_item_vat_amount",
      "kind": "mismatch",
      "line_item_index": 0,
      "supplied": "10",
      "expected": "15"
    }
  ]
}

Issue fields use snake_case names for invoice fields. Issue kinds are missing, empty, invalid_format, out_of_range, or mismatch. line_item_index is zero-based, or null for an invoice-level issue. Decimal values are exact strings with insignificant trailing zeroes removed; absent amounts are null.

Details type Structured fields invoice_validation issues: field, kind, item index, supplied and expected amounts schema_parse, schema_validation diagnostics: message, optional file, line, column, severity zatca_validation_execution kind, optional stage, assertion_site, location, diagnostics, and partial report xml_serialize, signing_xml, signing_input diagnostics api_response http_status: actual HTTP status; body: response text; response: complete parsed JSON or null api_response_decode http_status, body, message for a malformed 2xx response api_response_read http_status, message for a failed response-body read api_not_accepted http_status or null, outcome: rejected or unknown, response: typed validation body api_cleared_invoice http_status or null, message for invalid cleared-invoice content api_unauthorized response: timestamp, status, error, message api_server response: category, code, message missing_property path, key properties_parse path, diagnostics io path, diagnostics der_encode context, diagnostics csr_extension extension, diagnostics missing_field field invalid_value field, value invalid_xsd_path path invalid_environment, invalid_country_code, invalid_currency_code, invalid_timestamp, invalid_issue_date value qr_value_too_long tag, length, limit (255 bytes) qr_encoded_too_long length, limit (700 encoded characters)

Message-only failures use diagnostics containing a message. Their types are xml_parse, xpath, qr_xml, signing, invalid_subject, invalid_san, csr_request, csr_build, key_decode, key_encode, csr_validation, network, invalid_response, http, and client_state.

Types without additional fields are invalid_decimal, decimal_out_of_range, missing_seller_vat, missing_seller_name, missing_buyer_id, invalid_vat_format, and invalid_timeout. Binding-level failures use {"type":"binding_error"} with the classification and message available through their accessors.

Diagnostic location fields may be absent or null. File paths are converted to UTF-8 lossily when their native encoding cannot be represented. Nested signing and invoice-import failures retain their underlying validation, serialization, decimal, or QR details.

docs.title: Local ZATCA execution failures
docs.text:
Local validation returns a report for ordinary rejection or incomplete coverage. Inspect is_valid before accepting an invoice. is_complete describes stage coverage; has_errors includes findings obtained before a stage failed. Warnings allow validity once all required stages complete.

Interrupted execution produces an error. Its details have type zatca_validation_execution and these fields:

Field Meaning kind Execution failure kind from the table below stage xsd, cen, ksa, signature, qr, previous_invoice_hash, or null assertion_site Source assertion key, such as ksa:112:BR-KSA-CL-02, or null location Shared validation location, including namespace-independent XPath, or null diagnostics One diagnostic containing the execution failure's message report Full report up to the failure, with stage statuses and earlier findings Execution kind Shared classification invalid_xml Xml (4) unsupported_xml InvalidInput (1) capacity_exceeded InvalidInput (1) invalid_context InvalidInput (1) rule_evaluation Validation (2) schema Parse (3) integrity Crypto (5)

The rule_evaluation classification describes interrupted execution. Ordinary business-rule violations remain findings in a successfully returned report. Invalid arguments or malformed options can fail before validation starts and have no partial report. Always allow for that absence. See invoice validation for stage applicability and predecessor context.

docs.title: Invoice model
docs.text: Build invoices and calculate their totals with the typed model. Start with the runnable creation guide or the pricing recipes. For an existing XML document, start with XML parsing. For signatures and certificate inputs, see invoice signing.

docs.title: Building an invoice
docs.text:
Create a builder, set the required fields, append one or more line items, then build a finalized invoice. Building checks supported field formats and amounts and calculates totals. It does not run schema validation, all ZATCA business rules, or signature verification; use validation for those checks.

Scalar setters replace their previous value. Lines, notes, billing references, and independent adjustments append in order. Rust allowance(DocumentAdjustment) and charge(DocumentAdjustment) append document adjustments, and the generated bindings mirror them as add_allowance and add_charge. In the generated bindings, set_* methods replace a value and add_* methods append one. Use collection getters to read every repeated entry.

docs.title: Fields and expected values
docs.text:
Field Required Expected value and behavior Invoice type and subtype Yes Tax invoice, prepayment, credit note, or debit note; standard or simplified subtype. Supply original invoice references and correction reasons for credit/debit business validation. Original UUID and issue date are optional. ID Yes Nonblank invoice identifier, such as INV-1001. UUID Yes Invoice UUID text. The builder checks nonblank input, not UUID syntax. Issue datetime Yes UTC YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ, for example 2026-10-15T09:30:00Z. Currency Yes Recognized ISO currency code, such as SAR. Trimmed and normalized to uppercase. Previous invoice hash Yes Previous invoice hash text. The builder checks nonblank input; it does not verify the chain or decode the hash. Invoice counter Yes Unsigned 64-bit integer. The model accepts zero; check applicable business rules separately. Seller Yes Name, address, and VAT ID; optional other identification and scheme. Buyer No in builder Name with optional address and identifiers. Identification requirements depend on the invoice type and are checked by business validation. Payment means code Yes Nonblank code text, for example 10 for cash. The builder does not validate the complete payment code list. VAT category Yes Standard, zero-rated, exempt, or out of scope. Each line also has its own category. Line items Yes At least one. Nonblank description; nonnegative quantity and unit price. Unit code can be omitted; a supplied code must be nonblank. VAT rate Per line Percentage in the inclusive range 0–100, at most two decimal places. Categories other than standard require zero. Invoice charge / discount No Nonnegative decimal amount, at most two decimal places. Defaults to zero. Line pricing No Price-base quantity, gross price and price discount, supplied amounts, line allowances/charges. Independent document adjustments No Repeated allowances/charges with their own VAT category and rate. VAT breakdowns and exemptions No Supplied category/rate totals and independent exemption code/text. Prepaid amount / payable rounding No Prepaid amount subtracts from payable; rounding is signed. Business references No Repeated billing references, purchase order ID, contract ID. Delivery No Independent actual/latest dates. Payment entries No Ordered payment codes with optional instructions and financial account data. Party and item identifiers No Multiple party IDs; seller, buyer, and standard item IDs. Notes No Repeated language/text entries in insertion order. Flags No Third party, nominal, export, summary, self-billed. Defaults to no flags.

Address inputs are country code, city, street, building number, and postal code, with optional additional street, additional number, district, and province/state. Buyer addresses may be absent. Country accepts recognized ISO alpha-2 or alpha-3 values (SA or SAU) and is stored as alpha-3. A VAT ID wrapper checks only that trimmed text is nonempty; use ZATCA validation for country-specific requirements.

Credit/debit note original issue dates use YYYY-MM-DD. Optional values mean absence; an empty string is still a supplied value.

See decimal numbers for precision and rounding. Line totals are calculated from quantity and price. Explicitly supplied line net amounts have a 0.01 tolerance around the rounded calculation; imported amounts are not accepted merely because they parse.

docs.title: Returned data and totals
docs.text:
A finalized invoice contains invoice data and calculated totals. A signed invoice also stores the original signed XML alongside its QR payload and signature metadata. Signed import checks the signature and digests against the embedded certificate and verifies QR consistency. Certificate issuer trust and gateway acceptance remain separate checks.

Result Contents Invoice data Identity, type/subtype, parties, notes, original invoice reference, flags, line items, and invoice adjustments. Line item Description, quantity, unit code, unit price, line total, VAT rate, VAT amount, and category. Indexed access is zero-based and rejects out-of-range indexes. Totals Line extension, allowance total, charge total, taxable amount, tax amount, tax inclusive total, prepaid amount, payable rounding amount, and payable amount. Computed hash hash() hashes emitted XML for a finalized model and stored XML for a signed invoice. Signed import rejects digest mismatches and retains the original XML.

docs.title: Advanced building in the bindings
docs.text:
The bindings expose LineItemBuilder for price bases and line adjustments. Build the line, then append it with the invoice builder's add_item equivalent. add_line_item remains the shortcut for a line with quantity and unit price.

Operation Python JavaScript / TypeScript C# Kotlin / Java Create a line builder LineItemBuilder() LineItemBuilder.create() LineItemBuilder.Create() LineItemBuilder.create() Set price base set_item_price_base_quantity(value) setItemPriceBaseQuantity(value) SetItemPriceBaseQuantity(value) setItemPriceBaseQuantity(value) Add line allowance add_allowance(adjustment) addAllowance(adjustment) AddAllowance(adjustment) addAllowance(adjustment) Add line charge add_charge(adjustment) addCharge(adjustment) AddCharge(adjustment) addCharge(adjustment) Finish line build() build() Build() build() Append built line to invoice add_item(item) addItem(item) AddItem(item) addItem(item) Append document allowance add_allowance(...) addAllowance(...) AddAllowance(...) addAllowance(...) Append document charge add_charge(...) addCharge(...) AddCharge(...) addCharge(...) Set prepaid amount set_prepaid_amount(value) setPrepaidAmount(value) SetPrepaidAmount(value) setPrepaidAmount(value) Set payable rounding set_payable_rounding_amount(value) setPayableRoundingAmount(value) SetPayableRoundingAmount(value) setPayableRoundingAmount(value) Append billing reference add_billing_reference(reference) addBillingReference(reference) AddBillingReference(reference) addBillingReference(reference) Append payment entry add_payment_means(payment) addPaymentMeans(payment) AddPaymentMeans(payment) addPaymentMeans(payment)

Document allowance and charge arguments are (adjustment, category, rate, exemption), mirroring Rust allowance and charge. In Python the category, rate and exemption default to the fields of the Adjustment value, and the exemption to empty metadata; the other bindings require a TaxExemption object. Category values and decimal representations follow the language reference below.

For a prepayment adjustment line, use add_document_reference and add_tax_subtotal on the Python line builder (addDocumentReference and addTaxSubtotal in JavaScript/Kotlin/Java; PascalCase in C#). OriginalInvoiceRef constructors accept ID, UUID, date, time, and document type code in that order. Set the last argument to "386"; in Python it is the optional document_type_code keyword. The prepayment recipe shows which line amounts must be zero and how to supply the advance VAT subtotal.

For C, use fatoora_line_item_builder_new(&line, &error) and fatoora_line_item_builder_build(line, &item, &error). The setters above use the fatoora_line_item_builder_ prefix with snake_case names. Invoice operations use fatoora_invoice_builder_, including add_item, add_allowance, add_charge, and set_prepaid_amount. Each accepts the builder first and FatooraError ** last, and returns a status. Document allowances and charges take an adjustment handle, FatooraVatCategory category, decimal rate text, and exemption handle. Free owned handles after use, including consumed builders. See C ownership.

docs.title: Python line discount example
docs.text:
In the Python creation example, build this line first and replace the .add_line_item(...) call with .add_item(line). It produces the same SAR 276 payable amount as the Rust price-per-pack recipe:

from fatoora import Adjustment, LineItemBuilder

line = (
    LineItemBuilder()
    .set_item_name("Notebook")
    .set_invoiced_quantity("25")
    .set_invoiced_quantity_unit_code("PCE")
    .set_item_net_price("100")
    .set_item_price_base_quantity("10")
    .set_vat_category(VatCategory.STANDARD)
    .set_vat_rate("15")
    .add_allowance(Adjustment("10", reason="Volume discount"))
    .build()
)

For a document discount instead, keep the creation example's original line and add this call before .build(). The payable amount becomes SAR 103.50:

    .add_allowance(Adjustment("10", reason="Loyalty discount"),
                   VatCategory.STANDARD, "15")

docs.title: Language reference
docs.text:
Choose your language for callable signatures and lifecycle rules. Argument names correspond to the fields above.

RustPythonJavaScriptC#KotlinJavaC

Create and configure

Import model types from fatoora_core::invoice. InvoiceBuilder::new(invoice_type: InvoiceType) -> InvoiceBuilder accepts InvoiceType::Tax(subtype), Prepayment(subtype), CreditNote(subtype), or DebitNote(subtype). Subtype is InvoiceSubType::Standard or Simplified; add references with .billing_reference(OriginalInvoiceRef::new(id)) and a reason with .payment_instruction(reason). References support OriginalInvoiceRef::new(id) with optional with_uuid(uuid: InvoiceUuid), with_issue_date(date: InvoiceDate) and with_issue_time(time: InvoiceTime).

Every setter consumes and returns Self: chain calls or reassign the result.

Call Returns id(value: impl Into<String>) Self uuid(value: InvoiceUuid) Self issue_datetime(value: InvoiceTimestamp) Self currency(value: CurrencyCode) Self previous_invoice_hash(value: InvoiceHash) Self invoice_counter(value: u64) Self seller(value: Seller) Self buyer(value: Buyer) Self vat_category(value: VatCategory) Self flags(value: InvoiceFlags) Self note(value: InvoiceNote) Self line_item(value: LineItem) Self allowance(value: DocumentAdjustment) Self charge(value: DocumentAdjustment) Self billing_reference(value: OriginalInvoiceRef) Self payment_instruction(value: impl Into<String>) Self payment_means(value: PaymentMeans) Self purchase_order_id(value: impl Into<String>), contract_id(value: impl Into<String>) Self delivery(value: Delivery) Self prepaid_amount(value: Decimal), payable_rounding_amount(value: Decimal) Self tax_currency(currency: CurrencyCode, amount: Decimal) Self tax_exemption(category: VatCategory, rate: Decimal, exemption: TaxExemption) Self vat_breakdown(value: VatBreakdown) Self build(self) Result<FinalizedInvoice, InvoiceError>

payment_means appends a payment means; use .payment_means(PaymentMeans::new(code)) to set the payment means code. Add document-level allowances and charges with .allowance(DocumentAdjustment) and .charge(DocumentAdjustment); DocumentAdjustment carries the amount or percentage calculation, with_reason, with_reason_code, VAT category and rate, with_exemption, and omit_vat_rate() for out-of-scope entries.

To add an existing AllowanceCharge entry, convert it with DocumentAdjustment::from. VatBreakdown::omit_vat_rate omits an out-of-scope subtotal's rate; LineItem, VatBreakdown, AllowanceCharge and DocumentAdjustment all report an omitted rate through has_vat_rate(). The 0.5 aggregate setters and other names deprecated in 0.6 were removed in 0.7; see migrating to 0.7.

build(self) consumes the builder on success or failure. VatCategory variants are Standard, Zero, Exempt, and OutOfScope. Combine InvoiceFlags::THIRD_PARTY, NOMINAL, EXPORT, SUMMARY, and SELF_BILLED with \|.

Supporting values

LineItem::new(description, quantity, unit_code, unit_price, vat_rate, vat_category) takes text values for description/unit code, Decimal for quantities/amounts/rate, and VatCategory; it returns Result<LineItem, InvoiceError>. LineItem::from_totals(...) adds an explicit total_amount after unit price; try_from_parts(...) also adds vat_amount after VAT rate and checks both supplied amounts.

Use CountryCode::parse, CurrencyCode::parse, InvoiceTimestamp::parse, InvoiceDate::parse, InvoiceTime::parse, InvoiceUuid::parse, InvoiceHash::parse, and VatId::parse for validated wrappers; each returns Result<Wrapper, InvoiceError>, and each wrapper also implements FromStr and TryFrom<&str>. With the chrono feature, InvoiceTimestamp and InvoiceDate convert from chrono values via From; with the uuid feature, InvoiceUuid converts from uuid::Uuid. InvoiceNote::new(language, text) returns a note. OtherId::new(value) creates an ID without a scheme; OtherId::with_scheme(value, scheme_id) supplies both.

Construct Address with Address::new(country_code: CountryCode, city, street, building_number, postal_code) (text as impl Into<String>) and add the optional parts with with_additional_street, with_additional_number, with_district and with_province; read them back with the getters of the same names.

TaxExemption, PaymentAccount and Delivery start from Default and take with_* setters (with_reason_code/with_reason, with_payment_account_identifier/with_payment_terms, with_actual_date/with_latest_date); PaymentMeans::new(code) takes with_instruction_note and with_payee_financial_account, and code() returns the code. Line and document adjustments use Adjustment::amount(amount) or Adjustment::percent_of(base, percent) with with_reason, with_reason_code and with_base_amount; DocumentAdjustment::new(adjustment, category, rate) adds with_reason, with_reason_code, with_exemption and with_tax_category_count. Fields are private; each has a getter without a get_ prefix.

Seller::new(name: impl Into<String>, address: Address, vat_id: VatId, other_id: Option<OtherId>) -> Seller requires a VAT ID. Buyer::new(name: impl Into<String>, address: impl Into<Option<Address>>, vat_id: Option<VatId>, other_id: Option<OtherId>) -> Buyer accepts an absent address and identifiers; business validation checks applicability.

LineItem::builder() adds price-base quantities, gross pricing, line allowances and charges. It also accepts supplied amounts and supports item identifiers as well as prepayment references. See pricing recipes for construction examples and model coverage for preservation rules.

Read invoice data

Both invoice types provide data() -> &InvoiceData, totals() -> &InvoiceTotals, and hash() -> Result<InvoiceHash, SigningError>. Read fields through the returned data's accessor methods, including id(), uuid() -> &InvoiceUuid, issue_date() -> InvoiceDate, issue_time() -> InvoiceTime, previous_invoice_hash() -> &InvoiceHash, seller(), buyer(), line_items(), flags(), and invoice_type(). Decimal accessors return Decimal; optional fields return Option.

FinalizedInvoice::sign(self, signer: &InvoiceSigner) -> Result<SignedInvoice, SigningError> consumes the finalized invoice even if signing fails. Signed metadata and XML access are described in signing and XML.

Create and configure

Import from fatoora. Enum values are InvoiceTypeKind.TAX, PREPAYMENT, CREDIT_NOTE, DEBIT_NOTE; InvoiceSubType.STANDARD / SIMPLIFIED; and VatCategory.EXEMPT, STANDARD, ZERO, OUT_OF_SCOPE. Decimal inputs accept decimal.Decimal, a decimal string, or an integer; binary floats are rejected. Timestamps accept a timezone-aware datetime (converted to UTC) or "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ" text; dates accept datetime.date or "YYYY-MM-DD"; UUIDs accept uuid.UUID or text.

InvoiceBuilder(
    invoice_type: InvoiceTypeKind, invoice_subtype: InvoiceSubType, *,
    id: str | None = None, uuid: UUID | str | None = None,
    issue_datetime: datetime | str | None = None, currency: str | None = None,
    previous_invoice_hash: str | None = None, invoice_counter: int | None = None,
    vat_category: VatCategory | None = None, flags: int | InvoiceFlag | None = None,
    original_invoice: OriginalInvoiceRef | None = None,
    original_invoice_reason: str | None = None,
    seller: Party | None = None, buyer: Party | None = None,
)

Pass the header fields as keyword arguments, call the setters, or mix both. Every setter returns the builder, so calls chain: InvoiceBuilder(...).set_seller(...).add_line_item(...).build().

Call Notes set_id(invoice_id: str) set_uuid(uuid: UUID \| str) set_issue_datetime(issue_datetime: datetime \| str) Naive datetime raises ValueError. set_currency(currency_code: str) set_previous_invoice_hash(previous_invoice_hash: str) set_invoice_counter(invoice_counter: int) set_vat_category(vat_category: VatCategory) set_flags(flags: int \| InvoiceFlag) set_seller(party: Party) The seller needs an address and a VAT ID. The first of party.identifiers is the other ID; the rest are additional identifiers. set_seller(name: str, *, vat_id: str, address: Address \| None = None, country_code=..., city=..., street=..., building_number=..., postal_code=..., additional_street=None, additional_number=None, district=None, province=None, other_id=None, other_id_scheme=None) Pass address=Address(...) or the address fields, not both. set_buyer(party: Party) The buyer's address and VAT ID are optional. set_buyer(name: str, *, address: Address \| None = None, vat_id=None, other_id=None, other_id_scheme=None, ...address fields...) As set_seller; vat_id is optional. set_buyer_without_address(name: str, vat_id=None, other_id=None, scheme=None) add_line_item(description: str, quantity, unit_code: str, unit_price, vat_rate, vat_category: VatCategory, *, id=None, exemption=TaxExemption(), document_references=(), tax_subtotals=()) document_references holds OriginalInvoiceRef values. add_item(item: InvoiceLineItem) total_amount and vat_amount are calculated when None and checked when given. add_note(text: str, *, language: str \| None = None) Appends a note. add_payment_means(value: PaymentMeans) Appends a payment means. add_allowance(value: Adjustment, category: VatCategory \| None = None, rate=None, exemption=None) Document-level allowance (discount). Omitted arguments come from the Adjustment. add_charge(value: Adjustment, category: VatCategory \| None = None, rate=None, exemption=None) Document-level charge. add_adjustment(value: Adjustment) Allowance or charge described entirely by the value (charge, category, rate, tax category count, omitted rate), such as one read from invoice.adjustments. add_tax_exemption(category: VatCategory, rate, exemption: TaxExemption) set_delivery(actual: date \| str \| None = None, latest: date \| str \| None = None) build() Returns FinalizedInvoice.

build() consumes the builder's state on success or failure. Rejected setter inputs leave it available for correction. Close owned objects with close() or use a with block; closing a consumed builder is safe.

Read invoice data

FinalizedInvoice and SignedInvoice expose the invoice data as read-only properties:

Property Value id, currency, previous_invoice_hash, payment_means_code str uuid str (core keeps the UUID text verbatim) issue_datetime timezone-aware datetime (UTC) issue_date date issue_time str, HH:MM:SS (AST) or HH:MM:SSZ (UTC) as written invoice_counter, line_item_count, flags_raw int vat_category VatCategory invoice_type_kind / invoice_sub_type InvoiceTypeKind / InvoiceSubType seller / buyer Party / Optional[Party] notes, payment_means, billing_references lists of InvoiceNote, PaymentMeans, OriginalInvoiceRef original_invoice_ref / original_invoice_reason Optional[OriginalInvoiceRef] / Optional[str] actual_delivery_date / latest_delivery_date Optional[date] line_items list[InvoiceLineItem] adjustments / vat_breakdown list[Adjustment] / list[VatBreakdown] totals InvoiceTotals flags set[InvoiceFlag] xml str

Methods: line_item(index: int) -> InvoiceLineItem, hash() -> str (recomputes the base64 invoice hash), and the queries is_third_party(), is_nominal(), is_export(), is_summary(), is_self_billed() and is_simplified().

The invoice data is read from the native invoice once, on first access, and cached; invoices do not change after build() or parsing.

Value models

Everything read from an invoice is a frozen dataclass: compare values with ==, copy them with dataclasses.replace, and pass them back to the builder. They need no close(). Optional fields are None when absent.

Model Fields Party(name, address=None, vat_id=None, identifiers=()) vat_id and identifiers hold Identifier values (strings are accepted as input); other_id is the first identifier. Identifier(value, scheme=None) An identifier and its schemeID, such as Identifier("7003339333", "CRN"). Address(country_code, city, street, building_number, postal_code, additional_street=None, additional_number=None, district=None, province=None) Validated on construction; the country code becomes ISO alpha-3 ("SA" reads back as "SAU"). InvoiceNote(text, language_id=None) language is language_id or "en". OriginalInvoiceRef(id, uuid=None, issue_date=None, issue_time=None, document_type_code=None) Billing references and line document references. issue_date is a date. PaymentMeans(code, instruction_notes=(), account_identifier=None, payment_terms=None) with_instruction_note(note) and with_account(id, terms) return copies. Adjustment(amount, reason=None, reason_code=None, base_amount=None, percentage=None, charge=False, category=None, rate=None, exemption=TaxExemption(), tax_category_count=1, omitted_rate=False) Adjustment.percent_of(base, percent, **fields) calculates amount. Line adjustments read back with their line's category and rate. InvoiceLineItem(description, unit_code, quantity, unit_price, total_amount=None, vat_rate, vat_amount=None, vat_category, ...) vat_rate and vat_category are required; pass them by keyword when you leave out total_amount.

FinalizedInvoice.sign(signer: InvoiceSigner) -> SignedInvoice consumes the finalized invoice on success or signing failure; the signer remains reusable. See signing for metadata and XML for serialization.

The 0.5 names that 0.6 deprecated (InvoiceBuilder.new, the aggregate setters set_allowance, invoice_level_discount, invoice_level_charge and allowance_reason, AllowanceCharge, DocumentReference, VatId/OtherId and others) were removed in 0.7; see migrating to 0.7.

Import from fatoority. All decimal arguments and amounts are strings; counters use bigint, indexes and the flag mask use number, and codes are enum classes. Pass null for absent optional arguments. Operations are synchronous and throw a FatooraError subclass on failure. Value getters are read-only properties (data.id, totals.taxAmount) and optional text is string | null; getters returning native objects (seller(), lineItem(index)) stay methods.

Enums: InvoiceTypeKind (Tax, Prepayment, CreditNote, DebitNote), InvoiceSubType (Standard, Simplified), and VatCategory (Exempt, Standard, Zero, OutOfScope); pass them as InvoiceTypeKind.Tax, VatCategory.Standard, and so on. A returned enum's .value is the variant name, such as 'Standard'. Flags remain a number bitmask; build it from InvoiceFlag bits, for example InvoiceFlag.Export.bit | InvoiceFlag.Summary.bit (1 third party, 2 nominal, 4 export, 8 summary, 16 self-billed). Use zero for no flags.

Create and configure

Call Returns create(kind: InvoiceTypeKind, subtype: InvoiceSubType, originalId, originalUuid, originalDate, reason) InvoiceBuilder setId(value) void setUuid(value) void setIssueDatetime(value) void setCurrency(value) void setPreviousInvoiceHash(value) void addPaymentMeans(payment) void setInvoiceCounter(value) void setVatCategory(value: VatCategory) void setFlags(value) void addNote(language, value) void setSeller(name, address, vatId, otherId, scheme) void setBuyer(name, address, vatId, otherId, scheme) void addLineItem(description, quantity, unitCode, unitPrice, vatRate, category: VatCategory) void build() FinalizedInvoice

Address inputs

Call Returns create(countryCode, city, street, buildingNumber, postalCode, additionalStreet, additionalNumber, district) Address

Setters replace values; line-item calls append. Building consumes builder state even on validation failure. Signing through the signer consumes finalized invoice state. Further calls on consumed state fail.

Read invoice data

invoice.data() returns an owned InvoiceData snapshot; invoice.totals() returns owned InvoiceTotals. Both are independent of invoice state.

Member Value id string uuid string previousInvoiceHash string paymentMeansCode string currency string issueDatetime string invoiceLevelCharge string invoiceLevelDiscount string allowanceReason string \| null invoiceCounter bigint vatCategory VatCategory flags number invoiceTypeKind InvoiceTypeKind invoiceSubType InvoiceSubType seller() Party buyer() Party \| null note() InvoiceNote \| null lineItemsLen number lineItem(index) InvoiceLineItem originalInvoiceRef() OriginalInvoiceRef \| null originalInvoiceReason string \| null

Totals

Property Value taxInclusive string taxAmount string lineExtension string allowanceTotal string chargeTotal string taxableAmount string prepaidAmount string payableRoundingAmount string payableAmount string

Optional object accessors return null when absent. Line-item objects provide description, quantity, unit code, unit price, total amount, VAT rate, VAT amount, and category. See XML and signing for document and signature operations.

Use the Fatoora namespace. Quantities, prices, rates and amounts are decimal in both directions; counters use ulong, indexes use nuint, codes use C# enums, and the flag mask uses byte. Pass null for absent optional arguments. Members throw on failure. Scalar getters are read-only properties and optional text is string?; getters returning owned objects stay methods. Dispose each owned object with using.

Enums: InvoiceTypeKind (Tax, Prepayment, CreditNote, DebitNote), InvoiceSubType (Standard, Simplified), and VatCategory (Exempt, Standard, Zero, OutOfScope); pass them as InvoiceTypeKind.Tax, VatCategory.Standard, and so on. Flags remain a byte bitmask; build it by casting InvoiceFlag values, for example (byte)(InvoiceFlag.Export | InvoiceFlag.Summary) (1 third party, 2 nominal, 4 export, 8 summary, 16 self-billed). Use zero for no flags.

Create and configure

Call Returns New(InvoiceTypeKind kind, InvoiceSubType subtype, string? originalId, string? originalUuid, string? originalDate, string? reason) InvoiceBuilder SetId(string value) void SetUuid(string value) void SetIssueDatetime(string value) void SetCurrency(string value) void SetPreviousInvoiceHash(string value) void AddPaymentMeans(PaymentMeans payment) void SetInvoiceCounter(ulong value) void SetVatCategory(VatCategory value) void SetFlags(byte value) void AddNote(string? language, string value) void SetSeller(string name, Address address, string vatId, string? otherId, string? scheme) void SetBuyer(string name, Address address, string? vatId, string? otherId, string? scheme) void AddLineItem(string description, decimal quantity, string unitCode, decimal unitPrice, decimal vatRate, VatCategory category) void Build() FinalizedInvoice

Address inputs

Setters replace values; line-item calls append. Building consumes builder state even on validation failure. Signing through the signer consumes finalized invoice state. Further calls on consumed state fail.

Read invoice data

invoice.Data() returns an owned InvoiceData snapshot; invoice.Totals() returns owned InvoiceTotals. Both survive disposal of the invoice.

Member Returns Id string Uuid string PreviousInvoiceHash string PaymentMeansCode string Currency string IssueDatetime string InvoiceLevelCharge decimal InvoiceLevelDiscount decimal AllowanceReason string? InvoiceCounter ulong VatCategory VatCategory Flags byte InvoiceTypeKind InvoiceTypeKind InvoiceSubType InvoiceSubType Seller() Party Buyer() Party? Note() InvoiceNote? LineItemsLen nuint LineItem(nuint index) InvoiceLineItem OriginalInvoiceRef() OriginalInvoiceRef? OriginalInvoiceReason string?

Totals

All totals are decimal properties: TaxInclusive, TaxAmount, LineExtension, AllowanceTotal, ChargeTotal, TaxableAmount, PrepaidAmount, PayableRoundingAmount and PayableAmount.

Optional object accessors return null when absent. Line-item objects provide description, quantity, unit code, unit price, total amount, VAT rate, VAT amount, and category. See XML and signing for document and signature operations.

Use com.fatoora. Quantities, prices, rates and amounts are exact java.math.BigDecimal values; counters and indexes use java.math.BigInteger, codes use com.fatoora enums, and the flag mask uses Int. Optional values are nullable. Getters that return copied values are properties; getters that return native owners stay methods. Methods throw on failure. Close owned objects with use.

Enums: InvoiceTypeKind (Tax, Prepayment, CreditNote, DebitNote), InvoiceSubType (Standard, Simplified), and VatCategory (Exempt, Standard, Zero, OutOfScope) in com.fatoora; pass them as InvoiceTypeKind.Tax, VatCategory.Standard, and so on. Flags remain an Int bitmask; build it from InvoiceFlag bits, for example InvoiceFlag.Export.bit or InvoiceFlag.Summary.bit (1 third party, 2 nominal, 4 export, 8 summary, 16 self-billed). Use zero for no flags.

Create and configure

Use XML for serialization and signing for consuming signing operations and metadata.

docs.title: Invoice signing reference
docs.text: Create a signer from an X.509 certificate and an unencrypted secp256k1 private key in PKCS#8 format. Use it to sign a finalized invoice or existing XML. For a complete workflow, see the signing guide.

docs.title: Inputs and behavior
docs.text:
Operation Expected input Result and behavior Create from PEM Certificate PEM and private-key PEM text A reusable signer; rejects invalid certificate/key encodings Create from DER Certificate DER bytes and private-key PKCS#8 DER bytes A reusable signer with the same behavior as PEM construction Export certificate Live signer Certificate as PEM text or DER bytes Sign finalized invoice A finalized invoice and a live signer A signed invoice; consumes the finalized invoice's state Sign existing XML UBL invoice XML text Signed XML text; preserves bytes outside the signing structures it owns. Re-signing requires the same certificate Hash existing XML XML text Base64 invoice digest after invoice-specific exclusions and canonicalization

Signer construction parses the certificate and key; it does not establish that they match, that the certificate is trusted, or that its dates are valid. Signing checks that the private key matches the certificate and rejects a mismatch. It does not run the complete invoice validator. Validate the resulting XML separately when you need a local compliance report.

Keep signed XML unchanged for storage and submission. Signing existing XML does not construct an invoice model or run all model-import checks.

docs.title: Signed invoice values
docs.text:
All getters below leave the signed invoice usable. Signed imports verify local signature and QR consistency with the embedded certificate; certificate trust and clearance remain separate.

Value Returned content XML Original stored signed XML text XML Base64 Base64 of that stored XML text QR code Base64 TLV payload for rendering; see QR reference Invoice hash Embedded invoice digest from signature metadata Computed hash hash() recomputes the digest of the stored signed XML using ZATCA exclusions Signature Encoded invoice signature Public key Encoded public-key material ZATCA key signature Optional encoded certificate-signature material Issuer / serial Certificate issuer and serial from signed properties Certificate hash Encoded certificate digest Signed properties hash Encoded signed-properties digest Signing time UTC text in YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS format

The signed computed hash equals the XML hash operation on xml(). Signed imports reject altered digests, signatures and inconsistent QR data. Local integrity checks do not establish certificate issuer trust. See XML reference for parsing and consuming XML access.

docs.title: Methods by language
Invoice validation
docs.text: Validate the original invoice XML before relying on its structure or business-rule results. Choose a schema check for UBL structure, or a local ZATCA report for schema, business rules, and applicable integrity checks. For a runnable example, see the validation guide.

docs.title: Choose the check
docs.text:
Operation What it establishes Build an invoice Implemented field, range, and amount checks; calculated totals. Parse invoice XML Supported fields and supplied amounts can be represented by the invoice model. Validate the schema Conformance to the bundled UBL 2.1 schema. Run local ZATCA validation Results and coverage for the local profile's schema, business rules, signature, QR, and predecessor checks. Sign an invoice Signature material was generated; no implicit business-rule validation. Parse a signed invoice Signature material was extracted; no implicit authenticity check.

No local result proves remote acceptance, certificate issuer trust, or revocation status. Integrity checks verify supported algorithms and references, bind the embedded key to the signature, and compare QR data with the invoice and certificate.

docs.title: Inputs and options
docs.text:
All checks take complete invoice XML text and a configuration object. Pass original XML, not Base64 or a file path. Schema checks use bundled resources and do not need network access. Malformed XML is rejected rather than repaired.

Local validation additionally accepts these optional context values:

Option Expected value If omitted previous_invoice_hash Canonical Base64 SHA-256 digest, or the SDK's Base64-encoded hexadecimal digest representation. This is the expected predecessor hash, compared with the invoice's PIH. Predecessor stage reports context_required; the report is incomplete and is_valid is false. evaluated_at RFC3339 instant with timezone, such as 2026-10-15T09:30:00Z or 2026-10-15T12:30:00+03:00. One clock snapshot is used for the validation run.

The validator cannot obtain invoice history. Supply predecessor context from your own invoice sequence. An empty string is not an omitted option. APIs that accept options as JSON require an object containing only these keys, with string or null values. The encoded options input is limited to 4 KiB (4096 bytes); unknown keys and malformed values are rejected.

docs.title: Local ZATCA report
docs.text:
A completed function call means a report was produced. Always inspect is_valid; rejected invoices and incomplete coverage can both be returned without an execution error.

Report field Value and meaning schema_version Report format version, currently 1. profile Local validation profile identifier, currently zatca-sdk-238-R3.4.8. evaluated_at The evaluation clock snapshot, including offset. stages Ordered stage results: xsd, cen, ksa, signature, qr, previous_invoice_hash. is_complete All required stages completed exactly once; explicitly inapplicable signature/QR stages count as covered. has_errors At least one error finding exists, including findings from partial stages. is_valid Complete coverage with no error findings. Warnings do not make this false.

Each stage contains stage, status, findings, evaluated_assertions (the assertion sites evaluated), and optional provenance with source stylesheet and sha256. Provenance identifies the rules used; applications can retain it alongside reports for traceability.

Stage Checks xsd Bundled UBL XML structure. cen Applicable European invoice business rules in the selected profile. ksa Applicable Saudi invoice business rules in the selected profile. signature Local signature integrity; skipped as inapplicable for standard invoices under this profile. qr QR integrity and consistency; skipped as inapplicable for standard invoices under this profile. previous_invoice_hash Invoice PIH compared with supplied predecessor context. Stage status Meaning completed Checks finished; findings may still contain errors. not_run A dependency failed or execution stopped earlier. not_applicable The selected profile does not require this stage for this invoice. context_required Required predecessor context was not supplied. evaluation_failed Execution stopped before completion; findings may be partial.

Schema rejection returns a report and skips dependent stages. A report with no findings is not sufficient by itself: it can be incomplete. For example, missing predecessor context can yield has_errors: false, is_complete: false, and is_valid: false.

docs.title: Findings
docs.text:
Finding field Meaning layer field_checks, xsd, business_rules, signature, qr, or previous_invoice_hash. code Stable rule or library identifier; use this for programmatic handling. severity warning or error. message Human-readable explanation. Wording is not a stable API. location Optional model field path, XPath, or XML source coordinates. assertion_site Optional source assertion identifier on local ZATCA findings.

Field paths use zero-based indexes, such as line_items[0].quantity. XML line and column positions are one-based. Business-rule findings use XPath locations against the original document; some findings have no reliable location.

Field codes include FIELD_REQUIRED, FIELD_EMPTY, FIELD_INVALID_FORMAT, FIELD_OUT_OF_RANGE, and FIELD_MISMATCH. Schema violations use XSD_INVALID. Business-rule findings use their implemented rule codes.

docs.title: Execution failures and partial results
docs.text:
An invalid invoice is different from a check that could not finish. Malformed XML, unsupported DTDs, capacity limits, invalid context, and rule/integrity execution failures produce an error. When validation has started, the error carries the partial report and all findings collected so far.

Execution details include kind, optional stage, assertion_site, location, and report. The error message is exposed directly or in diagnostics, depending on the language API. Failure kinds are invalid_xml, unsupported_xml, capacity_exceeded, invalid_context, rule_evaluation, schema, and integrity. Invalid options rejected before validation starts need not carry a report. Never treat partial findings as complete coverage. See errors for the shared error contract.

docs.title: Report object in the generated bindings
docs.text:
JavaScript, C#, Kotlin, Java, and C return an owned ZatcaValidationReport that mirrors the Rust report. Python keeps returning the JSON dictionary.

Object Accessors ZatcaValidationReport schema_version, profile, evaluated_at, is_complete, has_errors, is_valid, stages_len, stage(index), and to_json for the JSON report above ZatcaStageReport stage (ZatcaStage), status (ZatcaStageStatus), nullable provenance, evaluated_assertions_len, evaluated_assertion(index), findings_len, finding(index) ZatcaRuleSource stylesheet, sha256 ZatcaFinding nullable assertion_site, layer (ValidationLayer), code, severity (Severity), message, nullable location_kind (ValidationLocationKind: Field, XPath, Xml), nullable location_path for field and XPath locations, nullable location_line and location_column for XML coordinates

Names follow each language's convention (the C# IsValid property, fatoora_zatca_validation_report_is_valid); Kotlin and the JavaScript fatoority/raw report expose the zero-argument value accessors as properties (report.isValid, stage.status), which Java reads as isValid() and getStatus(). Stage, status, and layer enums carry an Unknown variant for values added by a later core version. Child objects are independent snapshots and outlive the report.

docs.title: Language reference
Decimal numbers and rounding
docs.text: Use decimal strings or integers for invoice amounts. Parsing never silently rounds an input.

docs.title: Representation
docs.text:
Accepted syntax is [+-]digits[.digits], using ASCII digits. Whitespace, exponents, separators, infinities and NaN are rejected. Parsing never rounds. The range is a signed 96-bit coefficient with a scale from 0 through 28. Values outside that range fail with an out-of-range error.

Equality compares numeric values: 1.0 equals 1.00. Display and JSON use canonical decimal strings, without exponents or unnecessary trailing zeros. Negative zero is displayed as 0. XML monetary fields use two decimal places; quantities and unit prices retain their supported precision.

Arithmetic is checked. Values outside the supported decimal range return an error. Price-base division uses integer rational arithmetic until rounding, so a non-terminating per-unit price does not lose precision before the line calculation.

docs.title: Calculation boundaries
docs.text:
• Line net: round quantity × net price / price base to cents, subtract line allowances, and add line charges. The default price base is one.
