  • Calculated line VAT: round the accepted line net × rate / 100 to cents. Supplied line VAT is retained after its precision and amount checks.
  • Line gross: accepted line net plus accepted line VAT.
  • Group taxable amount: sum accepted line nets by VAT category and rate, subtract that group's document allowances, and add its document charges.
  • Calculated category VAT: round the group's taxable amount × rate / 100 to cents. Document VAT is the sum of accepted category taxes.
  • Payable: tax-inclusive amount minus prepaid amount plus signed payable rounding.

Default calculated amounts use half-up rounding. For three lines of 0.03 at 15%, each calculated line VAT is 0.00, while document VAT is 0.01. XML output and QR payloads use the accepted totals without recalculating them.

Rates must be between 0 and 100 with at most two decimal places. Categories other than standard require a zero rate. Supplied monetary totals must already have at most two decimal places. Negative line quantities, prices, discounts, and charges are rejected; credit notes use positive amounts with the appropriate document type. Payable rounding can be signed. Price bases must be positive.

Use Adjustment::amount or Adjustment::percent_of for line adjustments, and DocumentAdjustment for invoice adjustments with independent VAT categories and rates. Scalar invoice discount/charge setters require an unambiguous VAT group; combining them with independent adjustment entries is rejected. See pricing recipes for examples.

docs.title: Calculated and supplied values
docs.text:
The model checks supplied amounts and retains accepted values. A mismatch reports both the expected and supplied amounts. Acceptance depends on the field:

Supplied value Check Net price Exact agreement with gross price minus price discount, when both are supplied. Line net Within 0.01 of the calculated line net. Line gross Exact sum of accepted line net and line VAT. Adjustment amount and percentage Exact agreement with the rounded base × percentage / 100 calculation. Standard-category breakdown tax Within invoice-line count × 0.01 of the half-even rounded exact tax calculation. Other category tax Zero. Document VAT and totals Consistent with accepted breakdowns and the document total equations.

Default construction and supplied-tax tolerance checks use different rounding rules. For example, 53.30 at 5% produces 2.67 during construction. The standard-category supplied-tax check centers its tolerance on 2.66; with one invoice line, it accepts 2.65 through 2.67.

Prepayment adjustment lines contribute their taxable and tax subtotals to the prepaid amount, without increasing ordinary taxable sales. Imported XML also preserves supported optional-amount presence, including payable rounding.

These checks are separate from schema and business-rule validation. The model contract documents the field dependencies and differences between the published standard and the pinned SDK's executable rules. Run local validation for that rule profile.

docs.title: Values in your language
docs.text:
RustPythonJavaScriptC#KotlinJavaC

fatoora_core::Decimal accepts decimal strings through parse() and integers through Decimal::from. Parsing returns DecimalError on invalid syntax or range. Numeric getters return Decimal.

let price: fatoora_core::Decimal = "0.3333".parse()?;

Inputs accept decimal.Decimal, str, or int. Both float and bool are rejected. Numeric getters return decimal.Decimal.

from decimal import Decimal
price = Decimal("0.3333")

Pass quantities, prices, rates and amounts as decimal strings, such as "0.3333". Numeric getters return strings. Avoid converting financial values to Number, which can lose precision.

Pass quantities, prices, rates and amounts as decimal, such as 0.3333m; numeric getters return decimal (or decimal? when optional). The binding converts with the invariant culture, never through double, so values cross the boundary exactly. Returned values are normalized: 1.50m comes back as 1.5m, which compares equal.

Pass quantities, prices, rates and amounts as java.math.BigDecimal; amount getters return BigDecimal. Conversion is exact: the binding sends toPlainString() and parses results with BigDecimal(String), so no digits are lost. Compare values with compareTo, since returned values are normalized (10.50 reads back as 10.5).

Pass quantities, prices, rates and amounts as java.math.BigDecimal; amount getters return BigDecimal. Conversion is exact: the binding sends toPlainString() and parses results with BigDecimal(String), so no digits are lost. Compare values with compareTo, since returned values are normalized (10.50 reads back as 10.5).

Inputs are NUL-terminated UTF-8 decimal strings, such as "0.3333". Numeric getters return owned text through char **out; release it with fatoora_string_free(). Check the returned FatooraStatus before reading the output.

docs.title: QR payloads
docs.text: Signing generates a Base64-encoded TLV payload for the invoice. Pass this text to a QR image renderer to display or print it; the library returns text, not a PNG or SVG.

docs.title: Payload contract
docs.text:
Value Meaning Tags 1–5 Seller name, VAT registration number, timestamp, total including VAT and VAT total Tags 6–8 Invoice hash, signature and public key for stamped phase-two documents Tag 9 Certificate signature bytes; required for simplified invoices and their notes, prohibited on standard documents Individual field size At most 255 bytes per field; text uses UTF-8 and Arabic characters can occupy multiple bytes Encoded size At most 700 Base64 characters during generation

SignedInvoice::qr_code() returns the exact Base64 text embedded in xml(). Signing and signed imports check QR structure, values and local signature integrity. Imports retain the supplied XML byte for byte. They reject mismatches instead of regenerating QR data.

Typed signing serializes the model first, then constructs QR fields from that XML. XML signing reads Tag 4 from LegalMonetaryTotal/PayableAmount (BT-115) and Tag 5 from the first document-level TaxTotal/TaxAmount in the document currency (BT-110). XML scalar values lose only surrounding XML whitespace (space, tab, CR, LF). Seller names retain their text. Decimal spellings such as 300, 300.0 and 300.00 are preserved during construction. Both money fields use bounded exact XML-decimal comparison. The SDK validation profile additionally requires Tag 4's XML spelling to match, as observed in both the pinned SDK and development API. Signed import checks monetary integrity and retains the supplied payload; run full validation for formatting, amount scale and business rules.

Standard invoices receive their clearance stamp from ZATCA. A locally generated standard stamp is useful for SDK testing and submission preparation; it proves no clearance. Imports use the supplied document's signature and certificate, regardless of who created it. The supported standard stamp representation contains Tags 1–8; simplified stamps contain Tags 1–9. Unstamped CLI QR output contains only Tags 1–5 and is not a complete phase-two stamp.

The decoder enforces ascending, unique, nonempty tags, valid TLV framing, 255 bytes per field and 700 Base64 characters. Signature material must be valid Base64. Certificate signature metadata remains available on standard invoices even though Tag 9 is absent. Certificate issuer trust, revocation and gateway acceptance require separate evidence. The SDK validation profile continues to skip standard-invoice QR and signature checks. See SDK compatibility.

docs.title: Read the payload
docs.text:
The getter takes no arguments and leaves the signed invoice usable.

RustPythonJavaScriptC#KotlinJavaC

SignedInvoice::qr_code(&self) -> &str borrows the payload from the invoice. Copy with .to_owned() to keep it after dropping the invoice.

The SignedInvoice.qr_code property is an independent str.

The SignedInvoice.qrCode property is a string.

The SignedInvoice.QrCode property returns a managed string.

The SignedInvoice.qrCode property is a managed String.

SignedInvoice.getQrCode() returns a String.

fatoora_signed_invoice_qr_code(invoice, &out, &error) returns FatooraStatus. invoice is a live const FatooraSignedInvoice *; out is an owned char *. On success, release the payload with fatoora_string_free(out). Release any error with fatoora_error_free(error).

For a complete rendering workflow, see the QR guide.

docs.title: XML and schemas
docs.text: The library reads and writes UBL invoice XML and includes the UBL 2.1 invoice schema. Validation uses bundled resources and does not download schemas from locations supplied by an invoice. No SDK installation or network access is needed.

docs.title: Choose an operation
docs.text: Operation Input Result and guarantee Parse XML Invoice XML text A supported invoice model with field and amount checks; not a complete compliance check Validate the schema Original XML and configuration Checks element structure, attributes and schema types Validate locally Original XML, configuration and predecessor context A report covering schema, business rules and applicable integrity checks Hash XML Original XML text Base64 invoice digest after invoice-specific exclusions and canonicalization Sign XML XML, certificate and private key Signed XML; signing alone does not establish compliance

docs.title: Decimal values
docs.text:
The bundled schema's amount, measure, numeric and quantity fields accept XML decimal syntax without imposing a machine floating-point range. This preserves schema validation for large decimal values. An extension that directly uses xs:decimal can still encounter the schema engine's numeric capacity limit.

Invoice-model calculations and business-rule validation have separate precision and capacity limits. Passing schema validation does not mean a value can be calculated by the model. See decimal numbers and rounding.

docs.title: Hashing and signed XML
docs.text:
Invoice hashing applies the invoice-specific exclusions and C14N 1.1 canonicalization before calculating the digest. It is not a hash of the raw file bytes. Keep the returned signed XML unchanged when storing or submitting it: formatting or rebuilding it can change signature-relevant content.

Parsing a signed invoice preserves its XML and embedded QR, and verifies local signature and digest consistency. Certificate issuer trust and remote acceptance are outside these checks. Use the validation report to determine which checks actually completed.

docs.title: Invoice XML
docs.text: Use these APIs to read invoice XML into an invoice model, serialize a finalized invoice, or retrieve the exact XML stored by a signed invoice. For a walkthrough, see invoice signing or validation.

docs.title: Choose an operation
docs.text:
Operation Input Result and behavior Parse finalized invoice Complete invoice XML text or a file path A finalized invoice with supported fields and calculated totals. Supplied supported amounts are checked against calculations. Parse signed invoice Complete signed invoice XML text or a file path A signed invoice containing signature metadata and the exact supplied XML text. Parsing checks the signature, digests and QR against the embedded certificate; issuer trust and clearance remain unverified. Serialize finalized invoice Finalized invoice XML text with default two-space indentation. Serialization creates a document from the model; it is not a lossless XML editor. Read signed XML Signed invoice Exact stored XML, without formatting changes. Newly signed invoices store the output of signing; imported invoices store the input text. Take signed XML Signed invoice Exact stored XML and consumption of the invoice state. Encode signed XML Signed invoice Base64 of the stored XML, suitable for APIs that require encoded invoice content.

Text inputs contain XML, not Base64 or a filename. File variants take a local filesystem path and read its contents as text. Parsing can fail on malformed XML, unsupported or missing required fields, or inconsistent supplied amounts. File operations can also fail when the path cannot be read.

Parsing and serialization do not establish schema conformance, business-rule compliance, or invoice acceptance. Run validation explicitly when needed.

docs.title: Preserve signed XML
docs.text: Keep returned signed XML unchanged when saving or submitting it. Do not pretty-print, normalize whitespace, or reconstruct it from invoice data. Reading metadata does not change the stored XML. For edits followed by signing, see invoice signing.

docs.title: Language reference
docs.text:
Choose your language for imports, exact calls, returns, and ownership behavior.

RustPythonJavaScriptC#KotlinJavaC

Import parsing functions from fatoora_core::invoice::xml::parse and XmlFormat from fatoora_core::invoice::xml.

Parse XML

parse_finalized_invoice_xml(xml: &str) -> Result<FinalizedInvoice, ParseError>
parse_finalized_invoice_xml_file(path: impl AsRef<Path>) -> Result<FinalizedInvoice, ParseError>
parse_signed_invoice_xml(xml: &str) -> Result<SignedInvoice, ParseError>
parse_signed_invoice_xml_file(path: impl AsRef<Path>) -> Result<SignedInvoice, ParseError>

Serialize finalized invoices

FinalizedInvoice::to_xml(&self) -> Result<String, InvoiceXmlError>
FinalizedInvoice::to_xml_with_format(&self, format: XmlFormat) -> Result<String, InvoiceXmlError>

to_xml() uses two spaces of indentation. Choose XmlFormat::Compact for compact output or XmlFormat::Pretty { indent_char: ' ', indent_size: 4 } for explicit indentation. These are inherent methods; no serialization trait import is needed. They borrow the invoice and return a new owned string.

Read signed invoices

SignedInvoice::xml(&self) -> &str
SignedInvoice::into_xml(self) -> String
SignedInvoice::to_xml_base64(&self) -> String

xml() borrows stored XML for the invoice's lifetime. into_xml() consumes the invoice and transfers the stored string without copying. to_xml_base64() returns a new string and leaves the invoice available. Signed invoices have no formatting methods.

Import these functions and invoice types from fatoora.

Parse XML

FinalizedInvoice.from_xml(xml: str) -> FinalizedInvoice
FinalizedInvoice.from_file(path: str | os.PathLike) -> FinalizedInvoice
SignedInvoice.from_xml(xml: str) -> SignedInvoice
SignedInvoice.from_file(path: str | os.PathLike) -> SignedInvoice

Read XML

invoice.xml                       # property: str
signed.to_xml_base64() -> str

Finalized output uses the default formatting; signed output preserves stored text. String results are independent Python strings and reading them leaves state available. Use context managers or close() for owned objects. Errors raise exceptions; see errors.

Import FinalizedInvoice and SignedInvoice from fatoority. These operations are synchronous and throw a FatooraError subclass on failure.

const finalized = FinalizedInvoice.fromXml(xml);
const signed = SignedInvoice.fromXml(signedXml);
const unsignedText = finalized.xml;
const signedText = signed.xml;
const encoded = signed.toXmlBase64();
const takenText = signed.intoXml();

Both fromXml methods expect a string and return their named invoice object. The xml property and the XML methods are strings. intoXml() consumes the signed invoice state; subsequent access fails. Reading xml or calling toXmlBase64() leaves it available. Read a file using your host environment before passing its text to fromXml; filesystem parsing methods are not exposed in this binding. Finalized formatting is fixed to the default; signed output is exact stored text.

Use Fatoora. Methods throw on failure. Use using to dispose owned invoice objects.

FinalizedInvoice FinalizedInvoice.FromXml(string value)
FinalizedInvoice FinalizedInvoice.FromFile(string value)
SignedInvoice SignedInvoice.FromXml(string value)
SignedInvoice SignedInvoice.FromFile(string value)
string FinalizedInvoice.Xml { get; }
string SignedInvoice.Xml { get; }
string SignedInvoice.IntoXml()
string SignedInvoice.ToXmlBase64()

FromFile takes a local path. Returned strings are independent managed values. IntoXml() consumes invoice state, so further reads fail; disposal remains safe. Other accessors preserve the object. Finalized formatting uses two-space indentation; signed output is exact stored text.

Import com.fatoora.FinalizedInvoice and com.fatoora.SignedInvoice. Methods throw on failure. Close invoice objects with use.

FinalizedInvoice.fromXml(value: String): FinalizedInvoice
FinalizedInvoice.fromFile(value: String): FinalizedInvoice
SignedInvoice.fromXml(value: String): SignedInvoice
SignedInvoice.fromFile(value: String): SignedInvoice
FinalizedInvoice.xml: String
SignedInvoice.xml: String
SignedInvoice.intoXml(): String
SignedInvoice.toXmlBase64(): String

fromFile takes a local path. XML results are independent strings. intoXml() consumes invoice state; later access fails and close() remains safe. Reading xml or toXmlBase64() leaves the invoice available. Finalized output uses default two-space indentation; signed output is exact stored text.

Import com.fatoora.FinalizedInvoice and com.fatoora.SignedInvoice. Use try-with-resources to close invoice objects; methods throw on failure.

FinalizedInvoice FinalizedInvoice.fromXml(String value)
FinalizedInvoice FinalizedInvoice.fromFile(String value)
SignedInvoice SignedInvoice.fromXml(String value)
SignedInvoice SignedInvoice.fromFile(String value)
String FinalizedInvoice.getXml()
String SignedInvoice.getXml()
String SignedInvoice.intoXml()
String SignedInvoice.toXmlBase64()

Static fromFile methods take a local path. String results remain valid after the invoice is closed. intoXml() consumes signed state; later access fails, and closing remains safe. The other accessors preserve state. Finalized output uses two-space indentation; signed output is exact stored text.

Include fatoora.h. All calls below return FatooraStatus and take FatooraError **error as their final argument. Check status before reading an output; free any returned error with fatoora_error_free().

Parse XML

FatooraStatus fatoora_finalized_invoice_from_xml(const char *value,
    FatooraFinalizedInvoice **out, FatooraError **error);
FatooraStatus fatoora_finalized_invoice_from_file(const char *value,
    FatooraFinalizedInvoice **out, FatooraError **error);
FatooraStatus fatoora_signed_invoice_from_xml(const char *value,
    FatooraSignedInvoice **out, FatooraError **error);
FatooraStatus fatoora_signed_invoice_from_file(const char *value,
    FatooraSignedInvoice **out, FatooraError **error);

value is a NUL-terminated UTF-8 XML string for _from_xml, or a local path for _from_file. Returned invoice handles are owned; release them with fatoora_finalized_invoice_free() or fatoora_signed_invoice_free().

Read XML

FatooraStatus fatoora_finalized_invoice_xml(const FatooraFinalizedInvoice *self,
    char **out, FatooraError **error);
FatooraStatus fatoora_signed_invoice_xml(const FatooraSignedInvoice *self,
    char **out, FatooraError **error);
FatooraStatus fatoora_signed_invoice_into_xml(FatooraSignedInvoice *self,
    char **out, FatooraError **error);
FatooraStatus fatoora_signed_invoice_to_xml_base64(const FatooraSignedInvoice *self,
    char **out, FatooraError **error);

Each output is owned NUL-terminated text; release it with fatoora_string_free(). _xml copies the result and preserves invoice state. _into_xml consumes signed invoice state; further reads fail, but the outer handle must still be freed. _to_xml_base64 returns encoded text without consuming state. Finalized formatting uses two-space indentation; signed output is never reformatted.

See the model preservation contract for supported fields, normalization, rejected structures, and the boundary between model serialization and original signed XML preservation.

docs.title: C and C++ bindings
docs.text:
Use the native library to create CSRs, build and sign invoices, validate XML and call the ZATCA API. Headers and the shared library must come from the same release. Download them from the release assets.

Configure your runtime loader to find the shared library: .so on Linux, .dylib on macOS, or the DLL on Windows. Select your language for its include paths, return values and cleanup rules.

CC++

Include one header, check the shared status, and release returned owners. Passing NULL as the error argument is supported when only the status matters. The deliberately incomplete invoice below fails validation.

#include "fatoora.h"
#include <stdio.h>

int main(void) {
    FatooraError *error = NULL;
    bool valid = false;
    FatooraStatus status = fatoora_xml_validate("<Invoice></Invoice>", &valid, &error);
    if (status == FATOORA_OK) printf("valid: %s\n", valid ? "true" : "false");
    else fprintf(stderr, "error %d: %s\n", (int)status, fatoora_error_message(error));
    fatoora_error_free(error);
    return status == FATOORA_OK && valid ? 0 : 1;
}

String getters return owned char * values through output pointers; release them with fatoora_string_free(). Optional text returns NULL for absence and an allocated empty string for a present empty value. Decimal values are exact strings. Constructors and line items use named-field option structs. See the complete builder example and the ownership rules below.

Compile and link

Use matching headers and native libraries from the same release. Compile bindings/c/fatoora.c once alongside your application, include bindings/c, and link fatoora_ffi:

cc -std=c11 validate.c bindings/c/fatoora.c \
  -Ibindings/c -L/path/to/native-library -lfatoora_ffi -o validate

Release archives use include/fatoora.h, src/fatoora.c and include/generated/. Compile the archive's src/fatoora.c with -Iinclude and link the matching native library. If your application is C++, compile this adapter as C, then link the object into your application.

Values and ownership

Value Contract Text input Borrowed NUL-terminated UTF-8 for the duration of the call Optional text input NULL means absent; "" is present empty text Decimal input Exact decimal string; no exponent or whitespace Text output Owned char *; free with fatoora_string_free Object output Owned opaque handle; free with its fatoora_<type>_free function Byte output FatooraBytes owner; its data view borrows from that owner Error Owned FatooraError; its message and details strings borrow from the error Output arguments Cleared on entry; free any old value before reusing its slot Enumerated input Typed C enum such as FatooraEnvironment, FatooraInvoiceTypeKind, FatooraVatCategory, FatooraAdjustmentKind or FatooraClearanceMode; a value that is not a declared enumerator returns FATOORA_INVALID_INPUT Enumerated output Typed pointer such as FatooraVatCategory *out Optional status output FatooraReportingStatus, FatooraClearanceStatus, FatooraValidationStatus or FatooraMessageType plus bool *has_value; *_UNKNOWN means present but not recognized by this version, and the _raw getter returns the exact text Invoice flags Integer bitmask of FATOORA_FLAG_* (FatooraInvoiceFlag) values

Invoice, party, address and response getters return independent owned snapshots. They survive destruction of the source object. Optional owned output is NULL when absent. Freeing a null owner is safe. Passing NULL for the error-output slot discards detailed diagnostics but retains the returned status.

The facade validates enum arguments. The raw Diplomat headers under generated/ use enumerators such as Environment_NonProduction and VatCategory_Standard and do not validate them: passing a value that is not a declared enumerator is undefined behaviour. Prefer the facade from C.

Do not copy opaque owners by value or free them with the system allocator. FATOORA_OK from local invoice validation means a report was produced; check fatoora_zatca_validation_report_is_valid on that report.

C++ headers provide their own C-linkage declarations. Include them directly; no external extern "C" wrapper is needed. They return diplomat::result and manage objects with std::unique_ptr. Inspect is_ok(), then move the result's .ok() or .err() value to take ownership. Owners release their native objects automatically.

#include "fatoora/BindingError.hpp"
#include "fatoora/Xml.hpp"
#include <iostream>
#include <utility>

int main() {
    auto result = fatoora::Xml::validate("<Invoice></Invoice>");
    if (!result.is_ok()) {
        auto error = std::move(result).err().value();
        std::cerr << error->code() << ": " << error->message() << '\n';
        return 1;
    }
    return std::move(result).ok().value() ? 0 : 1;
}

Enums are scoped wrappers such as fatoora::Environment::NonProduction and fatoora::VatCategory::Standard; optional response statuses return std::optional<fatoora::ReportingStatus> (and likewise for the other status enums), with the exact wire text available from the *_raw() accessor as a std::optional<std::string>. fatoora::InvoiceFlag(fatoora::InvoiceFlag::Export).bit() returns a flag's bit for the uint8_t mask.

Fallible C++ text accessors return a result containing std::string; error text accessors return std::string directly. Owned strings survive destruction of their source objects. Byte spans still borrow from their Bytes owner.

Compile and link

Use C++17 or later and headers matching the native library release:

c++ -std=c++17 validate.cpp -Ibindings/cpp \
  -L/path/to/native-library -lfatoora_ffi -o validate_cpp

Text inputs are borrowed for the call. Decimal inputs and outputs use exact strings. Optional text is a std::optional<std::string>, except ValidationResponse::cleared_invoice_xml() and SignedInvoice::zatca_key_signature(), which fail when the value is absent: check cleared_invoice_xml_present() or zatca_key_signature_present() first. Returned invoice, party, address and response objects are independent snapshots. Keep a Bytes owner alive while using its byte span.

docs.title: Consumption and safety
docs.text:
Builder input errors allow correction. build() consumes the builder's inner state even when final validation fails. Signing consumes a finalized invoice, and the consuming XML getter consumes a signed invoice. Subsequent operations on a consumed owner return an error; the owner remains safe to destroy.

Callers must provide valid pointers, preserve borrowed storage lifetimes, and synchronize mutable access, consumption, and destruction. Malformed bytes are validated only after the caller has supplied a valid byte view. Invalid pointers, double destruction, and concurrent conflicting access violate the native contract.

Fallible operations catch unwinding Rust panics and return Internal errors. Abort-mode panics and allocation aborts cannot be recovered this way. A panic can leave an operation consumed; discard the affected owner after an Internal failure. See errors for numeric codes and structured details.

docs.title: Reference by operation
docs.text:
• Configuration: environment selection.
  • CSR and keys: certificate requests and key export.
  • Invoice model: builder fields, amounts and returned snapshots.
  • Signing and XML: signing, parsing and hashes.
  • Validation: schema results and local reports.
  • API client: credentials, submissions and response acceptance.
  • Errors: numeric status categories and JSON diagnostics.

docs.title: C# package reference
docs.text: Use the Fatoority NuGet package to build, sign, and validate invoices and send ZATCA API requests from .NET 8 or later. Public classes use the Fatoora namespace. The package includes the native library for its supported platforms.

docs.title: Install from NuGet
docs.text:
In your application project, install the published package:

dotnet add package Fatoority

Use the Fatoora namespace. Check the supported native platforms below before deploying your application.

docs.title: Supported platforms
docs.text:
Runtime identifier Platform linux-x64 Linux x86-64, glibc 2.28 or later win-x64 Windows x86-64 osx-arm64 macOS Apple Silicon

Match your application's OS and architecture to a packaged runtime identifier. NuGet supplies the native asset at runtime; no library search-path override is needed. Linux musl/Alpine is not included. A package built locally inherits its build host's libc requirements.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Import Fatoora and dispose native objects when finished:

using Fatoora;

using var config = Config.Create(ZatcaEnvironment.NonProduction);
using var key = SigningKey.Generate();
using var bytes = key.ToDer();
byte[] privateKey = bytes.ToArray();

privateKey is an independent managed copy. Keep it secure; disposing the native objects does not erase that array. Follow the CSR guide for a complete credential-generation workflow.

Use ZatcaEnvironment.NonProduction, ZatcaEnvironment.Simulation, or ZatcaEnvironment.Production. The enum is named ZatcaEnvironment so it does not clash with System.Environment under implicit usings. Configuration, CSR generation, and credentials must agree on the environment. See the CSR, signing, validation, and QR guides for complete C# examples.

docs.title: Values and ownership
Errors
docs.text:
public static void ShowError()
    {
        try
        {
            using var key = SigningKey.FromPem("invalid key");
        }
        catch (InvalidInputException error)
        {
            // Every library error derives from FatooraException; Kind names its category.
            Console.WriteLine($"{error.Kind} ({error.Code}): {error.Message}");
            Console.WriteLine(error.DetailsJson);
        }
    }

Library failures throw a subclass of FatooraException. Each error kind has its own class; a code this version does not know throws plain FatooraException with a null Kind:

Code ErrorKind Exception 1 InvalidInput InvalidInputException 2 Validation ValidationException 3 Parse ParseException 4 Xml XmlException 5 Crypto CryptoException 6 Io IoException 7 Network NetworkException 8 Unauthorized UnauthorizedException 9 Internal InternalException 10 Api ApiException

Message contains the native message, Code the numeric code, Kind the category, and DetailsJson the structured details such as HTTP status and response body. The exception copies these values, so there is nothing to dispose. If you also import System.Xml or System.ComponentModel.DataAnnotations, qualify Fatoora.XmlException or Fatoora.ValidationException. Invalid UTF-16 fails before the native call with EncoderFallbackException; invalid native inputs, including embedded NUL, throw InvalidInputException.

docs.title: API requests
docs.text:
Create a client with ZatcaClient.Create(config), or with ZatcaClient.WithTimeout(config, timeout) to bound each request from connecting until the response body is read. timeout is a TimeSpan, rounded up to whole milliseconds; a request that exceeds it throws NetworkException. A zero, negative (including Timeout.InfiniteTimeSpan), or over-uint.MaxValue-millisecond timeout throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException.

using var client = ZatcaClient.WithTimeout(config, TimeSpan.FromSeconds(30));

Dispose the client, credentials, and responses with using. The following methods return owned objects:

Method Inputs Returns RequestComplianceCsid(csr, otp) Csr, OTP string ComplianceCsid RequestProductionCsid(credentials) ComplianceCsid ProductionCsid RenewCsid(credentials, csr, otp, acceptLanguage) ProductionCsid, Csr, OTP, nullable language string ProductionCsid CheckInvoiceCompliance(invoice, credentials) SignedInvoice, ComplianceCsid ValidationResponse ReportSimplifiedInvoice(invoice, credentials, clearanceMode, acceptLanguage) SignedInvoice, ProductionCsid, ClearanceMode, nullable language string ValidationResponse ClearStandardInvoice(invoice, credentials, clearanceMode, acceptLanguage) SignedInvoice, ProductionCsid, ClearanceMode, nullable language string ValidationResponse

All listed arguments are required, including nullable arguments: pass null when no language override is needed. clearanceMode sets the clearance-status request header; use ClearanceMode.Disabled for ordinary reporting and ClearanceMode.Enabled for clearance. It does not describe the result of the operation.

The native client methods block the calling thread. HTTP success alone does not establish invoice acceptance: inspect Outcome or call EnsureAccepted(). For clearance, ClearedInvoiceXml returns the cleared XML as string?. See the API guide for rejection, unknown outcomes, and cleared-document semantics.

docs.title: Prepared requests
docs.text:
Blocking method Prepared equivalent Credential scope / result RequestComplianceCsid PrepareRequestComplianceCsid CSR and OTP to compliance credentials RequestProductionCsid PrepareRequestProductionCsid Compliance to production credentials RenewCsid PrepareRenewCsid Production credentials, CSR and OTP to renewed credentials CheckInvoiceCompliance PrepareCheckInvoiceCompliance Compliance credentials; validation response ReportSimplifiedInvoice PrepareReportSimplifiedInvoice Production credentials; reporting response ClearStandardInvoice PrepareClearStandardInvoice Production credentials; clearance response

PrepareRequestComplianceCsid returns ComplianceRequest; credential exchange and renewal return ProductionRequest; invoice operations return InvoiceRequest. Their arguments match the corresponding blocking method.

For asynchronous HTTP or cancellation, use a Prepare* method and your own HttpClient. The request exposes the Method, Url, and HeadersJson (a JSON array of header pairs) properties and an owned Body(). Copy its bytes before awaiting the transport. Pass the HTTP status and response bytes to Decode(ushort, byte[]), including non-2xx responses, so the library can classify gateway errors. Decode returns an owned ComplianceCsid, ProductionCsid, or ValidationResponse matching the request type; dispose it after use. Configure the transport to refuse redirects, and pass your cancellation token to send/read operations. The generated blocking methods do not accept a cancellation token.

Prepared requests own their wire data, credentials, and decoding context; keep the request alive until decoding completes. Headers contain credentials and should not be logged.

docs.title: Local validation
Licensing
docs.text:
The native library includes SDK-derived rules and messages subject to the upstream terms in the bundled third-party notices. Those terms apply to the native component distributed with the C# package, as they do to other SDK distributions.

For source-build instructions, see the binding development documentation.

docs.title: JavaScript package reference
docs.text: Use fatoority in Node.js or a browser to build, sign, and validate invoices and send ZATCA API requests. The package includes WebAssembly and TypeScript declarations. For a complete task walkthrough, start with the guides.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
npm install fatoority

Import from the package root for asynchronous API requests and validation with an automatically supplied clock:

import { Config, Environment, SigningKey, Xml, ZatcaClient } from 'fatoority';

const config = Config.create(Environment.NonProduction);
const key = SigningKey.generate();
const privateKeyPem = key.toPem();

The private key is secret material; store it securely. Environment values are Environment.NonProduction, Environment.Simulation, and Environment.Production. Configuration, CSR generation, and credentials must agree.

Node.js 22+ and modern browsers are supported. Browser execution requires WebAssembly, Web Crypto, FinalizationRegistry, and top-level await. TypeScript users can use NodeNext or bundler module resolution; no separate @types package is needed.

docs.title: Values, ownership and errors
Local validation
API requests
docs.text:
Create new ZatcaClient(config) to use the global fetch, or new ZatcaClient(config, { fetch: customFetch }) to provide a compatible transport. All methods below return promises. Optional options accepts { signal }, where signal is an AbortSignal.

Method Inputs Promise result requestComplianceCsid(csr, otp, options?) Csr, OTP string ComplianceCsid requestProductionCsid(credentials, options?) ComplianceCsid ProductionCsid renewCsid(credentials, csr, otp, acceptLanguage?, options?) ProductionCsid, Csr, OTP, optional language string ProductionCsid checkInvoiceCompliance(invoice, credentials, options?) SignedInvoice, ComplianceCsid ValidationResponse reportSimplifiedInvoice(invoice, credentials, clearanceMode, acceptLanguage?, options?) SignedInvoice, ProductionCsid, ClearanceMode; language defaults to null ValidationResponse clearStandardInvoice(invoice, credentials, clearanceMode, acceptLanguage?, options?) SignedInvoice, ProductionCsid, ClearanceMode; language defaults to null ValidationResponse

clearanceMode sets the Clearance-Status request header; it is not the result of the operation. It is required and must be ClearanceMode.Enabled or ClearanceMode.Disabled, as in every other binding and in the prepared-request methods on fatoority/raw; any other value, including a boolean or the variant name, rejects with a TypeError. acceptLanguage controls the language request header. Pass optional positional arguments explicitly when supplying a later argument.

HTTP success alone does not establish invoice acceptance. Inspect outcome or call ensureAccepted() on a ValidationResponse. For clearance, clearedInvoiceXml is the cleared document as a string, or null; save it when present. See API requests and responses for credential requirements and response fields, and the API guide for a complete workflow.

docs.title: Prepared requests
docs.text:
For your own HTTP integration, import ZatcaClient from fatoority/raw, construct it with ZatcaClient.create(config), and call its prepare* methods. These return ComplianceRequest, ProductionRequest, or InvoiceRequest objects.

Request member Value method HTTP method string url Complete request URL string headersJson JSON array of header-name/value pairs body() Bytes; use toUint8Array() for a copied request body decode(status, bytes) bytes is a Uint8Array; returns credentials or ValidationResponse, depending on request type; may throw

Prepared requests retain their data and decoding context independently of the original invoice and credentials. Copy the outgoing body before awaiting HTTP. Pass every HTTP status and its response bytes to decode, including non-2xx responses. Disable redirects. Headers contain credentials and should not be logged.

Alternatively, sendPrepared(request, { fetch, signal }) from fatoority performs these steps and returns a promise for the decoded result. It copies the body before awaiting, refuses redirects, and forwards HTTP error responses to decoding.

docs.title: Browser deployment
docs.text:
The loader resolves fatoora_ffi.wasm relative to its package modules. Deploy the modules and WASM together, or configure your bundler to copy WASM to that URL. Serve the application over HTTP(S), with WebAssembly execution and Web Crypto available.

Direct ZATCA requests depend on gateway CORS. Use a server-side transport when needed and decide where credentials and private keys should reside. Local validation runs without Java, external SDK files, or network access.

docs.title: Licensing and source builds
docs.text: The package contains ZATCA-derived rules and messages with additional terms in third-party notices. TypeScript declarations ship with the package. For source-build instructions, see the binding development documentation.

docs.title: Kotlin and Java package reference
docs.text: Use com.fatoora classes to build, sign, and validate invoices and send ZATCA API requests on the JVM or Android. Value getters are Kotlin properties (Java getX()), amounts are exact BigDecimal values, and failures throw a FatooraException subclass for each error kind.

docs.title: Install from Maven Central
docs.text:
Use a published release from Maven Central. Java/Kotlin imports remain com.fatoora; the Maven group is com.fatoority.

For desktop Gradle projects, add this to build.gradle.kts:

repositories { mavenCentral() }
dependencies {
    implementation("com.fatoority:fatoority:0.7.0")
}

For Android, include mavenCentral() in the repositories under dependencyResolutionManagement in settings.gradle.kts, then add the Android artifact to your app's build.gradle.kts:

dependencies {
    implementation("com.fatoority:fatoority-android:0.7.0")
}

Choose the desktop JAR or Android AAR, not both. They bundle the native libraries for their supported platforms and resolve their runtime dependencies transitively. Consumers do not need Rust or a separate native-library build.

Artifact Runtime Bundled native platforms com.fatoority:fatoority:0.7.0 Java 8+ Linux x86-64, Windows x86-64, macOS arm64 com.fatoority:fatoority-android:0.7.0 Android API 26+ arm64-v8a, x86_64

Linux requires glibc 2.28+; musl/Alpine is not included. Desktop binaries cannot be used on Android; use the Android artifact for Android applications.

Windows x86-64 also requires the Microsoft Visual C++ v14 x64 runtime. The native DLL imports VCRUNTIME140.dll; it is not bundled in the JAR.

docs.title: Kotlin and Java
docs.text:
Select your language for resource handling and examples.

KotlinJava 
import com.fatoora.*

SigningKey.generate().use { key ->
    val privateKeyPem = key.toPem()
    // Store privateKeyPem securely.
}

Use use for native owners, including objects returned from methods. Getters that return copied values are properties, such as address.city (String) or address.district (String?).

import com.fatoora.*;

try (SigningKey key = SigningKey.generate()) {
    String privateKeyPem = key.toPem();
    // Store privateKeyPem securely.
}

Use try-with-resources for native owners, including returned objects. Kotlin properties appear as getters, such as address.getCity(); boolean properties keep their names, such as report.isValid() and report.hasErrors(). Optional text getters return a nullable String.

Use Environment.NonProduction, Environment.Simulation, or Environment.Production. Configuration, CSR and credentials must agree on the environment. Factory names use create, such as Config.create(Environment.NonProduction); other method names use camel case.

docs.title: Ownership and values
docs.text:
Value Public JVM value Native object AutoCloseable; close after use Value getter (text, amount, number, enum, boolean) Kotlin val property; Java getX(), isX() or hasX() Getter returning a native object Method, such as invoice.totals(); close the result Optional text input Nullable String; null differs from "" Optional text output Nullable String Quantity, price, rate or amount java.math.BigDecimal, converted exactly in both directions Unsigned byte / short / int Checked JVM integer / integer / long Enumerated code com.fatoora enum with the native variant names: Environment, InvoiceTypeKind, InvoiceSubType, VatCategory, AdjustmentKind, ClearanceMode, InvoiceOutcome Response status Nullable ReportingStatus, ClearanceStatus, ValidationStatus, or MessageType; null when absent, Unknown when present but not recognized by this version. The *Raw property holds the exact text as a nullable String Invoice flags Int bitmask taken by InvoiceBuilder.setFlags and held by InvoiceData.flags; combine InvoiceFlag bits from its bit property (ThirdParty, Nominal, Export, Summary, SelfBilled) Unsigned 64-bit counter BigInteger, range 0 through 2^64−1 Binary input / copied output JVM byte array; copies survive closing their owner Native failure FatooraException subclass with code, kind, message, detailsJson

Close objects returned by methods as well as those you construct. Native errors are copied to managed data and freed immediately; exceptions need no cleanup. Bytes.toByteArray() copies bytes under the owner lock, so the returned array survives closing its native owner. Strings reject lone UTF-16 surrogates and embedded NUL.

Calls acquire all participating owners in a fixed lock order. Concurrent calls on the same object serialize; close() waits for active calls and is idempotent. Later calls throw IllegalStateException. Operations on independent owners can run concurrently. Consumed builders/invoices remain closeable but reject further use with a native error. Automatic cleanup is nondeterministic; explicitly close owners. Freeing native memory does not guarantee secret erasure.

Import public classes from com.fatoora. 0.7 removed the getter functions, String amount overloads, renamed aliases and Boolean coroutine overloads deprecated in 0.6; see the 0.7 migration guide.

docs.title: Amounts
docs.text:
Quantities, prices, rates and amounts are java.math.BigDecimal in both directions. The binding sends toPlainString() and parses results with BigDecimal(String), so no digits are lost and exponents never reach the native layer. Returned values are normalized, so 10.50 reads back as 10.5; compare with compareTo.

KotlinJava 
    fun lineTotals(): Pair<BigDecimal, BigDecimal> =
        InvoiceLineItem.create("Item", BigDecimal("2"), "PCE", BigDecimal("10.50"), BigDecimal("15"), VatCategory.Standard)
            .use { item -> item.totalAmount to item.vatAmount } // 21 and 3.15

    public static BigDecimal lineTotal() {
        try (InvoiceLineItem item = InvoiceLineItem.create("Item", new BigDecimal("2"), "PCE",
                 new BigDecimal("10.50"), new BigDecimal("15"), VatCategory.Standard)) {
            return item.getTotalAmount(); // getVatAmount() returns 3.15
        }
    }

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
Native failures throw a subclass of FatooraException chosen by error code:

Code ErrorKind Exception 1 InvalidInput InvalidInputException 2 Validation ValidationException 3 Parse ParseException 4 Xml XmlException 5 Crypto CryptoException 6 Io IoException 7 Network NetworkException 8 Unauthorized UnauthorizedException 9 Internal InternalException 10 Api ApiException

A code this version does not know throws plain FatooraException with a null kind. The code, kind, message, and JSON details are managed values; exceptions need no cleanup. Invalid UTF-16 and embedded NUL are rejected. Use structured error details to distinguish validation, input, cryptography, and gateway failures.

KotlinJava 
try {
    Address.create("XX", "Riyadh", "King Fahd Road", "1234", "12345").use { }
} catch (error: InvalidInputException) {
    println("Rejected input: ${error.message}")
} catch (error: FatooraException) {
    println("${error.kind} (${error.code}): ${error.message}")
    println(error.detailsJson)
}

try (Address address = Address.create("XX", "Riyadh", "King Fahd Road", "1234", "12345", null, null, null)) {
    // An unrecognized country code throws before this block.
} catch (InvalidInputException error) {
    System.err.println("Rejected input: " + error.getMessage());
} catch (FatooraException error) {
    System.err.println(error.getKind() + " (" + error.getCode() + "): " + error.getMessage());
    System.err.println(error.getDetailsJson());
}

docs.title: Local validation
docs.text:
Method Inputs Returns Xml.validate(xml) XML string true on schema success; throws for malformed XML or schema rejection Xml.validateZatca(xml, optionsJson) XML string, nullable options JSON Owned ZatcaValidationReport, including rejection or incomplete coverage Xml.hash(xml) XML string Base64 invoice hash string

Pass null for default options, or a JSON object string with previous_invoice_hash and/or evaluated_at. The timestamp uses RFC3339 format; omission uses one native UTC clock snapshot. Unknown option fields are rejected. Inspect the isValid and isComplete properties and stage(i) on the returned report (Java: isValid(), isComplete()), or read toJson(). Missing predecessor context makes coverage incomplete. Execution failures throw and may carry a partial report in their JSON details. See the validation reference.

Schemas are bundled; validation needs no external SDK or network. Local validation does not establish gateway acceptance or certificate issuer trust.

docs.title: API requests
docs.text:
Create a client with ZatcaClient.create(config), or with ZatcaClient.withTimeout(config, timeout) to bound each request from connecting until the response body is read. timeout is a java.time.Duration, or in Kotlin also a kotlin.time.Duration; it is rounded up to whole milliseconds, and a request that exceeds it throws NetworkException. A zero, negative, or longer-than-4294967.295-second timeout throws IllegalArgumentException.

KotlinJava 
import kotlin.time.Duration.Companion.seconds

val client = ZatcaClient.withTimeout(config, 30.seconds)

import java.time.Duration;

ZatcaClient client = ZatcaClient.withTimeout(config, Duration.ofSeconds(30));

Native HTTP methods block the calling thread and return objects that must be closed:

Method Inputs Returns requestComplianceCsid(csr, otp) Csr, OTP string ComplianceCsid requestProductionCsid(credentials) ComplianceCsid ProductionCsid renewCsid(credentials, csr, otp, acceptLanguage) ProductionCsid, Csr, OTP, nullable language ProductionCsid checkInvoiceCompliance(invoice, credentials) SignedInvoice, ComplianceCsid ValidationResponse reportSimplifiedInvoice(invoice, credentials, clearanceMode, acceptLanguage) SignedInvoice, ProductionCsid, ClearanceMode, nullable language ValidationResponse clearStandardInvoice(invoice, credentials, clearanceMode, acceptLanguage) SignedInvoice, ProductionCsid, ClearanceMode, nullable language ValidationResponse

The final acceptLanguage argument can be omitted; its default is null.

clearanceMode controls the request header; use ClearanceMode.Disabled for ordinary reporting and ClearanceMode.Enabled for clearance. The coroutine *Async helpers take the same ClearanceMode. acceptLanguage controls the language header; pass null for no override. It does not describe the response outcome.

A returned response is not necessarily accepted. Check the outcome property or call ensureAccepted(). clearedInvoiceXml is a nullable String; save the cleared XML when present. See the API reference.

KotlinJava

Coroutine extensions requestComplianceCsidAsync, requestProductionCsidAsync, renewCsidAsync, checkInvoiceComplianceAsync, reportSimplifiedInvoiceAsync, and clearStandardInvoiceAsync dispatch blocking calls to Dispatchers.IO.

// Inside a suspend function, with live client, invoice, and credentials.
client.reportSimplifiedInvoiceAsync(invoice, credentials, ClearanceMode.Disabled).use { response ->
    response.ensureAccepted()
}

Keep input owners open until completion. Cancellation cannot interrupt an in-flight native call. If cancellation discards a completed result, the coroutine wrapper closes it. Use a prepared request with a cancellable HTTP transport when you need to interrupt network work.

Blocking methods can run on your application's executor. Cancelling a task does not interrupt an in-flight native HTTP call. Keep its input owners open until completion. Use prepared requests with a cancellable HTTP transport when you need to interrupt network work.

docs.title: Prepared requests
docs.text: prepareReportSimplifiedInvoice, for example, returns an owned InvoiceRequest: read its url, method and headersJson properties and body(), send exactly those values, then call decode(status, responseBytes) and ensureAccepted() on the returned response. HTTP status is a checked integer; the response body is a byte array. Pass non-2xx responses through decoding too, and disable redirects. Close the prepared request, its body owner, and decoded response after use. Prepared requests own their bytes and decoding context independently of the original credentials/invoice. Headers contain credentials: do not log them.

docs.title: Android
docs.text:
Use the Android artifact alone. It supplies JNA's Android dependency and shrinker rules and declares the Internet permission. It supports 64-bit ABIs with 16 KiB ELF alignment. Run network, signing, and validation work off the UI thread.

Android native TLS uses bundled Mozilla/WebPKI roots. Android user-installed CAs and app network-security configuration do not modify that trust store. Prepared requests let apps use their own HTTP client and certificate policy.

docs.title: License
docs.text: Original SDK code is MIT OR Apache-2.0. Native packages contain ZATCA-derived rule predicates and messages under their own terms and include THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md and licenses/zatca/. See the third-party notices.

docs.title: Python package reference
docs.text: The published wheels support CPython 3.10–3.13. Use CPython 3.13 for the complete sandbox walkthrough. Install fatoority and import fatoora; this page describes Python-specific values and behavior.

docs.title: Install and import
docs.text:
python -m pip install fatoority

The asynchronous client needs the async extra, which adds httpx: python -m pip install "fatoority[async]".

from fatoora import Config, Environment, SigningKey

with Config(Environment.NON_PRODUCTION) as config:
    with SigningKey.generate() as key:
        private_key_pem = key.to_pem()

Keep the private key secure. Exported strings and bytes remain in Python memory after the native owner closes.

The default Config() environment is Environment.NON_PRODUCTION. Choose Environment.SIMULATION or Environment.PRODUCTION explicitly when needed. Configuration, CSR generation, and credentials must agree on the environment.

docs.title: Values and return types
docs.text:
Value Python representation Text str; embedded NUL is rejected Optional text str or None; "" remains a present empty string Decimal input decimal.Decimal, decimal str, or int; float and bool are rejected Decimal output decimal.Decimal Binary input/output bytes Invoice counter int in the unsigned 64-bit range Timestamp input timezone-aware datetime.datetime (converted to UTC) or "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ"; a naive datetime raises ValueError Timestamp output timezone-aware datetime.datetime in UTC (issue_datetime, signing_time, evaluated_at) Date input / output datetime.date or "YYYY-MM-DD" / datetime.date UUID input / output uuid.UUID or str / str (core keeps the UUID text verbatim) Local ZATCA report frozen ZatcaReport dataclass ZATCA response status str enum (ReportingStatus, ClearanceStatus, ValidationStatus, MessageType) or None Invoice data (parties, addresses, notes, references, payment means, adjustments, line items, totals) frozen dataclasses: Party, Address, Identifier, InvoiceNote, OriginalInvoiceRef, PaymentMeans, Adjustment, InvoiceLineItem, InvoiceTotals, VatBreakdown, TaxExemption

Use exact decimal text such as "0.3333", rather than constructing a Decimal from a binary float. See decimal numbers and rounding.

Public choices use IntEnum members. Prefer their names to raw integers:

Enum Members Environment NON_PRODUCTION, SIMULATION, PRODUCTION InvoiceTypeKind TAX, PREPAYMENT, CREDIT_NOTE, DEBIT_NOTE InvoiceSubType STANDARD, SIMPLIFIED VatCategory EXEMPT, STANDARD, ZERO, OUT_OF_SCOPE InvoiceFlag THIRD_PARTY, NOMINAL, EXPORT, SUMMARY, SELF_BILLED InvoiceOutcome UNKNOWN, ACCEPTED, REJECTED ClearanceMode DISABLED, ENABLED

Statuses read from a ZATCA response are str enums whose values are the wire text, so response.reporting_status == "REPORTED", str(), f-strings and json.dumps give the text ZATCA sent:

Enum Members ReportingStatus REPORTED, NOT_REPORTED ClearanceStatus CLEARED, NOT_CLEARED ValidationStatus PASS, WARNING, ERROR MessageType INFO, WARNING, ERROR

A status this version does not recognize is kept verbatim, as the core's Other(String) variant keeps it: it is still an instance of the enum, its name is "OTHER" and its value is the text ZATCA sent. Test status.name == "OTHER" to detect one.

Country/currency values are strings; their constructors validate and normalize supported values. See the invoice model.

docs.title: Properties, constructors and chaining
docs.text:
Values you read are properties: invoice.id, invoice.seller.address.city, response.reporting_status, config.env. They are read-only; optional values are None when absent. Operations that compute, convert or consume stay methods: hash(), to_xml_base64(), line_item(index), is_simplified(), ensure_accepted(), build(), sign(signer).

InvoiceBuilder(invoice_type, invoice_subtype, *, id=..., uuid=..., ...) takes the header fields as keyword arguments, and every setter returns the builder, so a whole invoice is one expression:

from datetime import datetime, timezone
from uuid import uuid4
from fatoora import (Address, InvoiceBuilder, InvoiceSubType, InvoiceTypeKind, Party,
                     PaymentMeans, VatCategory)

seller = Party("Acme", Address("SA", "Riyadh", "King Fahd", "1234", "12222"),
               vat_id="399999999900003")
invoice = (
    InvoiceBuilder(InvoiceTypeKind.TAX, InvoiceSubType.SIMPLIFIED,
                   id="INV-1", uuid=uuid4(), issue_datetime=datetime.now(timezone.utc),
                   currency="SAR", previous_invoice_hash=previous_hash,
                   invoice_counter=1, vat_category=VatCategory.STANDARD, seller=seller)
    .add_payment_means(PaymentMeans("10"))
    .add_line_item("Item", 1, "PCE", "100", "15", VatCategory.STANDARD)
    .build()
)

Every type you create directly has a constructor: Config(env), ZatcaClient(config), CsrProperties(*, ...), ComplianceCsid(env, *, token, secret, request_id=None), ProductionCsid(...), InvoiceBuilder(...), LineItemBuilder() and the invoice dataclasses. Types you obtain from data or from another call use named factories (InvoiceSigner.from_pem, SigningKey.generate, Csr.from_der, SignedInvoice.from_xml, ...); calling such a class raises TypeError naming them.

Arguments after the first are keyword-only for set_seller, set_buyer, add_note(text, *, language=None), CsrProperties(*, ...), the credentials after env, and the clearance/accept_language arguments of the report and clear methods. set_seller and set_buyer take a Party, or a name with either address=Address(...) or the address fields, not both. Parse invoices with FinalizedInvoice.from_xml(xml) / from_file(path) and SignedInvoice.from_xml(xml) / from_file(path).

docs.title: Object lifetime
docs.text:
Native owners support with and close(). Close objects returned by methods and properties as well as ones you construct. Closing is idempotent; later calls on, or property reads from, a closed owner raise InvalidInputError. Calls involving the same owners are synchronized. Independent owners can be used independently.

InvoiceBuilder.build() consumes the builder's inner state even when final validation fails. FinalizedInvoice.sign(signer) consumes the finalized invoice The wrapper remains safe to close, but further use of consumed state fails. Create a new input object to retry after a consuming operation fails.

Plain strings, bytes, decimal values, and the dataclass models do not need close(). Returned owners (such as a ValidationResponse and its validation_results) are independent of their parent, but still need their own cleanup.

docs.title: Invoice data models
docs.text:
Everything read from an invoice is a frozen dataclass. Values compare with ==, copy with dataclasses.replace, and go straight back into a builder, so an invoice read from XML can be rebuilt from its parts. An invoice reads its data from the native object once, on first access, and caches it.

Model Constructor and notes Party Party(name, address=None, vat_id=None, identifiers=()). vat_id and each identifier take an Identifier or a string. other_id is the first identifier. Identifier Identifier(value, scheme=None): replaces the VatId/OtherId handles and the (value, scheme) tuples of line item identifiers. Address Address(country_code, city, street, building_number, postal_code, additional_street=None, additional_number=None, district=None, province=None). Validated on construction; "SA" reads back as "SAU". InvoiceNote InvoiceNote(text, language_id=None); language defaults to "en". OriginalInvoiceRef OriginalInvoiceRef(id, uuid=None, issue_date=None, issue_time=None, document_type_code=None): billing references, the referenced original invoice, and line document references. PaymentMeans PaymentMeans(code, instruction_notes=(), account_identifier=None, payment_terms=None). Adjustment Adjustment(amount, reason=None, reason_code=None, ...) or Adjustment.percent_of(base, percent, ...): line and document allowances and charges. Document entries read back with charge, category, rate, exemption, tax_category_count and omitted_rate, and round-trip through builder.add_adjustment(entry). InvoiceLineItem As input to add_item, total_amount and vat_amount are optional: they are calculated when None and checked when given. 
from fatoora import Adjustment, FinalizedInvoice, InvoiceBuilder, InvoiceLineItem, VatCategory

parsed = FinalizedInvoice.from_file("invoice.xml")
print(parsed.seller.name, parsed.seller.vat_id.value, parsed.seller.address.city)

line = InvoiceLineItem("Notebook", "PCE", quantity=2, unit_price="50", vat_rate=15,
                       vat_category=VatCategory.STANDARD,
                       adjustments=(Adjustment(10, reason="Volume discount"),))
builder = InvoiceBuilder(parsed.invoice_type_kind, parsed.invoice_sub_type,
                         seller=parsed.seller, buyer=parsed.buyer)
builder.add_item(line)
builder.add_charge(Adjustment.percent_of(90, 5, reason="Delivery"), VatCategory.STANDARD, 15)

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
Library failures raise a subclass of FatooraError, one per ErrorKind. Use str(error) or .message for the message, .code for its numeric classification, .kind for the ErrorKind, and .details for structured data as a dict.

from fatoora import FatooraError, SigningKey

try:
    SigningKey.from_pem("invalid key")
except FatooraError as error:
    print(error.kind, error.code, error.message)
    print(error.details)
Code ErrorKind Exception 1 INVALID_INPUT InvalidInputError (also a ValueError) 2 VALIDATION ValidationError 3 PARSE ParseError 4 XML XmlError 5 CRYPTO CryptoError 6 IO IoError (also an OSError) 7 NETWORK NetworkError 8 UNAUTHORIZED UnauthorizedError 9 INTERNAL InternalError 10 API ApiError

ErrorKind is an IntEnum, so error.kind == error.code for a known code. Unknown native codes raise plain FatooraError with .kind set to None; .code and .details remain available. Python argument checks can raise TypeError or ValueError before a native call. Do not parse message text to identify an error; use error codes and structured details.

docs.title: Local validation
docs.text:
Function Inputs Returns validate_xml(xml) XML str True on schema success; raises on malformed XML or schema rejection validate_zatca(xml, *, previous_invoice_hash=None, evaluated_at=None) XML str, optional keyword-only context ZatcaReport, including rejection or incomplete coverage hash_xml(xml) XML str Base64 invoice hash str 
from pathlib import Path
from fatoora import Severity, validate_zatca

xml = Path("invoice.xml").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
report = validate_zatca(xml)
print(report.is_valid, report.is_complete)
for finding in report.findings:
    if finding.severity is Severity.ERROR:
        print(finding.code, finding.message, finding.location)

previous_invoice_hash supplies trusted invoice-history context. evaluated_at accepts a timezone-aware datetime or RFC 3339 text; omission uses one UTC clock snapshot. Missing predecessor context makes coverage incomplete. A returned report does not mean the invoice passed: inspect is_valid and the stage findings.

ZatcaReport is a frozen dataclass with is_valid, is_complete, has_errors, stages, evaluated_at (datetime), profile and schema_version, plus findings, errors and warnings (all stages, in order), stage(ZatcaStage.KSA), to_json() and to_dict(). Each ZatcaStageReport has stage, status, findings, evaluated_assertions and provenance (ZatcaRuleSource with stylesheet and sha256, or None). Each ZatcaFinding has severity, layer, code, message, location (ValidationLocation with kind, path, line, column, or None) and assertion_site. ZatcaStage, ZatcaStageStatus, Severity, ValidationLayer and ValidationLocationKind are string enums whose values are the JSON names, so finding.severity == "error" also holds.

Execution failures raise an exception and may include a partial report, as a dictionary, at error.details["report"]. Argument failures can have no report. All schemas are bundled; validation needs no network or external SDK. It does not establish remote acceptance or certificate issuer trust. See the validation reference.

docs.title: ZATCA API methods
docs.text:
Create ZatcaClient(config, *, timeout=None) with a live Config. Client methods block the calling thread and return owned objects.

timeout bounds each request, from connecting until the response body is read. Pass seconds as an int/float or a datetime.timedelta; it is rounded up to whole milliseconds and must be positive and at most about 49.7 days (otherwise ValueError; a non-numeric value raises TypeError). A request that exceeds it raises NetworkError. The default None applies no client-side timeout.

from datetime import timedelta
from fatoora import Config, Environment, ZatcaClient

client = ZatcaClient(Config(Environment.SIMULATION), timeout=30)
client = ZatcaClient(Config(Environment.SIMULATION), timeout=timedelta(seconds=30))
Method Inputs Returns request_compliance_csid(csr, otp) Csr, OTP str ComplianceCsid request_production_csid(ccsid) ComplianceCsid ProductionCsid renew_csid(pcsid, csr, otp, accept_language=None) ProductionCsid, Csr, OTP, optional language ProductionCsid check_invoice_compliance(invoice, ccsid) SignedInvoice, ComplianceCsid ValidationResponse report_simplified_invoice(invoice, pcsid, *, clearance, accept_language=None) SignedInvoice, ProductionCsid, keyword-only ClearanceMode and optional language ValidationResponse clear_standard_invoice(invoice, pcsid, *, clearance, accept_language=None) SignedInvoice, ProductionCsid, keyword-only ClearanceMode and optional language ValidationResponse

clearance is a required ClearanceMode controlling the Clearance-Status request header: ClearanceMode.DISABLED sends 0, ClearanceMode.ENABLED sends 1. It does not describe the result. accept_language is a string or None controlling the language header. These methods block; use timeout to bound how long a call can block, or the asynchronous client in asyncio code.

A successful HTTP request does not guarantee acceptance. Read outcome for the InvoiceOutcome, or call ensure_accepted() to raise for rejected/unknown outcomes. cleared_invoice_xml is str | None; save that XML for an accepted clearance when present. reporting_status is an optional ReportingStatus and clearance_status an optional ClearanceStatus. See API request and response contracts and the API guide.

docs.title: Asynchronous client
docs.text:
AsyncZatcaClient(config, *, timeout=None, http_client=None) has the methods above as coroutines, with the same arguments, return types and errors. The native library prepares each request and decodes each response, as for ZatcaClient; httpx sends it. Install the async extra for httpx (pip install "fatoority[async]"). Importing fatoora does not need httpx; creating an AsyncZatcaClient without it raises ImportError naming the extra.

import asyncio
from fatoora import AsyncZatcaClient, ClearanceMode, Config, Environment

async def report(invoice, pcsid):
    async with AsyncZatcaClient(Config(Environment.SIMULATION), timeout=30) as client:
        response = await client.report_simplified_invoice(invoice, pcsid, clearance=ClearanceMode.DISABLED)
    response.ensure_accepted()
    return response
  • timeout takes the same values as for ZatcaClient and bounds each request, from sending it until the response body is read. A request that exceeds it raises NetworkError. You can also cancel a call, for example with asyncio.wait_for.
  • Without http_client, the client creates an httpx.AsyncClient with no httpx timeouts and closes it in aclose() or at the end of async with. Pass your own httpx.AsyncClient to share its connection pool, proxy or TLS settings; its own timeouts then also apply (a timeout raises NetworkError), and closing the AsyncZatcaClient leaves it open.
  • Redirects are never followed, even when the httpx.AsyncClient enables them.
  • A transport failure, before the response arrives, raises NetworkError (details type network, with the httpx exception as __cause__). A response body that cannot be read raises NetworkError (details type api_response_read) for invoice operations. Every HTTP status reaches the decoder, so status errors are the same as ZatcaClient's.
  • FATOORA_ZATCA_BASE_URL overrides the gateway URL as it does for ZatcaClient.
  • Calls do not hold their arguments while waiting for the response. After aclose(), calls raise InvalidInputError.

docs.title: Signed invoice metadata
docs.text:
Property or method Value signature Encoded signature str public_key Encoded public key str cert_hash Encoded certificate hash str signed_props_hash Encoded signed-properties hash str signing_time Timezone-aware (UTC) datetime invoice_hash The invoice hash stored in the signature, str hash() The invoice hash recomputed from the XML, str

Parsing a signed invoice checks local signature, digest and QR integrity. Run explicit validation for schema and business-rule checks; issuer trust and clearance require separate evidence. See the signing reference for key/certificate formats and signing operations.

docs.title: Migrate from earlier versions
docs.text:
The migration guides walk through each upgrade with before-and-after code: 0.5 to 0.6 and 0.6 to 0.7. 0.7 removed every name that 0.6 deprecated; the 0.7 guide lists each one with its replacement.

The 0.6 changes that were hard breaks, with no deprecation period, are below. Getters became read-only properties: drop the parentheses (invoice.id() becomes invoice.id); calling a property fails like calling its value (TypeError: 'str' object is not callable). Rows marked "enforced" were warnings in 0.5.1 and became TypeErrors in 0.6.

0.5 0.6 and later Getter methods: invoice.id(), address.city(), response.reporting_status(), invoice.xml(), ... Properties: invoice.id, address.city, response.reporting_status, invoice.xml invoice.issue_datetime(), signed.signing_time() return str invoice.issue_datetime, signed.signing_time are aware datetimes issue_date(), actual_delivery_date(), latest_delivery_date(), OriginalInvoiceRef.issue_date() return str Properties of type datetime.date Setters return None Setters return the builder set_seller(name, country_code, ...) positional (enforced) set_seller(Party(...)), or set_seller(name, *, vat_id=..., address=Address(...)) or the address keywords set_buyer(name, country_code, ...) positional (enforced) set_buyer(name, *, address=..., ...) add_note(text, language) positional (enforced) add_note(text, language=...) CsrProperties.new(...) positional (enforced) CsrProperties(*, ...) report_simplified_invoice(invoice, pcsid, False) positional flags (enforced) report_simplified_invoice(invoice, pcsid, clearance=ClearanceMode.DISABLED) Line document_references hold DocumentReference values with a str issue_date OriginalInvoiceRef values whose issue_date is a date party.identifiers, payment_means.instruction_notes return lists Tuples reporting_status, clearance_status, results.status, message.message_type, message.status return str str enums ReportingStatus, ClearanceStatus, ValidationStatus, MessageType; comparisons with strings still hold, type(x) is str does not
